<file path="__test/regressions/insights-harness-path-resolution.test.ts">
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events'
import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from 'vitest'

/**
 * Regression: BSI-58 — the canary (Finder/Dock-launched) reported Claude Code
 * and Codex as unavailable and insights silently fell back to the fixture, while
 * a terminal-launched build worked. Root cause: the harness probed/ran the CLIs
 * through a non-interactive login shell (`zsh -lc`), which never sources
 * ~/.zshrc — where tool-manager PATH entries (bun, n, …) live. A GUI launch gets
 * a minimal launchd PATH, so the bare-name lookup missed the CLIs.
 *
 * The fix resolves each CLI to an absolute path against a PATH discovered ONCE
 * from the user's *interactive* login shell (`-ilc`), then runs it through the
 * original *non-interactive* `-lc` shell with that PATH injected. The interactive
 * shell is confined to the no-input PATH probe, so the untrusted-transcript
 * analysis run never sources ~/.zshrc. These tests pin that topology: an
 * interactive probe, a non-interactive run, absolute-path invocation, and a clean
 * failure when the CLI is genuinely missing. `spawn` is mocked so no real shell
 * runs under CI.
 */

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({ spawn: vi.fn() }))

vi.mock('node:child_process', () => ({ spawn: mocks.spawn }))

/** Minimal stand-in for a spawned child: emits a clean exit on the next tick. */
class FakeChild extends EventEmitter {
  exitCode: number | null = 0
  kill(): boolean {
    return true
  }
}

const ENV_KEYS = ['BLUME_REALCLI_BIN', 'BLUME_MYCLI_BIN'] as const

async function loadRunProcess(): Promise<
  typeof import('../../src/main/insights/nodeHarnessProcess')
> {
  // Fresh module each test so the process-lifetime PATH cache is reset.
  return import('../../src/main/insights/nodeHarnessProcess')
}

/** argv[0] of each mocked spawn call (the shell mode flag, e.g. -lc / -ilc). */
function shellModes(): string[] {
  return mocks.spawn.mock.calls.map((call) => call[1][0])
}

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.resetModules()
  mocks.spawn.mockReset()
  mocks.spawn.mockImplementation(() => {
    const child = new FakeChild()
    // Resolve waitForChild after its listeners attach. The fake writes no output
    // file, so captures/PATH probe read back empty — fine; these tests assert on
    // spawn arguments and the resolve/not-found contract, not parsed output.
    setImmediate(() => child.emit('close', 0, null))
    return child
  })
  for (const key of ENV_KEYS) delete process.env[key]
})

afterEach(() => {
  for (const key of ENV_KEYS) delete process.env[key]
})

describe('insights harness CLI resolution (BSI-58)', () => {
  test('resolveCommand resolves via an env override and rejects an unknown bin', async () => {
    const { resolveCommand, commandExists } = await loadRunProcess()
    process.env.BLUME_REALCLI_BIN = process.execPath // a real, absolute executable

    expect(await resolveCommand('realcli')).toBe(process.execPath)
    expect(await commandExists('realcli')).toBe(true)
    expect(await commandExists('totally-missing-cli-xyz')).toBe(false)
  })

  test('the PATH probe is interactive (-ilc); the analysis run is not (-lc)', async () => {
    const { runCliJson } = await loadRunProcess()
    process.env.BLUME_MYCLI_BIN = process.execPath

    await runCliJson({
      bin: 'mycli',
      args: ['--print'],
      prompt: 'hi',
      cwd: tmpdir(),
      timeoutMs: 1000
    })

    const modes = shellModes()
    expect(modes).toContain('-ilc') // one-time PATH probe sources ~/.zshrc
    expect(modes).toContain('-lc') // the actual run stays non-interactive
    // The untrusted-transcript run must never use an interactive shell.
    expect(modes).not.toContain('-lic')
    expect(modes).not.toContain('-i')
  })

  test('the run invokes the resolved absolute path, never the bare name', async () => {
    const { runCliJson } = await loadRunProcess()
    process.env.BLUME_MYCLI_BIN = process.execPath

    await runCliJson({
      bin: 'mycli',
      args: ['--print'],
      prompt: 'hi',
      cwd: tmpdir(),
      timeoutMs: 1000
    })

    const runCall = mocks.spawn.mock.calls.find((call) => call[1][0] === '-lc')
    expect(runCall).toBeTruthy()
    const commandLine = runCall?.[1][1] ?? ''
    expect(commandLine).toContain(process.execPath)
    expect(commandLine).toContain('--print')
  })

  test('an unresolvable CLI fails cleanly instead of running the bare name', async () => {
    const { runCliJson } = await loadRunProcess()

    const res = await runCliJson({
      bin: 'ghost-cli-xyz',
      args: [],
      prompt: 'hi',
      cwd: tmpdir(),
      timeoutMs: 1000
    })

    expect(res.json).toBeNull()
    expect(res.parseError).toMatch(/command not found/i)
    expect(res.exitCode).toBeNull()
    // No analysis run should have been spawned for an unresolved CLI.
    const ranAnalysis = mocks.spawn.mock.calls.some((call) => {
      return call[1][0] === '-lc' && String(call[1][1]).includes('ghost-cli-xyz')
    })
    expect(ranAnalysis).toBe(false)
  })

  test('Windows candidate names probe .exe/.cmd/.bat for a bare bin name', async () => {
    const { executableCandidateNames } = await loadRunProcess()
    expect(executableCandidateNames('claude', true)).toEqual([
      'claude.exe',
      'claude.cmd',
      'claude.bat'
    ])
    // A name that already carries an extension is used as-is.
    expect(executableCandidateNames('claude.exe', true)).toEqual(['claude.exe'])
    // POSIX keeps the bare name only.
    expect(executableCandidateNames('claude', false)).toEqual(['claude'])
  })

  test('Windows spawn plan: direct for .exe, cmd.exe /d /s /c for .cmd shims', async () => {
    const { win32SpawnPlan } = await loadRunProcess()

    expect(win32SpawnPlan('C:\\Users\\p\\.local\\bin\\claude.exe', ['--print'])).toEqual({
      file: 'C:\\Users\\p\\.local\\bin\\claude.exe',
      args: ['--print'],
      windowsVerbatimArguments: false
    })

    const shim = win32SpawnPlan('C:\\Users\\p q\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\claude.cmd', ['--print'])
    expect(shim.file).toBe(process.env.ComSpec ?? 'cmd.exe')
    expect(shim.windowsVerbatimArguments).toBe(true)
    // Spacey path is CRT-quoted, bare flags stay bare, outer quotes pair with /s.
    expect(shim.args).toEqual([
      '/d',
      '/v:off',
      '/s',
      '/c',
      '""C:\\Users\\p q\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\claude.cmd" --print"'
    ])

    // Embedded quotes (inline JSON config) survive via CRT escaping.
    const json = win32SpawnPlan('C:\\x\\claude.cmd', ['--mcp-config', '{"a":"b c"}'])
    expect(json.args[4]).toBe('""C:\\x\\claude.cmd" --mcp-config "{\\"a\\":\\"b c\\"}""')

    // cmd.exe metacharacters are refused rather than escaped — argv is
    // app-controlled (the untrusted prompt travels over stdin), so a hit is an
    // upstream bug, not a quoting need.
    expect(() => win32SpawnPlan('C:\\x\\claude.cmd', ['--flag=a&b'])).toThrow(/unsupported/)
  })

  test('captures through non-interactive zsh with temp-file stdio', async () => {
    const { runCliCapture } = await loadRunProcess()
    const spawnCalls: Array<any[]> = []
    const nowValues = [100, 145]
    const nowMs = () => nowValues.shift() ?? 145
    const fakeSpawn = ((...args: any[]) => {
      spawnCalls.push(args)
      const child = new FakeChild()
      setImmediate(async () => {
        const commandLine = String(args[1][1])
        const match = / < '([^']+)' > '([^']+)' 2> '([^']+)'$/.exec(commandLine)
        expect(match).toBeTruthy()
        const [, promptPath, stdoutPath, stderrPath] = match ?? []
        expect(await readFile(promptPath, 'utf8')).toBe('prompt text')
        await writeFile(stdoutPath, '{"ok":true}', 'utf8')
        await writeFile(stderrPath, 'diagnostic', 'utf8')
        child.emit('close', 0, null)
      })
      return child
    }) as any

    const capture = await runCliCapture({
      commandBase: "'/opt/bin/claude' '--print'",
      prompt: 'prompt text',
      cwd: tmpdir(),
      timeoutMs: 1000,
      env: { PATH: '/usr/bin' },
      spawnImpl: fakeSpawn,
      nowMs
    })

    expect(spawnCalls).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(spawnCalls[0][0]).toBe('/bin/zsh')
    expect(spawnCalls[0][1].slice(0, 1)).toEqual(['-lc'])
    expect(spawnCalls[0][2]?.stdio).toBe('ignore')
    expect(spawnCalls[0][2]?.env?.PATH).toBe('/usr/bin')
    expect(String(spawnCalls[0][1][1])).toMatch(/^'\/opt\/bin\/claude' '--print' < /)
    expect(capture).toEqual({
      stdout: '{"ok":true}',
      stderr: 'diagnostic',
      exitCode: 0,
      signal: null,
      timedOut: false,
      durationMs: 45
    })
  })
})
</file>

<file path="__test/regressions/insights-session-gate.test.ts">
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest'

import { sessionWindowQuietScore, sessionWindowReady } from '@blume/app-core'

describe('insights session gate', () => {
  test('smart timing opens only near reset with enough unused quota', () => {
    const now = 1_000

    expect(
      sessionWindowReady(
        { id: 'session', label: 'Session', usedPercent: 50, resetsAt: now + 10 * 60_000 },
        now
      )
    ).toBe(true)

    expect(
      sessionWindowReady(
        { id: 'session', label: 'Session', usedPercent: 50, resetsAt: now + 30 * 60_000 },
        now
      )
    ).toBe(false)

    expect(
      sessionWindowReady(
        { id: 'session', label: 'Session', usedPercent: 80, resetsAt: now + 10 * 60_000 },
        now
      )
    ).toBe(false)
  })

  test('quiet-chats score prefers more unused quota and less reset time', () => {
    const now = 1_000

    const urgentUnused = sessionWindowQuietScore(
      { id: 'session', label: 'Session', usedPercent: 40, resetsAt: now + 10 * 60_000 },
      now
    )
    const laterMoreUnused = sessionWindowQuietScore(
      { id: 'session', label: 'Session', usedPercent: 10, resetsAt: now + 60 * 60_000 },
      now
    )

    expect(urgentUnused).not.toBeNull()
    expect(laterMoreUnused).not.toBeNull()
    expect(urgentUnused!).toBeGreaterThan(laterMoreUnused!)
  })

  test('quiet-chats score ignores expired or unmeasurable windows', () => {
    const now = 1_000

    expect(
      sessionWindowQuietScore(
        { id: 'session', label: 'Session', usedPercent: 40, resetsAt: now },
        now
      )
    ).toBeNull()
    expect(
      sessionWindowQuietScore(
        { id: 'session', label: 'Session', usedPercent: null, resetsAt: now + 60_000 },
        now
      )
    ).toBeNull()
  })
})

<file path="__test/regressions/insights-suggestions-queries.test.ts">
import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite'

import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, test } from 'vitest'

import {
  RESOLVED_SUGGESTIONS_WHERE,
  VISIBLE_SUGGESTIONS_WHERE
} from '@blume/storage-sql'

// Exercises the real WHERE fragments the repository builds its list queries
// from (see insights.ts), against an in-memory DB. better-sqlite3 can't load
// under vitest (its native ABI is built for Electron), so we use Node's
// built-in SQLite — the SQL dialect is the same for these clauses.

const NOW = 1_000_000

interface Row {
  id: number
  status: string
  snoozed_until: number | null
  hidden_at: number | null
  hidden_until: number | null
}

describe('suggestion list WHERE fragments', () => {
  let db: DatabaseSync

  beforeEach(() => {
    db = new DatabaseSync(':memory:')
    db.exec(
      `CREATE TABLE suggestions (
         id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
         status TEXT NOT NULL,
         snoozed_until INTEGER,
         hidden_at INTEGER,
         hidden_until INTEGER,
         updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
       )`
    )
    const insert = db.prepare(
      'INSERT INTO suggestions (id, status, snoozed_until) VALUES (?, ?, ?)'
    )
    insert.run(1, 'active', null)
    insert.run(2, 'needs_review', null)
    insert.run(3, 'snoozed', NOW - 1) // timer elapsed → open
    insert.run(4, 'snoozed', NOW + 1) // timer in the future → resolved
    insert.run(5, 'snoozed', null) // malformed: no timer
    insert.run(6, 'dismissed', null)
    insert.run(7, 'applied', null)
    insert.run(8, 'archived', null)
    insert.run(9, 'draft', null)
    db.prepare('UPDATE suggestions SET hidden_at = ? WHERE id = ?').run(NOW - 10, 1)
  })

  afterEach(() => db.close())

  const ids = (where: string): number[] =>
    (
      db.prepare(`SELECT id FROM suggestions WHERE ${where} ORDER BY id`).all(NOW, NOW) as Row[]
    ).map((r) => r.id)

  test('visible list = active/needs_review + elapsed snooze (not NULL-timer)', () => {
    expect(ids(VISIBLE_SUGGESTIONS_WHERE)).toEqual([2, 3])
  })

  test('resolved list = applied/dismissed/archived + future snooze (not NULL-timer)', () => {
    expect(ids(RESOLVED_SUGGESTIONS_WHERE)).toEqual([1, 4, 6, 7, 8])
  })

  test('a snoozed row with NULL snoozed_until appears in neither list', () => {
    expect(ids(VISIBLE_SUGGESTIONS_WHERE)).not.toContain(5)
    expect(ids(RESOLVED_SUGGESTIONS_WHERE)).not.toContain(5)
  })

  test('a draft suggestion appears in neither list', () => {
    expect(ids(VISIBLE_SUGGESTIONS_WHERE)).not.toContain(9)
    expect(ids(RESOLVED_SUGGESTIONS_WHERE)).not.toContain(9)
  })
})

<file path="__test/regressions/insights.test.ts">
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { dirname, isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path'
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, test } from 'vitest'

import {
  buildConversationPacket,
  createImproveApplyRuntime,
  formatToolCallForPacket,
  parseExtraction,
  parsePlanning
} from '@blume/app-core'
import type { RevertRecord, SuggestionOperation } from '@blume/app-core'
import { buildScrubbedEnv } from '../../src/main/insights/nodeHarnessProcess'

const sha256 = (s: string): string => createHash('sha256').update(s, 'utf8').digest('hex')

async function readTextFile(path: string): Promise<string | null> {
  try {
    const s = await stat(path)
    if (!s.isFile()) return null
    return await readFile(path, 'utf8')
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

const applyRuntime = createImproveApplyRuntime({
  filesystem: {
    isAbsolutePath: isAbsolute,
    readTextFile,
    async writeTextFile(path: string, content: string): Promise<void> {
      await mkdir(dirname(path), { recursive: true })
      await writeFile(path, content, 'utf8')
    },
    async removeFile(path: string): Promise<void> {
      await rm(path, { force: true })
    }
  },
  hashText: sha256
})

const applyOperations = applyRuntime.applyOperations
const undoOperations = applyRuntime.undoOperations

describe('formatToolCallForPacket', () => {
  test('keeps call name and parameters but omits successful output', () => {
    const text = formatToolCallForPacket({
      name: 'exec_command',
      input_json: JSON.stringify({
        cmd: 'pnpm test',
        prompt: 'x'.repeat(1_200)
      }),
      result_text: 'SUCCESSFUL TOOL OUTPUT '.repeat(200),
      is_error: 0
    })

    expect(text).toContain('Tool call: exec_command')
    expect(text).toContain('Parameters:')
    expect(text).toContain('"cmd":"pnpm test"')
    expect(text).toContain('Errored: no')
    expect(text).toContain('chars)')
    expect(text).not.toContain('SUCCESSFUL TOOL OUTPUT')
    expect(text).not.toContain('x'.repeat(800))
  })

  test('includes only the error text for failed calls', () => {
    const text = formatToolCallForPacket({
      name: 'read_file',
      input_json: JSON.stringify({ path: '/tmp/missing.jsonl' }),
      result_text: 'ENOENT: no such file or directory',
      is_error: 1
    })

    expect(text).toContain('Tool call: read_file')
    expect(text).toContain('Errored: yes')
    expect(text).toContain('Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory')
  })
})

describe('buildConversationPacket', () => {
  test('hashes tool parameters while excluding successful tool output', async () => {
    let inputJson = JSON.stringify({ cmd: 'pnpm test' })
    let resultText = 'first successful command output'
    const events = [
      {
        id: 1,
        user_turn_id: 1,
        position: 0,
        kind: 'user_text',
        text: 'run the checks',
        timestamp_ms: null,
        tool_call_id: null
      },
      {
        id: 2,
        user_turn_id: 1,
        position: 1,
        kind: 'assistant_text',
        text: null,
        timestamp_ms: null,
        tool_call_id: null
      },
      {
        id: 3,
        user_turn_id: 1,
        position: 2,
        kind: 'tool_result',
        text: resultText,
        timestamp_ms: null,
        tool_call_id: 1
      }
    ]
    const reader = {
      async getConversationPacketRows() {
        return {
          events,
          toolCalls: [
            {
              id: 1,
              conversation_id: 1,
              event_id: 2,
              tool_use_id: 'call-1',
              name: 'exec_command',
              input_json: inputJson,
              result_text: resultText,
              is_error: 0,
              started_at_ms: null,
              ended_at_ms: null
            }
          ],
          userTurns: [
            {
              id: 1,
              conversation_id: 1,
              position: 1,
              prompt: 'run the checks',
              state: 'finished',
              started_at: null,
              ended_at: null
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    }

    const first = await buildConversationPacket(reader, 1)
    resultText = 'second successful command output'
    events[2].text = resultText
    const changedOutput = await buildConversationPacket(reader, 1)

    expect(changedOutput.messages).toEqual(first.messages)
    expect(changedOutput.transcriptHash).toBe(first.transcriptHash)
    expect(JSON.stringify(first.messages)).not.toContain('successful command output')

    inputJson = JSON.stringify({ cmd: 'pnpm typecheck' })
    const changedInput = await buildConversationPacket(reader, 1)

    expect(changedInput.messages).not.toEqual(first.messages)
    expect(changedInput.transcriptHash).not.toBe(first.transcriptHash)
    expect(JSON.stringify(changedInput.messages)).toContain('pnpm typecheck')
  })
})

describe('parseExtraction', () => {
  test('clamps painScore and confidence, normalizes kind', () => {
    const [sig] = parseExtraction({
      signals: [{ kind: 'nonsense', normalizedKey: 'k', summary: 's', painScore: 9, confidence: 2 }]
    })
    expect(sig.kind).toBe('other')
    expect(sig.painScore).toBe(3)
    expect(sig.confidence).toBe(1)
  })
  test('drops entries missing a summary or key', () => {
    const out = parseExtraction({
      signals: [{ kind: 'command', normalizedKey: 'k' }, { summary: 'no key' }]
    })
    expect(out).toHaveLength(0)
  })
  test('accepts snake_case fields from the model', () => {
    const [sig] = parseExtraction({
      signals: [{ kind: 'command', normalized_key: 'pm.pnpm', summary: 'use pnpm' }]
    })
    expect(sig.normalizedKey).toBe('pm.pnpm')
  })
})

describe('parsePlanning', () => {
  test('returns null when there are no operations', () => {
    expect(parsePlanning({ title: 't', summary: 's', operations: [] })).toBeNull()
  })
  test('parses an operation and defaults the title', () => {
    const planned = parsePlanning({
      operations: [{ action: 'update', targetPath: '/x', summary: 'u', patchPreview: 'p' }]
    })
    expect(planned).not.toBeNull()
    expect(planned?.operations[0].action).toBe('update')
    expect(planned?.title.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
  })
})

describe('applyOperations', () => {
  let dir = ''
  beforeEach(async () => {
    dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'blume-insights-test-'))
  })
  afterEach(async () => {
    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })
  })

  test('applies an update when the base hash matches', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'AGENTS.md')
    const original = '# Guide\n'
    await writeFile(path, original, 'utf8')
    const op: SuggestionOperation = {
      action: 'update',
      artifactType: 'doc',
      artifactScope: 'project',
      harnessApplicability: 'shared',
      targetPath: path,
      baseHash: sha256(original),
      summary: 'append',
      patchPreview: '+line',
      newContent: original + '- new rule\n'
    }
    const result = await applyOperations([op])
    expect(result.status).toBe('applied')
    expect(await readFile(path, 'utf8')).toContain('- new rule')
  })

  test('returns needs_review when the file changed (hash mismatch)', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'AGENTS.md')
    await writeFile(path, 'changed since planning\n', 'utf8')
    const op: SuggestionOperation = {
      action: 'update',
      artifactType: 'doc',
      artifactScope: 'project',
      harnessApplicability: 'shared',
      targetPath: path,
      baseHash: sha256('the original content'),
      summary: 'append',
      patchPreview: '+line',
      newContent: 'overwrite'
    }
    const result = await applyOperations([op])
    expect(result.status).toBe('needs_review')
    // The file must be untouched.
    expect(await readFile(path, 'utf8')).toBe('changed since planning\n')
  })

  test('creates a new file and refuses to create over an existing one', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'sub', 'new.md')
    const create: SuggestionOperation = {
      action: 'create',
      artifactType: 'doc',
      artifactScope: 'project',
      harnessApplicability: 'shared',
      targetPath: path,
      baseHash: null,
      summary: 'create',
      patchPreview: '+file',
      newContent: '# new\n'
    }
    expect((await applyOperations([create])).status).toBe('applied')
    expect((await stat(path)).isFile()).toBe(true)
    // Second create over the now-existing file → needs_review, no overwrite.
    expect((await applyOperations([create])).status).toBe('needs_review')
  })

  test('removes a file', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'gone.md')
    await writeFile(path, 'bye', 'utf8')
    const op: SuggestionOperation = {
      action: 'remove',
      artifactType: 'doc',
      artifactScope: 'project',
      harnessApplicability: 'shared',
      targetPath: path,
      baseHash: sha256('bye'),
      summary: 'remove',
      patchPreview: '-file'
    }
    expect((await applyOperations([op])).status).toBe('applied')
    await expect(stat(path)).rejects.toThrow()
  })

  test('refuses an update with no base hash (fail closed)', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'AGENTS.md')
    const original = '# Guide\n'
    await writeFile(path, original, 'utf8')
    const op: SuggestionOperation = {
      action: 'update',
      artifactType: 'doc',
      artifactScope: 'project',
      harnessApplicability: 'shared',
      targetPath: path,
      baseHash: null,
      summary: 'append',
      patchPreview: '+line',
      newContent: original + '- new rule\n'
    }
    const result = await applyOperations([op])
    expect(result.status).toBe('needs_review')
    expect(await readFile(path, 'utf8')).toBe(original) // untouched
  })

  test('rolls back earlier writes when a later op fails (atomic)', async () => {
    const keep = join(dir, 'keep.md')
    const original = '# keep\n'
    await writeFile(keep, original, 'utf8')
    const update: SuggestionOperation = {
      action: 'update',
      artifactType: 'doc',
      artifactScope: 'project',
      harnessApplicability: 'shared',
      targetPath: keep,
      baseHash: sha256(original),
      summary: 'edit',
      patchPreview: '~',
      newContent: '# keep\n- edited\n'
    }
    // A create whose parent dir is actually a file → mkdir fails at apply time,
    // after the update has already been written.
    const doomed: SuggestionOperation = {
      action: 'create',
      artifactType: 'doc',
      artifactScope: 'project',
      harnessApplicability: 'shared',
      targetPath: join(keep, 'child.md'),
      baseHash: null,
      summary: 'create',
      patchPreview: '+',
      newContent: 'x'
    }
    const result = await applyOperations([update, doomed])
    expect(result.status).toBe('error')
    // The earlier update must have been rolled back to the original bytes.
    expect(await readFile(keep, 'utf8')).toBe(original)
  })
})

describe('buildScrubbedEnv', () => {
  test('drops secret-bearing vars but keeps provider CLI auth + session vars', () => {
    const env = buildScrubbedEnv({
      PATH: '/usr/bin',
      HOME: '/Users/x',
      GITHUB_TOKEN: 'ghp_secret',
      AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: 'aws',
      MY_PASSWORD: 'pw',
      DB_SESSION: 'sess',
      SSH_AUTH_SOCK: '/tmp/agent.sock',
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: 'sk-ant',
      OPENAI_API_KEY: 'sk-oai'
    })
    // Non-secret config passes through.
    expect(env.PATH).toBe('/usr/bin')
    expect(env.HOME).toBe('/Users/x')
    // Unrelated secrets are scrubbed.
    expect(env.GITHUB_TOKEN).toBeUndefined()
    expect(env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY).toBeUndefined()
    expect(env.MY_PASSWORD).toBeUndefined()
    expect(env.DB_SESSION).toBeUndefined()
    // Allowlisted: session var + the provider CLIs' own auth keys.
    expect(env.SSH_AUTH_SOCK).toBe('/tmp/agent.sock')
    expect(env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).toBe('sk-ant')
    expect(env.OPENAI_API_KEY).toBe('sk-oai')
  })
})

describe('undoOperations', () => {
  let dir = ''
  beforeEach(async () => {
    dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'blume-undo-test-'))
  })
  afterEach(async () => {
    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })
  })

  test('fails closed when a create/update revert record has no applied hash', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'doc.md')
    await writeFile(path, 'CURRENT', 'utf8')
    const revert: RevertRecord[] = [
      { path, action: 'update', previousContent: 'OLD', appliedHash: null }
    ]
    const result = await undoOperations(revert)
    expect(result.status).toBe('needs_review')
    expect(await readFile(path, 'utf8')).toBe('CURRENT') // untouched
  })

  test('rolls back an earlier revert when a later one fails (atomic)', async () => {
    const a = join(dir, 'A.md')
    await writeFile(a, 'APPLIED-A', 'utf8')
    // `B` is a regular file; the 2nd record targets a path *under* it, so undo's
    // mkdir(dirname) hits ENOTDIR and throws mid-loop.
    const bFile = join(dir, 'B')
    await writeFile(bFile, 'iamafile', 'utf8')
    const revert: RevertRecord[] = [
      { path: a, action: 'update', previousContent: 'OLD-A', appliedHash: sha256('APPLIED-A') },
      {
        path: join(bFile, 'child.md'),
        action: 'update',
        previousContent: 'OLD-B',
        appliedHash: sha256('x')
      }
    ]
    const result = await undoOperations(revert)
    expect(result.status).toBe('error')
    // A must be rolled back to its applied bytes, not left at the reverted 'OLD-A'.
    expect(await readFile(a, 'utf8')).toBe('APPLIED-A')
  })
})

import {
  IMPROVE_INSTALLATION_ID_SETTING,
  IMPROVE_INSTALLATION_TOKEN_SETTING
} from '@blume/app-core'
const fixture = vi.hoisted(() => ({ values: new Map<string, string>(), available: true }))
vi.mock('../../src/main/settingsStore', () => ({
  getSetting: (key: string) => fixture.values.get(key) ?? null,
  setSetting: (key: string, value: string) => {
    fixture.values.set(key, value)
  }
}))
vi.mock('../../src/main/blume-user-host', () => ({
  getOrCreateBlumeId: async () => 'fixture-installation'
}))
vi.mock('electron', () => ({
  safeStorage: {
    isEncryptionAvailable: () => fixture.available,
    encryptString: (value: string) => Buffer.from(`encrypted:${value}`),
    decryptString: (value: Buffer) => {
      const encoded = value.toString()
      if (!encoded.startsWith('encrypted:')) throw new Error('Cannot decrypt')
      return encoded.slice('encrypted:'.length)
    }
  }
}))
const release = {
  version: '1.0.76-c.0',
  channel: 'canary',
  sourceSha: 'a'.repeat(40),
  bundleId: 'fixture-bundle'
} as const
beforeEach(() => {
  vi.resetModules()
  fixture.values.clear()
  fixture.available = true
})
afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals())

test('main decrypts an existing installation credential before minting a worker access token', async () => {
  fixture.values.set(IMPROVE_INSTALLATION_ID_SETTING, 'fixture-installation')
  const ciphertext = `enc:v1:${Buffer.from('encrypted:stored-installation-secret').toString('base64')}`
  fixture.values.set(IMPROVE_INSTALLATION_TOKEN_SETTING, ciphertext)
  const request = vi.fn(async (input: string, init: RequestInit) => {
    expect(input.endsWith('/v1/token')).toBe(true)
    expect(new Headers(init.headers).get('x-blume-installation-token')).toBe(
      'stored-installation-secret'
    )
    expect(init.body).not.toContain('enc:v1:')
    return Response.json({
      accessToken: 'short-lived-worker-jwt',
      expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 120_000).toISOString()
    })
  })
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', request)
  const { getLlmInstallationAccessToken } = await import('../../src/main/installationCredentials')
  await expect(getLlmInstallationAccessToken(release)).resolves.toBe('short-lived-worker-jwt')
  expect(request).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
  expect(fixture.values.get(IMPROVE_INSTALLATION_TOKEN_SETTING)).toBe(ciphertext)
})

test('main registers a new installation once and persists only encrypted credentials', async () => {
  const request = vi.fn(async () =>
    Response.json({
      installationId: 'fixture-installation',
      clientToken: 'new-installation-secret'
    })
  )
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', request)
  const { getInstallationCredentials } = await import('../../src/main/installationCredentials')
  await Promise.all([getInstallationCredentials(), getInstallationCredentials()])
  expect(request).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
  const stored = fixture.values.get(IMPROVE_INSTALLATION_TOKEN_SETTING)!
  expect(stored.startsWith('enc:v1:')).toBe(true)
  expect(stored).not.toBe('new-installation-secret')
})

test('unavailable OS encryption never persists a plaintext bootstrap credential', async () => {
  fixture.available = false
  vi.stubGlobal(
    'fetch',
    vi.fn(async () =>
      Response.json({
        installationId: 'fixture-installation',
        clientToken: 'new-installation-secret'
      })
    )
  )
  const { getInstallationCredentials } = await import('../../src/main/installationCredentials')
  await expect(getInstallationCredentials()).rejects.toThrow(
    'refusing to store the secret in plaintext'
  )
  expect(fixture.values.has(IMPROVE_INSTALLATION_TOKEN_SETTING)).toBe(false)
})

<file path="__test/regressions/legacy-exclusions-parsing-gate.test.ts">
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { expect, test } from 'vitest'

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const SRC_MAIN = resolve(HERE, '../../src/main')

// Registrations name only a harness and a conversation id, so the old excluded projects are
// honoured where the conversation's workspace is known: in the refresh worker, before storing.
test('the refresh worker leaves out conversations in excluded projects that have not moved yet', () => {
  const source = readFileSync(resolve(SRC_MAIN, 'conversations/refreshWorker.ts'), 'utf8')
  const read = source.indexOf('readLegacyProjectExclusions(')
  const gate = source.indexOf('legacyExclusionExcludesConversation(')
  const canonicalize = source.indexOf('observedWorkspaceIdentity.canonicalizeConversation(parsed)')
  const ingest = source.indexOf('ingestRuntime.ingestConversation(')
  expect(read).toBeGreaterThan(-1)
  expect(gate).toBeGreaterThan(read)
  expect(canonicalize).toBeGreaterThan(gate)
  expect(ingest).toBeGreaterThan(gate)
  // Read inside each refresh, so a row the move removes stops excluding at the next pass.
  expect(read).toBeGreaterThan(source.indexOf('async function refresh('))
})

<file path="__test/regressions/legacy-login-items.test.ts">
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { describe, expect, test, vi } from 'vitest'

import {
  cleanupLegacyBlumeTauriLaunchAgent,
  legacyBlumeTauriLaunchAgentPath
} from '../../src/main/legacyLoginItems'
import { shouldMigrateLegacyLoginItem } from '../../src/main/releaseChannel'

function tempHome(): string {
  return join(tmpdir(), `blume-legacy-login-items-${randomUUID()}`)
}

function writeLaunchAgent(homeDir: string, contents: string): string {
  const path = legacyBlumeTauriLaunchAgentPath(homeDir)
  mkdirSync(join(homeDir, 'Library', 'LaunchAgents'), { recursive: true })
  writeFileSync(path, contents)
  return path
}

const LEGACY_PLIST = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key>
  <string>Blume Tauri</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/Users/test/project/apps/tauri-desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/blume-desktop</string>
  </array>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key>
  <true/>
</dict>
</plist>
`

describe('legacy login item cleanup', () => {
  test('only stable may migrate the machine-global legacy login item', () => {
    expect(shouldMigrateLegacyLoginItem('stable')).toBe(true)
    expect(shouldMigrateLegacyLoginItem('canary')).toBe(false)
  })

  test('disables the old Blume Tauri LaunchAgent', async () => {
    const homeDir = tempHome()
    const bootout = vi.fn(async () => {})

    try {
      const path = writeLaunchAgent(homeDir, LEGACY_PLIST)
      const result = await cleanupLegacyBlumeTauriLaunchAgent({
        homeDir,
        platform: 'darwin',
        bootout,
        disabledSuffix: '.disabled-test'
      })

      expect(result.cleaned).toBe(true)
      expect(result.disabledPath).toBe(`${path}.disabled-test`)
      expect(bootout).toHaveBeenCalledWith(path, expect.any(AbortSignal))
      expect(existsSync(path)).toBe(false)
      expect(readFileSync(`${path}.disabled-test`, 'utf8')).toBe(LEGACY_PLIST)
    } finally {
      rmSync(homeDir, { recursive: true, force: true })
    }
  })

  test('leaves unrelated LaunchAgents alone', async () => {
    const homeDir = tempHome()
    const bootout = vi.fn(async () => {})

    try {
      const contents = LEGACY_PLIST.replace('blume-desktop', 'something-else')
      const path = writeLaunchAgent(homeDir, contents)
      const result = await cleanupLegacyBlumeTauriLaunchAgent({
        homeDir,
        platform: 'darwin',
        bootout
      })

      expect(result).toMatchObject({
        cleaned: false,
        path,
        reason: 'not-legacy-blume-tauri'
      })
      expect(bootout).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
      expect(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')).toBe(contents)
    } finally {
      rmSync(homeDir, { recursive: true, force: true })
    }
  })

  test('bounds a stalled launchctl cleanup and still archives the legacy item', async () => {
    const homeDir = tempHome()

    try {
      const path = writeLaunchAgent(homeDir, LEGACY_PLIST)
      const startedAt = Date.now()
      const result = await cleanupLegacyBlumeTauriLaunchAgent({
        homeDir,
        platform: 'darwin',
        bootout: async () => await new Promise(() => {}),
        bootoutTimeoutMs: 20,
        disabledSuffix: '.disabled-timeout-test'
      })

      expect(Date.now() - startedAt).toBeLessThan(500)
      expect(result.cleaned).toBe(true)
      expect(existsSync(`${path}.disabled-timeout-test`)).toBe(true)
    } finally {
      rmSync(homeDir, { recursive: true, force: true })
    }
  })

  test('keeps synchronous filesystem and subprocess work out of the migration adapter', () => {
    const source = readFileSync(
      join(import.meta.dirname, '../../src/main/legacyLoginItems.ts'),
      'utf8'
    )
    expect(source).not.toMatch(/\b(?:spawnSync|execFileSync|\w+Sync)\b/)
  })
})

<file path="__test/regressions/main-session-and-flag-reads.test.ts">
/**
 * Main answers the account session and PostHog flags without a network round trip per read
 * (docs/desktop-runtime-performance.md, October 27, 2026): concurrent session reads share one
 * request, a flag is asked of PostHog at most once a minute, and an account change forgets both.
 */
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from 'vitest'

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  settings: new Map<string, string>(),
  getFeatureFlagResult: vi.fn(),
  authClient: {
    authenticate: vi.fn(),
    setupMain: vi.fn(),
    signIn: { email: vi.fn() },
    signUp: { email: vi.fn() },
    signOut: vi.fn(),
    getSession: vi.fn(),
    updateUser: vi.fn(),
    listAccounts: vi.fn()
  }
}))

vi.mock('electron', () => ({
  app: {
    getVersion: () => '1.0.69',
    userAgentFallback: 'Blume/1.0.69'
  },
  BrowserWindow: {
    getFocusedWindow: () => null
  }
}))

vi.mock('better-auth/client', () => ({
  createAuthClient: () => mocks.authClient
}))

vi.mock('better-auth/client/plugins', () => ({
  adminClient: () => ({ id: 'admin' })
}))

vi.mock('@better-auth/electron/client', () => ({
  electronClient: () => ({ id: 'electron' }),
  normalizeUserOutput: (value: { id: string }) => ({ ...value, image: null })
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/blume-user-host', () => ({
  getOrCreateBlumeDeviceId: vi.fn(async () => 'device-test-id'),
  getOrCreateBlumeId: vi.fn(async () => 'blume-test-id')
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/secureStore', () => ({
  getSecret: vi.fn(),
  setSecret: vi.fn()
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/releaseMetadata', () => ({
  resolveDesktopReleaseMetadata: () => ({
    version: '1.0.69',
    channel: 'stable',
    sourceSha: null,
    bundleId: null
  })
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/settingsStore', () => ({
  getSetting: vi.fn((key: string) => mocks.settings.get(key) ?? null)
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/logger', () => ({
  writeAppLog: vi.fn()
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/sentry', () => ({
  captureSentryException: vi.fn()
}))

vi.mock('posthog-node', () => ({
  PostHog: class {
    getFeatureFlagResult = mocks.getFeatureFlagResult
  }
}))

const FLAG = 'desktop-menu-bar-status-item'

function deferred<T>(): { promise: Promise<T>; resolve(value: T): void } {
  let resolve!: (value: T) => void
  const promise = new Promise<T>((done) => (resolve = done))
  return { promise, resolve }
}

function sessionOf(userId: string | null) {
  return userId
    ? {
        session: { expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60_000).toISOString() },
        user: { id: userId, name: 'Preview', email: 'preview@example.invalid', role: '' }
      }
    : null
}

/** The account service, answering `user` (null: signed out) once `release` is called, if given. */
function answerSessionAs(user: () => string | null, gate?: Promise<void>): void {
  mocks.authClient.getSession.mockImplementation(async ({ fetchOptions }) => {
    await gate
    const data = sessionOf(user())
    await fetchOptions.onResponse({ response: Response.json(data) })
    return { data, error: null }
  })
}

async function settle(): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) await Promise.resolve()
  await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, 0))
}

async function load() {
  vi.resetModules()
  const accounts = await import('../../src/main/accounts')
  const telemetry = await import('../../src/main/telemetry')
  // As the main entry wires it (src/main/index.ts).
  accounts.deliveryAccounts.onChanged?.(telemetry.clearPosthogFeatureFlagCache)
  return { ...accounts, ...telemetry }
}

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.clearAllMocks()
  vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })
  vi.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-10-27T12:00:00Z'))
  process.env.VITE_POSTHOG_KEY = 'test-posthog-key'
  mocks.settings.clear()
  mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockResolvedValue({ key: FLAG, enabled: true })
  mocks.authClient.listAccounts.mockResolvedValue({ data: [], error: null })
  mocks.authClient.signOut.mockResolvedValue({ error: null })
})

afterEach(() => {
  vi.useRealTimers()
  delete process.env.VITE_POSTHOG_KEY
})

describe('account session reads in main', () => {
  test('concurrent reads make one request to the account service', async () => {
    const gate = deferred<void>()
    answerSessionAs(() => 'person-a', gate.promise)
    const { getAccountSession } = await load()

    const reads = Array.from({ length: 8 }, () => getAccountSession())
    gate.resolve()
    const sessions = await Promise.all(reads)

    expect(mocks.authClient.getSession).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
    expect(sessions.every((session) => session?.user.id === 'person-a')).toBe(true)
  })

  test('the accounts are read side by side with the session, not after it', async () => {
    const gate = deferred<void>()
    answerSessionAs(() => 'person-a', gate.promise)
    const { getAccountSession } = await load()

    const read = getAccountSession()
    await settle()
    expect(mocks.authClient.listAccounts).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
    gate.resolve()
    await expect(read).resolves.toMatchObject({ user: { id: 'person-a', hasPassword: false } })
  })

  test('an older answer is given at once while one newer read runs', async () => {
    answerSessionAs(() => 'person-a')
    const { getAccountSession } = await load()
    await getAccountSession()

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 5_000)
    await getAccountSession()
    expect(mocks.authClient.getSession).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 20_000)
    const gate = deferred<void>()
    answerSessionAs(() => 'person-a', gate.promise)
    // Neither waits for the service; together they start one read.
    await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toMatchObject({ user: { id: 'person-a' } })
    await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toMatchObject({ user: { id: 'person-a' } })
    expect(mocks.authClient.getSession).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
    gate.resolve()
  })

  test('a session revoked elsewhere reaches the app as an account change', async () => {
    let user: string | null = 'person-a'
    answerSessionAs(() => user)
    const { getAccountSession, deliveryAccounts } = await load()
    const changed = vi.fn()
    deliveryAccounts.onChanged?.(changed)
    await getAccountSession()

    user = null
    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 20_000)
    // The read that finds it gone runs behind the last answer...
    await getAccountSession()
    await settle()
    expect(changed).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
    // ...and the next reader is told at once, without another request.
    await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toBeNull()
    expect(mocks.authClient.getSession).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
  })

  test('an answer older than ten minutes is not given', async () => {
    let user: string | null = 'person-a'
    answerSessionAs(() => user)
    const { getAccountSession } = await load()
    await getAccountSession()

    user = null
    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 11 * 60_000)
    await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toBeNull()
  })

  test('a failed read is not hidden behind the last answer', async () => {
    answerSessionAs(() => 'person-a')
    const { getAccountSession } = await load()
    await getAccountSession()

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 20_000)
    mocks.authClient.getSession.mockImplementation(async ({ fetchOptions }) => {
      await fetchOptions.onResponse({ response: new Response('bad gateway', { status: 502 }) })
      return { data: null, error: { status: 502 } }
    })
    await getAccountSession()
    await settle()
    await expect(getAccountSession()).rejects.toThrow()
  })
})

describe('PostHog flag reads in main', () => {
  test('reads within a minute make no PostHog request', async () => {
    const { isPosthogFeatureEnabled, getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await load()

    await expect(isPosthogFeatureEnabled(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(true)
    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 30_000)
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(true)

    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
  })

  test('concurrent first reads share one PostHog request', async () => {
    const answer = deferred<{ key: string; enabled: boolean; variant: string }>()
    mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockReturnValue(answer.promise)
    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await load()

    const reads = Array.from({ length: 5 }, () => getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG))
    answer.resolve({ key: FLAG, enabled: true, variant: 'page_footer' })

    expect(await Promise.all(reads)).toEqual(Array(5).fill('page_footer'))
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
  })

  test('an older assignment is answered at once and renewed behind it', async () => {
    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await load()
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 61_000)
    const answer = deferred<{ key: string; enabled: boolean }>()
    mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockReturnValue(answer.promise)
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(true)
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(true)
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)

    answer.resolve({ key: FLAG, enabled: false })
    await settle()
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(false)
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
  })

  test('a request that fails keeps the last assignment and tries again soon', async () => {
    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await load()
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 61_000)
    mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockRejectedValue(new Error('offline'))
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)
    await settle()
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(true)
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 11_000)
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3)
  })

  test('a flag PostHog stops answering (switched off or deleted) is off', async () => {
    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await load()
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 61_000)
    mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockResolvedValue(undefined)
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)
    await settle()
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(false)
  })

  test('an assignment five minutes old is not given: the read waits for PostHog', async () => {
    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await load()
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 5 * 60_000)
    mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockResolvedValue({ key: FLAG, enabled: false })
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(false)
  })

  test('a renewed assignment that differs is announced once, so subscribers read again', async () => {
    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue, onPosthogFeatureFlagsChanged } = await load()
    const announced = vi.fn()
    onPosthogFeatureFlagsChanged(announced)
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 61_000)
    await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)
    await settle()
    expect(announced).not.toHaveBeenCalled()

    vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 61_000)
    mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockResolvedValue({ key: FLAG, enabled: false })
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(true)
    await settle()
    expect(announced).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(false)
  })

  test('a first read that fails answers false, as before', async () => {
    mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockRejectedValue(new Error('offline'))
    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await load()
    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)).resolves.toBe(false)
  })
})

test('signing out forgets both the session and the flags', async () => {
  answerSessionAs(() => 'person-a')
  const { getAccountSession, getPosthogFeatureFlagValue, deliveryAccounts } = await load()
  await getAccountSession()
  await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)

  answerSessionAs(() => null)
  await deliveryAccounts.signOut()

  // Neither the last session nor the last assignment is given: both are asked again.
  await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toBeNull()
  await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)
  expect(mocks.authClient.getSession).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
  expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
})

test('an account change announces the flags, so subscribers read them again', async () => {
  answerSessionAs(() => 'person-a')
  const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue, onPosthogFeatureFlagsChanged, deliveryAccounts } = await load()
  const announced = vi.fn()
  onPosthogFeatureFlagsChanged(announced)
  await getPosthogFeatureFlagValue(FLAG)

  await deliveryAccounts.signOut()
  await settle()
  expect(announced).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
})

test('signing in keeps the session it read, so the next reader does not ask again', async () => {
  answerSessionAs(() => null)
  const { getAccountSession, registerAccountIpcHandlers } = await load()
  await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toBeNull()

  answerSessionAs(() => 'person-b')
  mocks.authClient.signIn.email.mockResolvedValue({ data: {}, error: null })
  type Handler = Parameters<Parameters<typeof registerAccountIpcHandlers>[0]>[1]
  const handlers = new Map<string, Handler>()
  registerAccountIpcHandlers((name, handler) => handlers.set(name, handler))
  await handlers.get('account:signIn')!(undefined as never, {
    email: 'preview@example.invalid',
    password: 'synthetic-password'
  })

  await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toMatchObject({ user: { id: 'person-b' } })
  expect(mocks.authClient.getSession).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
})

test('a sign-in read that an account change overtakes is not kept', async () => {
  answerSessionAs(() => null)
  const { getAccountSession, registerAccountIpcHandlers, deliveryAccounts } = await load()
  await getAccountSession()

  const gate = deferred<void>()
  answerSessionAs(() => 'person-b', gate.promise)
  mocks.authClient.signIn.email.mockResolvedValue({ data: {}, error: null })
  type Handler = Parameters<Parameters<typeof registerAccountIpcHandlers>[0]>[1]
  const handlers = new Map<string, Handler>()
  registerAccountIpcHandlers((name, handler) => handlers.set(name, handler))
  const signingIn = handlers.get('account:signIn')!(undefined as never, {
    email: 'preview@example.invalid',
    password: 'synthetic-password'
  })
  await settle()
  // A sign-out lands while the sign-in is still reading its session.
  await deliveryAccounts.signOut()
  gate.resolve()
  await signingIn

  answerSessionAs(() => null)
  await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toBeNull()
})

test('a sign-in read that a revocation found behind the last answer overtakes is not kept', async () => {
  let user: string | null = 'person-a'
  answerSessionAs(() => user)
  const { getAccountSession, registerAccountIpcHandlers } = await load()
  await getAccountSession()

  // A sign-in starts reading its session, and is held there.
  const signInGate = deferred<void>()
  mocks.authClient.signIn.email.mockResolvedValue({ data: {}, error: null })
  mocks.authClient.getSession.mockImplementationOnce(async ({ fetchOptions }) => {
    await signInGate.promise
    const data = sessionOf('person-a')
    await fetchOptions.onResponse({ response: Response.json(data) })
    return { data, error: null }
  })
  type Handler = Parameters<Parameters<typeof registerAccountIpcHandlers>[0]>[1]
  const handlers = new Map<string, Handler>()
  registerAccountIpcHandlers((name, handler) => handlers.set(name, handler))
  const signingIn = handlers.get('account:signIn')!(undefined as never, {
    email: 'preview@example.invalid',
    password: 'synthetic-password'
  })
  await settle()

  // Meanwhile a newer read finds the session revoked.
  user = null
  vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 20_000)
  await getAccountSession()
  await settle()

  signInGate.resolve()
  await signingIn
  await expect(getAccountSession()).resolves.toBeNull()
})

async function loadTelemetry(): Promise<typeof import('../../src/main/telemetry')> {
  vi.resetModules()
  return import('../../src/main/telemetry')
}

beforeEach(() => {
  process.env.VITE_POSTHOG_KEY = 'test-posthog-key'
  mocks.settings.clear()
  mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockClear()
  mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockResolvedValue({ enabled: true })
  mocks.getAllFlags.mockClear()

afterEach(() => {
  delete process.env.VITE_POSTHOG_KEY

describe('main telemetry feature flags', () => {

    mocks.settings.set('posthogTrackingDisabled', 'true')

    const { isPosthogFeatureEnabled } = await loadTelemetry()

    await expect(isPosthogFeatureEnabled('desktop-menu-bar-status-item')).resolves.toBe(true)
    expect(mocks.posthogConstructor).toHaveBeenCalledWith(

    )
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'desktop-menu-bar-status-item',
      'blume-test-id',
      { sendFeatureFlagEvents: false }
    )
  })

  test('keeps feature flag exposure events enabled when capture is allowed', async () => {
    const { isPosthogFeatureEnabled } = await loadTelemetry()

    await expect(isPosthogFeatureEnabled('desktop-menu-bar-status-item')).resolves.toBe(true)
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'desktop-menu-bar-status-item',
      'blume-test-id',
      { sendFeatureFlagEvents: true }
    )
  })

  test('preserves a multivariate feature flag assignment', async () => {
    mocks.getFeatureFlagResult.mockResolvedValue({
      key: 'referral-share-prompt-placement',
      enabled: true,
      variant: 'page_footer',
      payload: undefined
    })

    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await loadTelemetry()

    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue('referral-share-prompt-placement')).resolves.toBe(
      'page_footer'
    )
  })

  test.each([
    ['enabled', true],
    ['disabled', false]
  ])('uses a locally forced %s value without asking PostHog', async (_label, enabled) => {
    mocks.settings.set(
      'posthogFeatureFlagOverrides',
      JSON.stringify({ 'desktop-menu-bar-status-item': enabled })
    )

    const { isPosthogFeatureEnabled } = await loadTelemetry()

    await expect(isPosthogFeatureEnabled('desktop-menu-bar-status-item')).resolves.toBe(enabled)
    expect(mocks.posthogConstructor).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })

  test('uses a locally forced experiment variant without asking PostHog', async () => {
    mocks.settings.set(
      'posthogExperimentOverrides',
      JSON.stringify({ 'referral-share-prompt-placement': 'page_footer' })
    )

    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagValue } = await loadTelemetry()

    await expect(getPosthogFeatureFlagValue('referral-share-prompt-placement')).resolves.toBe(
      'page_footer'
    )
    expect(mocks.posthogConstructor).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
    expect(mocks.getFeatureFlagResult).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })

  test('separates PostHog status from this installation evaluation', async () => {
    mocks.settings.set(
      'posthogFeatureFlagOverrides',
      JSON.stringify({ 'desktop-menu-bar-status-item': true })
    )
    mocks.getAllFlags.mockResolvedValue({
      'desktop-menu-bar-status-item': false,
      'cursor-usage': true,
      'desktop-conversation-continuation-menu': 'test-variant'
    })

    const { getPosthogFeatureFlagEvaluations } = await loadTelemetry()
    const evaluations = await getPosthogFeatureFlagEvaluations()

    expect(evaluations['desktop-menu-bar-status-item']).toEqual({
      posthogStatus: 'enabled',
      installationEnabled: false
    })
    expect(evaluations['cursor-usage']).toEqual({
      posthogStatus: 'enabled',
      installationEnabled: true
    })
    expect(evaluations['desktop-conversation-continuation-menu']).toEqual({
      posthogStatus: 'enabled',
      installationEnabled: true
    })
    expect(evaluations['artifact-sync']).toEqual({
      posthogStatus: 'not-active',
      installationEnabled: false
    })
    expect(mocks.getAllFlags).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'blume-test-id',
      expect.objectContaining({
        flagKeys: expect.arrayContaining([
          'desktop-menu-bar-status-item',
          'cursor-usage',
          'artifact-sync'
        ])
      })
    )
  })

<file path="__test/regressions/main-window-navigation.test.ts">
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest'

import { isDevRendererNavigation, isExternallyOpenableUrl } from '../../src/main/nativeWindow'

const nativeWindow = readFileSync(
  new URL('../../src/main/nativeWindow.ts', import.meta.url),
  'utf8'
)

describe('main window navigation', () => {
  test('the primary window cannot be stranded in macOS background throttling', () => {
    const primaryWindow = nativeWindow.match(
      /const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow\(\{[\s\S]*?\n {4}\}\)/
    )
    expect(primaryWindow).not.toBeNull()
    expect(primaryWindow?.[0]).toContain('backgroundThrottling: true')
    expect(nativeWindow).toMatch(
      /mainWindow\.on\('focus',[\s\S]*?setBackgroundThrottling\(false\)/
    )
    expect(nativeWindow).toMatch(
      /const restoreBackgroundThrottling[\s\S]*?setBackgroundThrottling\(true\)/
    )
    expect(nativeWindow).toContain("mainWindow.on('blur', restoreBackgroundThrottling)")
    expect(nativeWindow).toContain("mainWindow.on('minimize', restoreBackgroundThrottling)")
    expect(nativeWindow).toContain("mainWindow.on('hide', restoreBackgroundThrottling)")
  })

  test('a top-level navigation is intercepted, not just a new-window request', () => {
    // `setWindowOpenHandler` only fires for requests to open a *new* window. A
    // plain in-page link is a top-level navigation, so without this guard it
    // replaces the app with the page — in a window with no chrome to go back.
    const guard = nativeWindow.match(
      /mainWindow\.webContents\.on\('will-navigate'[\s\S]*?\n {4}\}\)/
    )
    expect(guard).not.toBeNull()
    expect(guard?.[0]).toContain('event.preventDefault()')
    expect(guard?.[0]).toContain('openExternallyIfSafe(url)')
  })

  test('the dev renderer is still allowed to navigate itself', () => {
    // Vite reloads the renderer by navigating it; denying that would break dev.
    const guard = nativeWindow.match(
      /mainWindow\.webContents\.on\('will-navigate'[\s\S]*?\n {4}\}\)/
    )
    expect(guard?.[0]).toContain(
      'deps.isDev && deps.rendererUrl && isDevRendererNavigation(url, deps.rendererUrl)'
    )

    expect(
      isDevRendererNavigation('http://localhost:5173/conversations/1', 'http://localhost:5173')
    ).toBe(true)
    expect(
      isDevRendererNavigation('http://localhost:5173@evil.example/path', 'http://localhost:5173')
    ).toBe(false)
    expect(isDevRendererNavigation('not a URL', 'http://localhost:5173')).toBe(false)
  })

  test('only browser and mail schemes are handed to the OS', () => {
    // `shell.openExternal` delegates to the OS: a `file:` URL opens or launches
    // whatever it points at, and dropping a file onto the window is itself a
    // renderer-initiated navigation to `file://`. Anything that is not plainly
    // a web or mail address must die at the guard.
    for (const url of [
      'https://example.com/docs',
      'http://localhost:5173/',
      'mailto:someone@example.com'
    ]) {
      expect(isExternallyOpenableUrl(url), `should open: ${url}`).toBe(true)
    }

    for (const url of [
      'file:///Users/someone/Downloads/installer.dmg',
      'file:///Applications/Calculator.app',
      'javascript:alert(1)',
      'data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>',
      'vscode://file/etc/passwd',
      'smb://attacker.example/share',
      'ftp://example.com/payload',
      'blume://deep-link',
      'not a url at all',
      ''
    ]) {
      expect(isExternallyOpenableUrl(url), `must not reach the OS: ${url}`).toBe(false)
    }
  })

  test('every path out to the OS shares the same guard', () => {
    // Three call sites can hand a URL to the OS: the new-window handler (a
    // link with target="_blank" reaches it rather than will-navigate), the
    // will-navigate guard, and the rejected-webview branch, whose `src` is
    // renderer-authored. None may call openExternal directly.
    const openHandler = nativeWindow.match(
      /setWindowOpenHandler\(\(details\) => \{[\s\S]*?\n {4}\}\)/
    )
    expect(openHandler?.[0]).toContain('openExternallyIfSafe(details.url)')

    const webview = nativeWindow.match(/on\('will-attach-webview'[\s\S]*?\n {4}\}\)/)
    expect(webview?.[0]).toContain('openExternallyIfSafe(params.src)')

    // Only the helper itself may reach deps.openExternal.
    const directCalls = [...nativeWindow.matchAll(/deps\.openExternal\(/g)]
    expect(directCalls.length, 'openExternal should have exactly one call site').toBe(1)
  })

  test('the preferences shortcut ignores keyboard auto-repeat', () => {
    const shortcut = nativeWindow.match(/function wirePreferencesShortcut[\s\S]*?\n {2}\}/)
    expect(shortcut).not.toBeNull()
    expect(shortcut?.[0]).toContain('if (input.isAutoRepeat) return')
    expect(shortcut?.[0].indexOf('input.isAutoRepeat')).toBeLessThan(
      shortcut?.[0].indexOf("openPathFromNativeMenu('/settings')") ?? -1
    )
  })
})
</file>

<file path="__test/regressions/menu-bar-popover-load-error-policy.test.ts">
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'

import {
  isExpectedMenuBarBlumeMenuLoadFailure,
  isExpectedMenuBarDataUrlLoadFailure,
  isExpectedMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure,
  isExpectedMenuBarPopoverLoadTimeout,
  MENU_BAR_POPOVER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE,
  reportMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure,
  shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError,
  summarizeMenuBarPopoverLoadErrorMessage
} from '../../src/main/menuBarPopoverLoadErrorPolicy'

function errFailedDataHtml(documentSnippet: string): Error {
  return new Error(
    `ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'data:text/html;charset=utf-8,${encodeURIComponent(documentSnippet)}'`
  )
}

function errAbortedBlumeMenu(action: string): Error {
  return new Error(`ERR_ABORTED (-3) loading 'blume-menu://${action}'`)
}

describe('menu bar popover data:URL load failure policy', () => {
  it('treats Chromium ERR_FAILED on menu-bar popover data:HTML as expected non-reportable noise', () => {
    const error = errFailedDataHtml(
      '<!doctype html>\n<html class="dark"><head><title>Blume</title></head></html>'
    )

    expect(isExpectedMenuBarDataUrlLoadFailure(error)).toBe(true)
    expect(shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError(error)).toBe(false)
  })

  it('treats legacy Blume tray icon renderer ERR_FAILED data:URL loads as expected', () => {
    const error = errFailedDataHtml(
      '<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Blume tray icon renderer</title>'
    )

    expect(isExpectedMenuBarDataUrlLoadFailure(error)).toBe(true)
    expect(shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError(error)).toBe(false)
  })

  it('treats ERR_ABORTED data:text/html load aborts as expected', () => {
    const error = new Error(
      `ERR_ABORTED (-3) loading 'data:text/html;charset=utf-8,${encodeURIComponent('<html></html>')}'`
    )

    expect(isExpectedMenuBarDataUrlLoadFailure(error)).toBe(true)
  })

  it('treats destroyed-window races that still mention data:text/html as expected', () => {
    const error = new Error(
      "Object has been destroyed while loading 'data:text/html;charset=utf-8,<html></html>'"
    )

    expect(isExpectedMenuBarDataUrlLoadFailure(error)).toBe(true)
  })

  it('does not call captureAppError for expected data:URL load failures', () => {
    const captureAppError = vi.fn()
    const logInfo = vi.fn()
    const error = errFailedDataHtml(
      '<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Blume tray icon renderer</title>'
    )

    reportMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure('main.menu-bar-popover-preload', error, {
      captureAppError,
      logInfo
    })

    expect(captureAppError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
    expect(logInfo).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'expected menu bar data URL load failure',
      expect.objectContaining({
        source: 'main.menu-bar-popover-preload',
        error_name: 'Error',
        reporting_action: 'local_log_only'
      })
    )

    const logged = logInfo.mock.calls[0]?.[1] as { error_message?: string }
    expect(logged.error_message).toEqual(summarizeMenuBarPopoverLoadErrorMessage(error.message))
    expect(logged.error_message).toContain('ERR_FAILED')
    expect(logged.error_message).toContain('data:text/html;<redacted>')
    expect(logged.error_message).not.toContain('<!doctype')
    expect(logged.error_message).not.toContain(encodeURIComponent('<!doctype'))
    expect(logged.error_message).not.toBe(error.message)
    expect(logged.error_message!.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(200)
  })

  it('summarizeMenuBarPopoverLoadErrorMessage redacts data:URL bodies and preserves markers', () => {
    const raw =
      "ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'data:text/html;charset=utf-8," +
      encodeURIComponent(
        '<!doctype html><title>Blume tray icon renderer</title><body>secret</body>'
      ) +
      "'"

    const summary = summarizeMenuBarPopoverLoadErrorMessage(raw)
    expect(summary).toContain('ERR_FAILED')
    expect(summary).toContain('data:text/html;<redacted>')
    expect(summary).not.toContain('<!doctype')
    expect(summary).not.toContain('secret')
    expect(summary.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(200)
  })

  it('treats ERR_ABORTED on blume-menu://open and blume-menu://quit as expected', () => {
    for (const action of ['open', 'quit'] as const) {
      const error = errAbortedBlumeMenu(action)

      expect(isExpectedMenuBarBlumeMenuLoadFailure(error)).toBe(true)
      expect(isExpectedMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure(error)).toBe(true)
      expect(isExpectedMenuBarDataUrlLoadFailure(error)).toBe(false)
      expect(shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError(error)).toBe(false)
    }
  })

  it('treats related transient Chromium failures on other blume-menu:// actions as expected', () => {
    const cases = [
      new Error("ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'blume-menu://preferences'"),
      new Error("ERR_CONNECTION_RESET (-101) loading 'blume-menu://open'"),
      new Error("Object has been destroyed while loading 'blume-menu://conversation?ref=abc'")
    ]

    for (const error of cases) {
      expect(isExpectedMenuBarBlumeMenuLoadFailure(error)).toBe(true)
      expect(shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError(error)).toBe(false)
    }
  })

  it('does not call captureAppError for expected blume-menu:// load aborts', () => {
    const captureAppError = vi.fn()
    const logInfo = vi.fn()
    const error = errAbortedBlumeMenu('open')

    reportMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure('main.menu-bar-popover', error, {
      captureAppError,
      logInfo
    })

    expect(captureAppError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
    expect(logInfo).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'expected menu bar blume-menu protocol load abort',
      expect.objectContaining({
        source: 'main.menu-bar-popover',
        error_name: 'Error',
        error_message: "ERR_ABORTED (-3) loading 'blume-menu://open'",
        reporting_action: 'local_log_only'
      })
    )
  })

  it('treats the exact menu-bar popover load timeout as expected non-reportable noise', () => {
    const error = new Error(MENU_BAR_POPOVER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE)

    expect(isExpectedMenuBarPopoverLoadTimeout(error)).toBe(true)
    expect(isExpectedMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure(error)).toBe(true)
    expect(isExpectedMenuBarDataUrlLoadFailure(error)).toBe(false)
    expect(isExpectedMenuBarBlumeMenuLoadFailure(error)).toBe(false)
    expect(shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError(error)).toBe(false)
  })

  it('does not call captureAppError for the dedicated load timeout', () => {
    const captureAppError = vi.fn()
    const logInfo = vi.fn()
    const error = new Error(MENU_BAR_POPOVER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE)

    reportMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure('main.menu-bar-popover', error, {
      captureAppError,
      logInfo
    })

    expect(captureAppError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
    expect(logInfo).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'expected menu bar popover load timeout',
      expect.objectContaining({
        source: 'main.menu-bar-popover',
        error_name: 'Error',
        error_message: MENU_BAR_POPOVER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE,
        reporting_action: 'local_log_only'
      })
    )
  })

  it('does not demote height-measurement timeouts or updater staging timeouts', () => {
    const cases: unknown[] = [
      new Error('Menu bar popover height measurement timed out'),
      new Error('macOS native updater did not stage v1.0.72 within 120000ms'),
      new Error('Menu bar popover load timed out; extra context')
    ]

    for (const error of cases) {
      expect(isExpectedMenuBarPopoverLoadTimeout(error)).toBe(false)
      expect(shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError(error)).toBe(true)
    }
  })

  it('still reports HTTPS ERR_ABORTED when blume-menu:// appears only in the query', () => {
    const error = new Error(
      "ERR_ABORTED (-3) loading 'https://example.com/popover?next=blume-menu://open'"
    )

    expect(isExpectedMenuBarBlumeMenuLoadFailure(error)).toBe(false)
    expect(isExpectedMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure(error)).toBe(false)
    expect(shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError(error)).toBe(true)

    const captureAppError = vi.fn()
    reportMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure('main.menu-bar-popover', error, {
      captureAppError,
      logInfo: vi.fn()
    })
    expect(captureAppError).toHaveBeenCalledWith('main.menu-bar-popover', error)
  })

  it('still reports unrelated URL load failures and non-lifecycle exceptions', () => {
    const cases: unknown[] = [
      new Error("ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'https://example.com/popover'"),
      new Error("ERR_ABORTED (-3) loading 'https://example.com/popover'"),
      new Error('Object has been destroyed'),
      new Error('Unexpected height measurement failure'),
      new TypeError('Cannot read properties of null')
    ]

    for (const error of cases) {
      expect(isExpectedMenuBarDataUrlLoadFailure(error)).toBe(false)
      expect(isExpectedMenuBarBlumeMenuLoadFailure(error)).toBe(false)
      expect(isExpectedMenuBarPopoverLoadTimeout(error)).toBe(false)
      expect(shouldCaptureMenuBarPopoverLoadAppError(error)).toBe(true)

      const captureAppError = vi.fn()
      reportMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure('main.menu-bar-popover', error, {
        captureAppError,
        logInfo: vi.fn()
      })
      expect(captureAppError).toHaveBeenCalledWith('main.menu-bar-popover', error)
    }
  })

  it('routes update and click sources through the same capture gate', () => {
    const cases = [
      errFailedDataHtml('<html class="light"></html>'),
      errAbortedBlumeMenu('quit'),
      new Error(MENU_BAR_POPOVER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE)
    ]

    for (const error of cases) {
      for (const source of [
        'main.menu-bar-popover',
        'main.menu-bar-popover-preload',
        'main.menu-bar-popover-update'
      ] as const) {
        const captureAppError = vi.fn()
        reportMenuBarPopoverLoadFailure(source, error, {
          captureAppError,
          logInfo: vi.fn()
        })
        expect(captureAppError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
      }
    }
  })
})
