  test('classifies manual-recovery dialog presentation failures as non-fatal', async () => {
    const { isNonFatalUpdaterError } = await import('../../src/main/updater')

    expect(
      isNonFatalUpdaterError(
        new Error('The operation couldn\u2019t be completed. (OSStatus error -60006.)')
      )
    ).toBe(true)
    expect(isNonFatalUpdaterError(new Error('The request timed out.'))).toBe(true)
    expect(isNonFatalUpdaterError(new Error('Превышен лимит времени на запрос.'))).toBe(true)
    // Substring-only English timeout without the Apple dialog terminator stays fatal.
    expect(
      isNonFatalUpdaterError(
        new Error('The request timed out while contacting the update proxy')
      )
    ).toBe(false)
    // Keep unrelated timeout strings reportable unless they have their own marker.
    expect(isNonFatalUpdaterError(new Error('request timed out waiting for socket'))).toBe(false)
    expect(isNonFatalUpdaterError(new Error('operation timed out'))).toBe(false)
  })

  test('prompts for manual recovery when download fails with read-only volume during native staging', async () => {
    let rejectDownload: (err: Error) => void = () => undefined
    const downloadPromise = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
      rejectDownload = reject
    })
    downloadPromise.catch(() => undefined)
    mocks.checkForUpdates.mockResolvedValue({ downloadPromise })

    const updaterListeners = new Map<string, (...args: unknown[]) => void>()
    mocks.updaterOn.mockImplementation((event: string, listener: (...args: unknown[]) => void) => {
      updaterListeners.set(event, listener)
    })

    const { startAutoUpdates } = await import('../../src/main/updater')
    startAutoUpdates()
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)
    await Promise.resolve()
    await Promise.resolve()

    updaterListeners.get('update-downloaded')?.({ version: '1.2.3' })
    const readOnlyError = new Error(
      'Cannot update while running on a read-only volume. Please move the application and try again.'
    )
    mocks.logError.mockClear()
    mocks.captureAppError.mockClear()
    mocks.dialogShowMessageBox.mockClear()
    rejectDownload(readOnlyError)
    await Promise.resolve()
    await Promise.resolve()

    expect(mocks.logError).toHaveBeenCalledWith('download update failed', readOnlyError)
    expect(mocks.dialogShowMessageBox).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
    expect(mocks.dialogShowMessageBox).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ message: 'Blume could not prepare the downloaded update.' })
    )
    expect(mocks.captureAppError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })

  test('keeps signing failures reportable even when paired with staging-timeout wording', async () => {
    const { isNonFatalUpdaterError } = await import('../../src/main/updater')

    expect(
      isNonFatalUpdaterError(
        new Error(
          'macOS native updater did not stage v1.0.72 within 120000ms; New version is not signed'
        )
      )
    ).toBe(false)
    expect(
      isNonFatalUpdaterError(
        new Error(
          'macOS native updater did not stage v1.0.72 within 120000ms; net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID'
        )
      )
    ).toBe(false)
  })

  test('keeps signing failures reportable even when paired with read-only volume wording', async () => {
    const { isNonFatalUpdaterError } = await import('../../src/main/updater')

    expect(
      isNonFatalUpdaterError(
        new Error('Cannot update while running on a read-only volume; New version is not signed')
      )
    ).toBe(false)
    expect(
      isNonFatalUpdaterError(
        new Error(
          'Cannot update while running on a read-only volume; net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID'
        )
      )
    ).toBe(false)
    expect(

  test('keeps signing failures reportable even when paired with install-mismatch wording', async () => {

    expect(mocks.logError).toHaveBeenCalledWith('quitAndInstall failed', spawnEperm)
    expect(mocks.captureAppError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })

  test('does not capture Windows installer spawn EACCES as PostHog exceptions', async () => {
    setPlatform('win32')
    mocks.getAllWindows.mockReturnValue([])
    const spawnEacces = Object.assign(new Error('spawn EACCES'), {

<file path="__test/regressions/usage-connect.test.ts">
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events'
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from 'vitest'

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  homedir: vi.fn(() => '/Users/tester'),
  spawn: vi.fn(),
  openInTerminal: vi.fn()
}))

vi.mock('node:child_process', () => ({ spawn: mocks.spawn }))
vi.mock('node:os', () => ({ homedir: mocks.homedir }))
// connect.ts imports these from conversations/resume, which transitively pulls
// in electron and the DB layer. Stub the module so the unit stays isolated.
vi.mock('../../src/main/conversations/resume', () => ({
  openInTerminal: mocks.openInTerminal
}))

import { openKeychainAccess, openProviderLogin } from '../../src/main/usage/connect'
import { CLAUDE_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE } from '@blume/app-core'

/** A spawned child that reports success on the next tick, like a real `open`. */
function spawnedChild(): EventEmitter & { unref: () => void } {
  const child = Object.assign(new EventEmitter(), { unref: vi.fn() })
  process.nextTick(() => child.emit('spawn'))
  return child
}

const originalPlatform = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(process, 'platform')

function setPlatform(value: NodeJS.Platform): void {
  Object.defineProperty(process, 'platform', { value, configurable: true })
}

afterEach(() => {
  if (originalPlatform) Object.defineProperty(process, 'platform', originalPlatform)
  mocks.homedir.mockReset()
  mocks.homedir.mockReturnValue('/Users/tester')
  mocks.spawn.mockReset()
  mocks.openInTerminal.mockReset()
})

describe('usage connection helpers', () => {
  test('opens the Keychain Access app by bundle id on macOS', async () => {
    setPlatform('darwin')
    mocks.spawn.mockImplementation(() => spawnedChild())

    await openKeychainAccess()

    expect(mocks.spawn).toHaveBeenCalledWith('open', ['-b', 'com.apple.keychainaccess'], {
      detached: true,
      stdio: 'ignore'
    })
  })

  test('refuses to launch Keychain Access off macOS', async () => {
    setPlatform('linux')

    await expect(openKeychainAccess()).rejects.toThrow(/only available on macOS/)
    expect(mocks.spawn).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })

  test('Claude keychain service name stays in sync with the CLI', () => {
    expect(CLAUDE_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE).toBe('Claude Code-credentials')
  })

  test('terminal sign-in opens the embedded terminal with the projected command', async () => {
    await openProviderLogin('codex')

    expect(mocks.openInTerminal).toHaveBeenCalledWith('codex', '/Users/tester', 'codex login')
  })

  test('terminal sign-in no longer falls back to a native terminal app', async () => {
    await openProviderLogin('claude')

    expect(mocks.openInTerminal).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'claude',
      '/Users/tester',
      'claude auth login'
    )
  })

  test('terminal sign-in failure explains how to complete login manually', async () => {
    mocks.openInTerminal.mockRejectedValue(new Error('terminal worker exited'))

    await expect(openProviderLogin('claude')).rejects.toThrow(
      "Blume couldn't open its terminal. Run “claude auth login” in a terminal, then return to Blume and try again."
    )
  })

  test('terminal sign-in refuses providers without touching terminal adapters', async () => {
    await expect(openProviderLogin('cursor')).rejects.toThrow(
      'No terminal sign-in flow for provider: cursor'
    )
    await expect(
      openProviderLogin('unknown' as Parameters<typeof openProviderLogin>[0])
    ).rejects.toThrow('No terminal sign-in flow for provider: unknown')

    expect(mocks.homedir).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
    expect(mocks.openInTerminal).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })
})

<file path="__test/regressions/usage-parse.test.ts">
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest'
import {
  asEpochMs,
  decodeJwtClaims,
  normalizeCursorCookie,
  parseRetryAfterMs,
  parseClaudeCredentials,
  parseClaudeUsage,
  parseCodexAuth,
  parseCodexUsage,
  parseCursorUsage
} from '@blume/app-core'

const NOW = Date.parse('2026-06-10T12:00:00Z')

function fakeJwt(payload: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const body = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(payload)).toString('base64url')
  return `header.${body}.signature`
}

describe('usage parsing', () => {
  test('asEpochMs handles ISO strings, seconds, and ms', () => {
    expect(asEpochMs('2026-06-10T12:00:00Z')).toBe(NOW)
    expect(asEpochMs(NOW / 1000)).toBe(NOW)
    expect(asEpochMs(NOW)).toBe(NOW)
    expect(asEpochMs('not a date')).toBeNull()
    expect(asEpochMs(null)).toBeNull()
  })

  test('parseClaudeCredentials reads the claudeAiOauth wrapper', () => {
    const creds = parseClaudeCredentials({
      claudeAiOauth: {
        accessToken: 'sk-ant-oat-123',
        refreshToken: 'refresh-123',
        subscriptionType: 'max',
        expiresAt: NOW + 60_000,
        scopes: ['user:profile'],
        rateLimitTier: 'standard'
      }
    })
    expect(creds).toEqual({
      accessToken: 'sk-ant-oat-123',
      refreshToken: 'refresh-123',
      subscriptionType: 'max',
      expiresAt: NOW + 60_000,
      scopes: ['user:profile'],
      rateLimitTier: 'standard'
    })
    expect(parseClaudeCredentials({})).toBeNull()
    expect(parseClaudeCredentials(null)).toBeNull()
  })

  test('parseClaudeUsage maps five_hour/seven_day windows', () => {
    const { windows, costUsd } = parseClaudeUsage({
      five_hour: { utilization: 42, resets_at: '2026-06-10T14:00:00Z' },
      seven_day: { utilization: 18, resets_at: '2026-06-14T00:00:00Z' },
      seven_day_sonnet: null,
      seven_day_opus: { utilization: 7, resets_at: '2026-06-14T00:00:00Z' },
      extra_usage: { used_cents: 1250 }
    })
    expect(windows.map((w) => w.id)).toEqual(['session', 'weekly', 'weekly-opus'])
    expect(windows[0]).toMatchObject({
      label: 'Session (5h)',
      usedPercent: 42,
      resetsAt: Date.parse('2026-06-10T14:00:00Z')
    })
    expect(costUsd).toBe(12.5)
  })

  test('parseClaudeUsage tolerates unknown payloads', () => {
    expect(parseClaudeUsage(null)).toEqual({ windows: [], costUsd: null })
    expect(parseClaudeUsage({ five_hour: 'oops' }).windows).toEqual([])
  })

  test('parseCodexAuth extracts account id and plan from the id_token', () => {
    const auth = parseCodexAuth({
      tokens: {
        access_token: 'access-123',
        refresh_token: 'refresh-123',
        last_refresh: '2026-06-01T12:00:00Z',
        id_token: fakeJwt({
          email: 'demo@blume.page',
          'https://api.openai.com/auth': {
            chatgpt_account_id: 'acct-9',
            chatgpt_plan_type: 'plus'
          }
        })
      }
    })
    expect(auth).toEqual({
      accessToken: 'access-123',
      refreshToken: 'refresh-123',
      idToken: expect.any(String),
      lastRefreshAt: Date.parse('2026-06-01T12:00:00Z'),
      accountId: 'acct-9',
      plan: 'plus',
      email: 'demo@blume.page'
    })
    expect(parseCodexAuth({ tokens: {} })).toBeNull()
    expect(decodeJwtClaims('garbage')).toBeNull()
  })

  test('parseCodexUsage maps primary/secondary rate-limit windows', () => {
    const { windows, plan } = parseCodexUsage(
      {
        plan_type: 'plus',
        rate_limit: {
          primary_window: {
            used_percent: 88,
            limit_window_seconds: 18_000,
            resets_in_seconds: 3_600
          },
          secondary_window: {
            used_percent: 51,
            window_minutes: 10_080,
            resets_at: NOW / 1000 + 172_800
          }
        }
      },
      NOW
    )
    expect(windows).toHaveLength(2)
    expect(windows[0]).toMatchObject({
      id: 'session',
      label: 'Session (5h)',
      usedPercent: 88,
      resetsAt: NOW + 3_600_000
    })
    expect(windows[1]).toMatchObject({ id: 'weekly', label: 'Weekly', usedPercent: 51 })
    expect(plan).toBe('plus')
  })

  test('parseCursorUsage reads the individualUsage summary shape', () => {
    // Trimmed real /api/usage-summary response (2026-06).
    const { windows, plan, account, costUsd } = parseCursorUsage(
      {
        summary: {
          billingCycleStart: '2026-05-25T00:05:29.000Z',
          billingCycleEnd: '2026-06-25T00:05:29.000Z',
          membershipType: 'pro_plus',
          limitType: 'user',
          isUnlimited: false,
          individualUsage: {
            plan: {
              enabled: true,
              used: 7000,
              limit: 7000,
              remaining: 0,
              breakdown: { included: 7000, bonus: 5989, total: 12989 },
              autoPercentUsed: 4.835,
              apiPercentUsed: 100,
              totalPercentUsed: 25.468627450980392
            },
            onDemand: { enabled: true, used: 4511, limit: 20000, remaining: 15489 }
          },
          teamUsage: {}
        },
        legacy: {
          'gpt-4': { numRequests: 0, maxRequestUsage: null },
          startOfMonth: '2026-05-25T00:05:29.000Z'
        },
        me: { email: 'demo@blume.page' }
      },
      NOW
    )
    expect(plan).toBe('Pro+')
    expect(account).toBe('demo@blume.page')
    expect(costUsd).toBe(45.11)
    const cycleEnd = Date.parse('2026-06-25T00:05:29.000Z')
    expect(windows).toEqual([
      { id: 'plan', label: 'Included usage', usedPercent: 25.468627450980392, resetsAt: cycleEnd },
      { id: 'api', label: 'Named models (API)', usedPercent: 100, resetsAt: cycleEnd },
      {
        id: 'on-demand',
        label: 'On-demand ($45.11 / $200.00)',
        usedPercent: 22.555,
        resetsAt: cycleEnd
      }
    ])
  })

  test('parseCursorUsage falls back to the legacy request counter', () => {
    const { windows, plan, costUsd } = parseCursorUsage(
      {
        summary: { membershipType: 'pro', onDemandSpendCents: 340 },
        legacy: {
          'gpt-4': { numRequests: 120, maxRequestUsage: 500 },
          startOfMonth: '2026-06-01T00:00:00Z'
        },
        me: { email: 'demo@blume.page' }
      },
      NOW
    )
    expect(plan).toBe('Pro')
    expect(costUsd).toBe(3.4)
    const requests = windows.find((w) => w.id === 'requests')
    expect(requests).toMatchObject({ usedPercent: 24 })
    expect(requests?.resetsAt).toBe(Date.parse('2026-07-01T00:00:00Z'))
  })

  test('parseRetryAfterMs handles delta-seconds, HTTP-dates, and garbage', () => {
    expect(parseRetryAfterMs('120', NOW)).toBe(120_000)
    expect(parseRetryAfterMs(' 0 ', NOW)).toBe(0)
    expect(parseRetryAfterMs('Wed, 10 Jun 2026 12:05:00 GMT', NOW)).toBe(300_000)
    // Dates in the past clamp to zero instead of going negative.
    expect(parseRetryAfterMs('Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:00:00 GMT', NOW)).toBe(0)
    expect(parseRetryAfterMs('soon', NOW)).toBeNull()
    expect(parseRetryAfterMs(null, NOW)).toBeNull()
  })

  test('normalizeCursorCookie accepts bare tokens and full cookie strings', () => {
    expect(normalizeCursorCookie('abc123')).toBe('WorkosCursorSessionToken=abc123')
    expect(normalizeCursorCookie('WorkosCursorSessionToken=abc123')).toBe(
      'WorkosCursorSessionToken=abc123'
    )
    expect(normalizeCursorCookie('abc123==')).toBe('WorkosCursorSessionToken=abc123==')
    expect(normalizeCursorCookie('other=1; WorkosCursorSessionToken=abc123')).toBe(
      'other=1; WorkosCursorSessionToken=abc123'
    )
    expect(normalizeCursorCookie('   ')).toBeNull()
  })
})

const originalPlatformDescriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(process, 'platform')
const originalCodexHome = process.env.CODEX_HOME

function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  return {
    ok: status >= 200 && status < 300,
    status,
    headers: new Headers(),
    json: async () => body
  } as Response
}

function fakeJwt(payload: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const body = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(payload)).toString('base64url')
  return `header.${body}.signature`
}

function execFileResult(stdout: string): { stdout: string; stderr: string } {
  return { stdout, stderr: '' }
}

describe('Claude usage credentials', () => {

import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from 'vitest'
import type { ProviderUsageSnapshot, UsageReport } from '@blume/app-core'

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  captureTelemetryEvent: vi.fn(async () => true),
  settings: new Map<string, string>()
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/settingsStore', () => ({
  getSetting: vi.fn((key: string) => mocks.settings.get(key) ?? null),
  setSetting: vi.fn((key: string, value: string) => {
    mocks.settings.set(key, value)
  }),
  initializeSettingsStore: vi.fn(async () => undefined)
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/telemetry', () => ({
  captureTelemetryEvent: mocks.captureTelemetryEvent
}))

vi.mock('../../src/main/secureStore', () => ({
  clearSecret: vi.fn(),
  getSecret: vi.fn(() => null),
  setSecret: vi.fn()
}))

import {
  resetUsageSetupTelemetryForTests,
  trackUsageSetupTelemetry
} from '../../src/main/usage/providerUsage'

const originalPlatform = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(process, 'platform')

function setPlatform(value: NodeJS.Platform): void {
  Object.defineProperty(process, 'platform', { value, configurable: true })
}

function snapshot(
  provider: ProviderUsageSnapshot['provider'],
  status: ProviderUsageSnapshot['status'],
  cta: ProviderUsageSnapshot['cta'] = null
): ProviderUsageSnapshot {
  return {
    provider,
    status,
    account: null,
    plan: provider === 'claude' && status === 'ok' ? 'max' : null,
    windows:
      status === 'ok' ? [{ id: 'session', label: 'Session', usedPercent: 10, resetsAt: null }] : [],
    costUsd: null,
    detail: status === 'ok' ? null : 'Setup needed',
    cta
  }
}

function report(providers: ProviderUsageSnapshot[]): UsageReport {
  return { providers, fetchedAt: Date.now() }
}

function captured(event: string): Record<string, unknown>[] {
  return mocks.captureTelemetryEvent.mock.calls
    .filter(([name]) => name === event)
    .map(([, properties]) => properties as Record<string, unknown>)
}

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.useFakeTimers()
  vi.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-06-22T10:00:00Z'))
  mocks.captureTelemetryEvent.mockClear()
  mocks.settings.clear()
  resetUsageSetupTelemetryForTests()
  setPlatform('darwin')
})

afterEach(() => {
  vi.useRealTimers()
  if (originalPlatform) Object.defineProperty(process, 'platform', originalPlatform)
})

describe('usage setup telemetry', () => {
  test('classifies first successful usage as immediate setup', () => {
    trackUsageSetupTelemetry(report([snapshot('claude', 'ok')]), false)
    trackUsageSetupTelemetry(report([snapshot('claude', 'ok')]), false)

    const successes = captured('usage_provider_setup_succeeded')
    expect(successes).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(successes[0]).toMatchObject({
      harness: 'claude',
      provider: 'claude',
      os_platform: 'darwin',
      setup_state: 'usage',
      setup_path: 'immediate',
      first_observed_state: 'usage',
      seen_login_state: false,
      seen_keychain_issue_state: false,
      has_usage_windows: true,
      usage_window_count: 1
    })
  })

  test('classifies login state followed by usage as login_then_usage across restarts', () => {
    trackUsageSetupTelemetry(
      report([snapshot('claude', 'unauthenticated', 'terminal-login')]),
      false
    )
    resetUsageSetupTelemetryForTests()
    vi.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-06-22T10:05:00Z'))

    trackUsageSetupTelemetry(report([snapshot('claude', 'ok')]), true)

    const successes = captured('usage_provider_setup_succeeded')
    expect(successes).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(successes[0]).toMatchObject({
      harness: 'claude',
      setup_path: 'login_then_usage',
      first_observed_state: 'login',
      seen_login_state: true,
      seen_keychain_issue_state: false,
      force_fetch: true,
      success_elapsed_ms: 5 * 60_000
    })
  })

  test('classifies Claude keychain issue followed by usage as keychain_then_usage', () => {
    trackUsageSetupTelemetry(report([snapshot('claude', 'error', 'claude-keychain-access')]), false)
    vi.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-06-22T10:03:00Z'))

    trackUsageSetupTelemetry(report([snapshot('claude', 'ok')]), true)

    const states = captured('usage_provider_setup_state_observed')
    expect(states.map((state) => state.setup_state)).toEqual(['keychain_issue', 'usage'])

    const successes = captured('usage_provider_setup_succeeded')
    expect(successes).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(successes[0]).toMatchObject({
      harness: 'claude',
      setup_path: 'keychain_then_usage',
      first_observed_state: 'keychain_issue',
      seen_login_state: false,
      seen_keychain_issue_state: true,
      success_elapsed_ms: 3 * 60_000
    })
  })
})

<file path="__test/regressions/windows-paths.test.ts">
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest'

import {
  basenameIfPath,
  condenseHomePaths,
  describeProjectPath,
  normalizePathSeparators as normalizeSeparators,
  pathLeaf as pathBasename
} from '@blume/app-core'

describe('Windows path handling', () => {
  test('normalizeSeparators flips backslashes and keeps drive letters', () => {
    expect(normalizeSeparators('C:\\Users\\me\\proj')).toBe('C:/Users/me/proj')
    expect(normalizeSeparators('/Users/me/proj')).toBe('/Users/me/proj')
  })

  test('pathBasename handles both separators', () => {
    expect(pathBasename('C:\\Users\\me\\sessions\\abc.jsonl')).toBe('abc.jsonl')
    expect(pathBasename('/Users/me/sessions/abc.jsonl')).toBe('abc.jsonl')
  })

  test('describeProjectPath parses a plain Windows cwd', () => {
    const info = describeProjectPath('C:\\Users\\me\\dev\\my-app')
    expect(info.project).toBe('my-app')
    expect(info.projectRoot).toBe('C:/Users/me/dev/my-app')
    expect(info.display).toBe('my-app')
  })

  test('describeProjectPath parses a Windows tooling worktree', () => {
    const info = describeProjectPath('C:\\Users\\me\\dev\\my-app\\.claude\\worktrees\\bold-fox')
    expect(info.project).toBe('my-app')
    expect(info.projectRoot).toBe('C:/Users/me/dev/my-app')
    expect(info.worktree).toBe('bold-fox')
    expect(info.display).toBe('my-app · bold-fox')
  })

  test('describeProjectPath keeps Codex global worktree identity on Windows', () => {
    const first = describeProjectPath('C:\\Users\\me\\.codex\\worktrees\\011f\\my-app')
    const second = describeProjectPath('C:\\Users\\me\\.codex\\worktrees\\055e\\my-app')
    expect(first.projectRoot).toBe('C:/Users/me/.codex/projects/my-app')
    expect(second.projectRoot).toBe(first.projectRoot)
    expect(first.worktree).toBe('011f')
  })

  test('describeProjectPath preserves UNC roots', () => {
    const info = describeProjectPath('\\\\server\\share\\my-app\\.claude\\worktrees\\bold-fox')
    expect(info.project).toBe('my-app')
    expect(info.projectRoot).toBe('//server/share/my-app')
    expect(info.worktree).toBe('bold-fox')
  })

  test('POSIX paths keep their existing identity values', () => {
    const info = describeProjectPath('/Users/me/dev/my-app/.claude/worktrees/bold-fox')
    expect(info.projectRoot).toBe('/Users/me/dev/my-app')
    expect(info.display).toBe('my-app · bold-fox')
  })

  test('basenameIfPath strips Windows paths', () => {
    expect(basenameIfPath('C:\\Users\\me\\dev\\file.ts')).toBe('file.ts')
  })

  test('condenseHomePaths condenses Windows home paths', () => {
    expect(condenseHomePaths('cat C:\\Users\\me\\dev\\file.ts && pnpm build')).toBe(
      'cat file.ts && pnpm build'
    )
    expect(condenseHomePaths('cat /Users/olav/prosjekt/foo/bar.ts && pnpm build')).toBe(
      'cat bar.ts && pnpm build'
    )
  })
})

  test('resolves the current checkout without falling through to shared node_modules', async () => {
    const fixtureRoot = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'blume-workspace-loader-'))
    tempDirectories.push(fixtureRoot)
    const checkoutRoot = join(fixtureRoot, 'checkout')
    const packageRoot = join(checkoutRoot, 'packages', 'example')
    const currentEntry = join(packageRoot, 'src', 'index.ts')
    writeJson(join(packageRoot, 'package.json'), {
      name: '@blume/example',
      exports: { '.': './src/index.ts' }
    })
    mkdirSync(dirname(currentEntry), { recursive: true })
    writeFileSync(currentEntry, 'export const source = "current"\n')

    const sharedNodeModules = join(fixtureRoot, 'shared-node-modules')
    const stalePackage = join(sharedNodeModules, '@blume', 'example')
    const staleEntry = join(stalePackage, 'stale.ts')
    writeJson(join(stalePackage, 'package.json'), {
      name: '@blume/example',
      exports: { '.': './index.ts', './stale': './stale.ts' }
    })
    writeFileSync(staleEntry, 'export const source = "stale"\n')
    mkdirSync(checkoutRoot, { recursive: true })
    const nodeModulesLink = join(checkoutRoot, 'node_modules')
    symlinkSync(sharedNodeModules, nodeModulesLink, 'dir')

    const packages = findWorkspacePackages([join(checkoutRoot, 'packages')])
    const resolve = createWorkspacePackageResolve(packages)
    const nextResolve = vi.fn(async () => ({ url: pathToFileURL(staleEntry).href }))

    const result = await resolve('@blume/example', { conditions: ['node', 'import'] }, nextResolve)
    expect(fileURLToPath(result.url)).toBe(currentEntry)
    await expect(
      resolve('@blume/example/stale', { conditions: ['node', 'import'] }, nextResolve)
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({
      code: 'ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED',
      packageName: '@blume/example',
      subpath: './stale'
    })
    expect(nextResolve).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
    expect(readlinkSync(nodeModulesLink)).toBe(sharedNodeModules)

    await expect(
      resolve('@blume/not-in-this-checkout', { conditions: ['node', 'import'] }, nextResolve)
    ).resolves.toEqual({ url: pathToFileURL(staleEntry).href })
    expect(nextResolve).toHaveBeenCalledOnce()
  })

  test('local link repair refuses a shared node_modules symlink', () => {
    const fixtureRoot = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'blume-workspace-links-'))
    tempDirectories.push(fixtureRoot)
    const sharedNodeModules = join(fixtureRoot, 'shared-node-modules')
    const nodeModulesLink = join(fixtureRoot, 'checkout', 'node_modules')
    mkdirSync(sharedNodeModules, { recursive: true })
    mkdirSync(dirname(nodeModulesLink), { recursive: true })
    symlinkSync(sharedNodeModules, nodeModulesLink, 'dir')

    expect(() => assertSafeNodeModules(nodeModulesLink)).toThrow(
      /Refusing to rewrite shared node_modules/
    )
    expect(readlinkSync(nodeModulesLink)).toBe(sharedNodeModules)
  })

  test('local link repair refuses a symlinked workspace package scope', () => {
    const fixtureRoot = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'blume-workspace-scope-'))
    tempDirectories.push(fixtureRoot)
    const nodeModules = join(fixtureRoot, 'checkout', 'node_modules')
    const sharedScope = join(fixtureRoot, 'shared-node-modules', '@blume')
    const stalePackage = join(sharedScope, 'example')
    const marker = join(stalePackage, 'keep.txt')
    const currentPackage = join(fixtureRoot, 'checkout', 'packages', 'example')
    mkdirSync(stalePackage, { recursive: true })
    mkdirSync(currentPackage, { recursive: true })
    writeFileSync(marker, 'must remain untouched\n')
    mkdirSync(nodeModules, { recursive: true })
    const scopeLink = join(nodeModules, '@blume')
    symlinkSync(sharedScope, scopeLink, 'dir')

    expect(() =>
      replaceWorkspacePackageLink(nodeModules, join(scopeLink, 'example'), currentPackage)
    ).toThrow(/Refusing to rewrite workspace package through symlinked parent/)
    expect(readlinkSync(scopeLink)).toBe(sharedScope)
    expect(readFileSync(marker, 'utf8')).toBe('must remain untouched\n')
  })
})

<file path="__test/regressions/wrapped-generate-worker-error-policy.test.ts">
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'

import {
  WRAPPED_GENERATE_WORKER_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_MESSAGE,
  WRAPPED_GENERATE_WORKER_DISPOSED_MESSAGE,
  WRAPPED_GENERATE_WORKER_UNRESPONSIVE_MESSAGE,
  WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError,
  isExpectedWrappedGenerateWorkerOperationalError,
  isWrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError,
  shouldReportWrappedGenerateAppError
} from '../../src/main/wrapped/generateHost'

describe('wrapped generate worker operational error policy', () => {
  it('classifies unresponsive, dispose, and circuit-breaker as expected', () => {
    const errors = [
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError(WRAPPED_GENERATE_WORKER_UNRESPONSIVE_MESSAGE),
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError(WRAPPED_GENERATE_WORKER_DISPOSED_MESSAGE),
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError(WRAPPED_GENERATE_WORKER_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_MESSAGE)
    ]

    for (const error of errors) {
      expect(isWrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError(error)).toBe(true)
      expect(isExpectedWrappedGenerateWorkerOperationalError(error)).toBe(true)
      expect(shouldReportWrappedGenerateAppError(error)).toBe(false)
    }
  })

  it('still reports unexpected worker infrastructure failures', () => {
    const errors = [
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError('wrapped generate worker exited'),
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError('failed to message wrapped generate worker'),
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError('failed to cancel wrapped worker request'),
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError('failed to spawn wrapped generate worker'),
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError('wrapped generate worker unavailable'),
      new WrappedGenerateWorkerUnavailableError('wrapped generate worker disabled'),
      new Error(WRAPPED_GENERATE_WORKER_UNRESPONSIVE_MESSAGE)
    ]

    for (const error of errors) {
      expect(isExpectedWrappedGenerateWorkerOperationalError(error)).toBe(false)
      expect(shouldReportWrappedGenerateAppError(error)).toBe(true)
    }
  })
})

handle('control:plugin', (op, input) => {
  if (op === 'devBuild') return { status: 'release' }
  if (op === 'status') return pluginStatuses
  if (op === 'agents') return []
  if (op === 'install') {
    const harnesses = input?.harnesses
    if (
      !Array.isArray(harnesses) ||
      !harnesses.length ||
      harnesses.some(
        (harness) => !pluginStatuses.some((agent) => agent.harness === harness && agent.available)
      )
    )
      return unexpected('plugin:install:invalid-harness')
    global.releaseCheckInstalls.push([...harnesses])
    // Simulate only the native result; no key, file, agent or network is touched.
    return harnesses.map((harness) => {
      const agent = pluginStatuses.find((entry) => entry.harness === harness)
      agent.installed = true
      agent.version = agent.latest
      return { harness, ok: true, version: agent.version }
    })
  }
  return unexpected(`plugin:${op}`)
})
handle('control:request', (op, input) => {
  if (op === 'workspace') return { kind: 'personal', id: '0' }
  if (op !== 'call' || !reads.has(input.operation))
    return unexpected(`ledger:${op}:${input?.operation}`)
  if (input.operation === 'plugin_installations')
    return {
      scope: 'local',
      checkedAt: Date.now(),
      installations: [],
      note: 'Isolated release check'
    }
  if (input.operation === 'context') return { viewerId: account.user.id, capabilities: {} }
  return { items: [], more: false, offset: 0 }
})
ipcMain.on('control:feed', (event) => {
  const { port1, port2 } = new MessageChannelMain()

    if (data.op !== 'changes') return

      'scenarios',
      'suites',
      'acceptanceSets',
      'executions',
      'removed'
    ])
      result[key] = []
    port1.postMessage({ id: data.id, result })
  })
  port1.start()
  event.sender.postMessage('control:feed', null, [port2])
  event.sender.once('destroyed', () => port1.close())
})

const { test: base, expect, _electron: electron } = require('@playwright/test')
const { access, mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } = require('node:fs/promises')
const { tmpdir } = require('node:os')
const path = require('node:path')

// Capture the Electron content surface directly. Chromium's screenshot command can
// stall after a view closes; this also works when another app has focus.
async function captureElectron(app, file) {
  const png = await app.evaluate(async ({ BrowserWindow }) => {
    const image = await BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()[0].webContents.capturePage(undefined, {
      stayHidden: true,
      stayAwake: true
    })
    return image.toPNG().toString('base64')
  })
  await writeFile(file, Buffer.from(png, 'base64'))
}

const test = base.extend({
  agentsAvailable: [true, { option: true }],
  app: async ({ agentsAvailable }, use, info) => {
    const profile = await mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), 'blume-onboarding-release-'))
    let app
    const logs = []
    try {
      const env = {
        ...process.env,
        BLUME_ONBOARDING_PROFILE: profile,
        BLUME_ONBOARDING_AGENTS: agentsAvailable ? 'available' : 'unavailable',
        BLUME_ONBOARDING_OUT: path.resolve(process.env.BLUME_ONBOARDING_OUT || 'out')
      }
      await access(path.join(env.BLUME_ONBOARDING_OUT, 'renderer/index.html'))
      await access(path.join(env.BLUME_ONBOARDING_OUT, 'preload/index.js'))
      delete env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE
      app = await electron.launch({ args: [path.join(__dirname, 'host.cjs')], env, timeout: 30000 })
      app.process().stderr.on('data', (data) => logs.push(String(data)))
      await use(app)
      expect(
        logs.join(''),
        'The native fixture must cover every requested IPC channel'
      ).not.toContain('No handler registered')
    } finally {
      if (app) {
        await writeFile(info.outputPath('electron.log'), logs.join(''))
        await info.attach('Electron log', {
          path: info.outputPath('electron.log'),
          contentType: 'text/plain'
        })
        await app.close()
      }
      await rm(profile, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5 })
    }
  },
  page: async ({ app }, use, info) => {
    const page = await app.firstWindow()
    const errors = []
    page.on('console', (message) => {
      if (message.type() === 'error') console.log('Renderer:', message.text())
    })
    page.on('pageerror', (error) => errors.push(error.message))
    await app.context().tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true })
    try {
      await use(page)
      expect(errors, 'Renderer errors').toEqual([])
      expect(
        await app.evaluate(() => global.releaseCheckUnexpected),
        'Demo must not mutate the customer host'
      ).toEqual([])
    } finally {
      await captureElectron(app, info.outputPath('electron.png')).catch(() => {})
      await info
        .attach('Electron screenshot', {
          path: info.outputPath('electron.png'),
          contentType: 'image/png'
        })
        .catch(() => {})
      await app.context().tracing.stop({ path: info.outputPath('trace.zip') })
    }
  }
})

test('release: actual onboarding journey, reload and clear', async ({ page, app }, info) => {
  const guide = page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Guided walkthrough' })
  const highlighted = async (target) => {
    await expect
      .poll(
        async () => {
          const ring = await page.locator('[data-guided-overlay] > [aria-hidden]').boundingBox()
          const box = await target.boundingBox()
          return Boolean(
            ring &&
            box &&
            ['x', 'y', 'width', 'height'].every((key) => Math.abs(ring[key] - box[key]) < 3)
          )
        },
        { message: 'Guide must highlight the actual next control' }
      )
      .toBe(true)
  }
  const click = async (name) => {
    // Approve is the bar's: the Decision part repeats it at the document's foot.
    // The guide's own action repeats the control it points at; press the page's control.
    const button = String(name).startsWith('/^Approve')
      ? page.locator('button[data-decision-entry][data-approve]')
      : page
          .getByRole('button', { name, exact: typeof name === 'string' })
          .and(page.locator(':not([data-arrow-popover] *)'))
    if (name === 'Mark reviewed' || name === 'Send answer' || String(name).startsWith('/^Approve'))
      await highlighted(button)
    await button.click()
  }
  const captures = []
  let currentStage = 'Start'
  const shot = async (name) => {
    // Let the coachmark's geometry observer catch up with native page motion.
    await page.waitForTimeout(350)
    const title = `${String(captures.length + 1).padStart(2, '0')} · ${name}`
    const file = info.outputPath(`${title.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gi, '-').toLowerCase()}.png`)
    await captureElectron(app, file)
    await info.attach(title, { path: file, contentType: 'image/png' })
    captures.push({ title, file })
    await writeFile(info.outputPath('flow.json'), JSON.stringify(captures, null, 2))
  }
  const invoiceRow = page
    .locator('[data-list-item]')
    .filter({ hasText: 'Example · Export invoices as PDF' })
  const stage = async (n, phase, list = false) => {
    currentStage = phase
    console.log(`Checking stop ${n}: ${phase}`)
    await expect(guide).toContainText(`${n} of 4`)
    if (list) {
      // The walkthrough shows the deliveries as a list, never the phase board.
      await expect(invoiceRow).toContainText(phase)
      await expect(page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Deliveries by phase' })).toHaveCount(0)
    } else {
      await expect(page.getByRole('region', { name: 'The delivery', exact: true })).toBeVisible()
      await expect(page).toHaveURL(/delivery=onboarding-example-invoice/)
    }
    await shot(`${currentStage} ${list ? 'list' : 'delivery'}`)
  }
  const layouts = async (label) => {
    for (const width of [360, 430, 900, 1440]) {
      await app.evaluate(
        ({ BrowserWindow }, width) => BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()[0].setContentSize(width, 900),
        width
      )
      await expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => innerWidth)).toBe(width)
      await expect
        .poll(async () => {
          const box = await guide.boundingBox()
          return Boolean(
            box &&
            box.x >= 0 &&
            box.y >= 0 &&
            box.x + box.width <= width + 1 &&
            box.y + box.height <= 901
          )
        })
        .toBe(true)
      if (label.startsWith('Outcome brief') || label === 'Outcome all evidence') {
        // The bar's Approve stays on screen; the Decision part repeats it at the document's foot.
        const approve = page.locator('button[data-decision-entry][data-approve]')
        await expect
          .poll(
            async () => {
              const box = await approve.boundingBox()
              return Boolean(box && box.x >= 0 && box.x + box.width <= width + 1)
            },
            { message: 'Approval must stay fully inside the window' }
          )
          .toBe(true)
        if (width < 640) {
          // In verification the guide collapses; More shows its points, Less folds them.
          const more = guide.getByRole('button', { name: 'More', exact: true })
          await expect(more).toBeVisible()
          await expect(guide).not.toContainText('Inspect the evidence')
          await more.click()
          await expect(guide).toContainText('Inspect the evidence')
          await guide.getByRole('button', { name: 'Less', exact: true }).click()
          await expect(guide).not.toContainText('Inspect the evidence')
        }
      }
      await shot(`${label} at ${width}px`)
    }
  }
  await expect(guide).toBeVisible()
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => Boolean(window.api && window.blumeControl))).toBe(true)
  await stage(1, 'Start', true)
  await test.step('phases, who acts and the guide on the invoice row', async () => {
    for (const phase of ['Start', 'Plan', 'Build', 'Test', 'Review', 'Release', 'Done'])
      await expect(guide).toContainText(phase)
    await expect(guide).toContainText('Your agent does the work; you make the calls')
    await expect(guide).toContainText('You approve outcome, then merge')
    await expect(guide).toContainText('Your approval, or live on merge')
    await expect(guide.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open example', exact: true })).toBeVisible()
    await layouts('Phase overview')
    // Next goes to where the example needs you: its outcome review.
    await guide.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next', exact: true }).click()
    await stage(2, 'Review')
    await expect(guide).toContainText('The agent brings the result, its proof and its limits')
  })
  await test.step('active outcome review survives reload', async () => {
    const review = page
      .getByRole('group', { name: 'Outcome review', exact: true })
      .getByRole('button', { name: 'Review', exact: true })
    await highlighted(review)
    await review.click()
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Your invoice, ready to send.', exact: true })
    ).toBeVisible()
    const reviewUrl = page.url()
    await page.reload()
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(reviewUrl)
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Your invoice, ready to send.', exact: true })
    ).toBeVisible()
    await expect(guide).toContainText('open the invoice evidence')
    await layouts('Outcome brief cover')
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next in the brief', exact: true }).click()
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Every line item makes it into the PDF.', exact: true })
    ).toBeVisible()
    await layouts('Outcome brief matching details')
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next in the brief', exact: true }).click()
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', {
        name: 'One invoice checked. The edge cases still need proof.',
        exact: true
      })
    ).toBeVisible()
    await layouts('Outcome brief limits')
    // Resizing reflows the document and the page follows the reading, so go by the contents.
    await page
      .getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Contents', exact: true })
      .getByRole('button', { name: /All the evidence/ })
      .click()
    await expect(page.getByRole('main', { name: 'All the evidence', exact: true })).toBeVisible()
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Every line item makes it into the PDF.', exact: true })
    ).toContainText('Both line items and the $320.00 total match')
    await layouts('Outcome all evidence')
    // macOS CI can constrain the content height to 656px. Follow the guide's
    // persistent evidence tab: scrolling an offscreen card into view can move
    // the guide over the click while the active document part changes.
    await app.evaluate(({ BrowserWindow }) =>
      BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()[0].setContentSize(1440, 656)
    )
    await expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => innerHeight)).toBe(656)
    const evidenceTab = page
      .locator('nav[aria-label="This part and its evidence"] [data-evidence-row] button')
      .first()
    await highlighted(evidenceTab)
    await evidenceTab.click()
    await expect(
      page
        .getByRole('button', { name: 'Mark reviewed', exact: true })
        .and(page.locator(':not([data-arrow-popover] *)'))
    ).toBeVisible()
    const evidence = page.locator('[data-walkthrough-surface]')
    await expect(evidence).toContainText('Compare the invoice with the downloaded PDF')
    await expect(evidence).toContainText('INV-1042')
    await expect(evidence).toContainText('$320.00')
    await expect(evidence).toContainText('not a real browser test')
    await expect(evidence).not.toContainText('Not reported')
    await expect(evidence).toContainText('ask the agent for those checks before approving')
    await layouts('Outcome evidence')
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Switch to dark theme', exact: true }).click()
    await expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'dark')
    await expect(page.locator('html')).not.toHaveAttribute('data-theme-wave', '')
    await layouts('Dark outcome evidence')
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Switch to light theme', exact: true }).click()
    await expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'light')
    await expect(page.locator('html')).not.toHaveAttribute('data-theme-wave', '')
    await click('Mark reviewed')
    await shot('Outcome reviewed and ready to approve')
    await click(/^Approve/)
    await stage(3, 'Release')
  })
  await test.step('direct review to deployment flow and completion', async () => {
    await expect(guide).toContainText('goes out the way your workspace is set up')
    await expect(guide).toContainText('goes live on merge')
    await expect(guide).toContainText('set it up with the Blume plugin')
    await expect(page.getByRole('region', { name: 'The delivery', exact: true })).toContainText(
      'Production'
    )

    await guide.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next', exact: true }).click()
    await expect(guide).toContainText('4 of 4')
    await expect(guide).toContainText('The invoice delivery went from Start to Done')
    await shot('Done')
    await guide.getByRole('button', { name: 'Finish onboarding', exact: true }).click()
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Welcome to Blume', exact: true })).toBeVisible()
    await shot('Welcome after completing onboarding')
  })
  await test.step('completion persists without a replay banner', async () => {
    await expect(guide).toHaveCount(0)

    await page.reload()
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('button', { name: /^(Resume|Try) example deliveries$/ })
    ).toHaveCount(0)
    await expect(guide).toHaveCount(0)
    await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toHaveCount(0)
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Welcome to Blume', exact: true })).toBeVisible()
    await shot('Welcome persists after reload')
  })

// Smoke test for the shared install host with desktop native ports. Points HOME
// at a tempdir, runs the installer twice (first to install, second to confirm
// the marker short-circuits), and asserts the side effects.
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, existsSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { cp, mkdir, readFile, rename, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { homedir, tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { createInstallHost } from '@blume/app-core'
import { is } from '@electron-toolkit/utils'
import { app } from 'electron'

const DESKTOP_ROOT = dirname(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)))
process.chdir(DESKTOP_ROOT)

const FAKE_HOME = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'blume-install-test-'))
process.env.HOME = FAKE_HOME

// Seed an existing ~/.claude/settings.json with an unrelated user setting,
// so we can verify the merge preserves it.
const claudeDir = join(FAKE_HOME, '.claude')
mkdirSync(claudeDir, { recursive: true })
const seedSettings = {
  permissions: { allow: ['Bash(ls)'] },
  hooks: {
    UserPromptSubmit: [
      { hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: 'echo pre-existing-user-hook' }] },
      { hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: 'node ~/.blume/hooks/inject-rules.mjs' }] }
    ]
  }
}
writeFileSync(join(claudeDir, 'settings.json'), JSON.stringify(seedSettings, null, 2))
mkdirSync(join(FAKE_HOME, '.blume', 'rules'), { recursive: true })
mkdirSync(join(FAKE_HOME, '.blume', 'hooks'), { recursive: true })
mkdirSync(join(FAKE_HOME, '.cursor', 'rules'), { recursive: true })
writeFileSync(join(FAKE_HOME, '.blume', 'rules', 'todo-list.md'), 'todo list')
writeFileSync(join(FAKE_HOME, '.blume', 'hooks', 'inject-rules.mjs'), 'legacy hook')
writeFileSync(join(FAKE_HOME, '.cursor', 'rules', 'blume-todo-list.mdc'), 'legacy rule')

console.log('[test] HOME =', FAKE_HOME)

const { getBlumeRoot } = await import('../src/main/blume-home.ts')
const installHost = createInstallHost({
  currentAppVersion: () => app.getVersion(),
  appPath: () => app.getAppPath(),
  resourcesPath: () => process.resourcesPath,
  isDev: is.dev,
  blumeHome: getBlumeRoot,
  homeDir: homedir,
  platform: () => process.platform,
  pid: () => process.pid,
  fs: {
    copy: (src, dest, options) => cp(src, dest, options),
    async mkdir(path, options) {
      await mkdir(path, options)
    },
    readTextFile: (path) => readFile(path, 'utf-8'),
    writeTextFile: (path, contents) => writeFile(path, contents, 'utf-8'),
    rename,
    removeFile: (path) => rm(path, { force: true })
  },
  path: { dirname, join },
  now: () => new Date()
})
const blumeHome = getBlumeRoot()
assert.ok(
  blumeHome.startsWith(join(FAKE_HOME, '.blume')),
  'install should write inside the fake HOME .blume tree'
)

// --- first run: should do work
const first = await installHost.runInstall()
console.log('[test] first run state:', JSON.stringify(first, null, 2))

// Marker file written
const markerPath = join(blumeHome, 'install-state.json')
assert.ok(existsSync(markerPath), 'install-state.json should exist')
const marker = JSON.parse(readFileSync(markerPath, 'utf-8'))
assert.equal(marker.appVersion, '1.0.10-test')
assert.equal(marker.harnesses.claude.status, 'skipped')
assert.equal(marker.harnesses.cursor.status, 'skipped')
assert.equal(marker.harnesses.codex.status, 'skipped')
assert.equal(marker.migrations['remove-todo-list-integration'].status, 'ok')

// Legacy global integrations removed
const hookPath = join(blumeHome, 'hooks', 'inject-rules.mjs')
const rulePath = join(blumeHome, 'rules', 'todo-list.md')
const cursorRule = join(FAKE_HOME, '.cursor', 'rules', 'blume-todo-list.mdc')
assert.ok(!existsSync(hookPath), 'legacy hook script should be removed')
assert.ok(!existsSync(rulePath), 'legacy Claude todo rule should be removed')
assert.ok(!existsSync(cursorRule), 'legacy Cursor todo rule should be removed')

// Claude settings.json migrated: pre-existing user hook preserved, Blume hook removed.
const mergedRaw = readFileSync(join(claudeDir, 'settings.json'), 'utf-8')
const merged = JSON.parse(mergedRaw)
assert.deepEqual(merged.permissions, { allow: ['Bash(ls)'] }, 'unrelated keys preserved')
const ups = merged.hooks.UserPromptSubmit
assert.equal(ups.length, 1, 'should keep only the user hook')
assert.equal(ups[0].hooks[0].command, 'echo pre-existing-user-hook')

// Backup written
const backupDir = join(blumeHome, 'backups')
assert.ok(existsSync(backupDir), 'backup dir should exist')

// --- second run: marker should short-circuit
const before = readFileSync(markerPath, 'utf-8')
const second = await installHost.runInstall()
console.log('[test] second run state matched marker:', second.appVersion === marker.appVersion)
const after = readFileSync(markerPath, 'utf-8')
assert.equal(before, after, 'marker file should be untouched on no-op re-run')

// --- third run: force=true remains idempotent and does not restore the integration
await installHost.runInstall({ force: true })
const reMerged = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(claudeDir, 'settings.json'), 'utf-8'))
assert.equal(
  reMerged.hooks.UserPromptSubmit.length,
  1,
  'force re-run must not restore the Blume hook entry'
)

console.log('\n[test] all assertions passed ✓')

<file path="__test/loader.mjs">
// Custom resolver that swaps `electron` and `@electron-toolkit/utils`
// for local stubs, so we can exercise the install module under plain
// Node + tsx without launching Electron.
/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/explicit-function-return-type */
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { resolve as resolvePath, dirname } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const STUBS = {
  electron: pathToFileURL(resolvePath(here, 'stubs/electron.mjs')).href,
  '@electron-toolkit/utils': pathToFileURL(resolvePath(here, 'stubs/electron-toolkit-utils.mjs'))
    .href
}

export async function resolve(specifier, context, nextResolve) {
  if (STUBS[specifier]) {
    return { url: STUBS[specifier], format: 'module', shortCircuit: true }
  }
  // Node's --experimental-strip-types doesn't auto-append `.ts` for
  // extensionless relative imports. Try the bare specifier first; if it
  // 404s and the specifier is relative, retry with `.ts`.
  try {
    return await nextResolve(specifier, context)
  } catch (err) {
    if (
      err?.code === 'ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND' &&
      (specifier.startsWith('./') || specifier.startsWith('../'))
    ) {
      return nextResolve(`${specifier}.ts`, context)
    }
    throw err
  }
}
</file>
