<file path="docs/universal-links.md">
# Clickable links from agent chats

Agents continue to share HTTPS links. They do not call `blume_open_app` as a side
effect of posting updates. A click can go through macOS's Universal Links handler
to Blume; the existing website remains the fallback for unsupported clients,
older apps and development-channel links.

## Contract and ownership

The website serves `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` as JSON with no
redirect. Only `/open/deliveries/*` is associated. The stable app
`5YWNUNABHW.page.blume.sidecar` handles absent/empty `app` or `app=stable`; Canary
`5YWNUNABHW.page.blume.sidecar.canary` handles `app=canary`. Explicit other
channels are excluded from Stable. The team and bundle identifiers were checked
against the installed signed apps and existing release configuration.

The shared `@blume/app-core/app-links` decoder preserves valid delivery, task and
workspace IDs. Native receipt rejects wrong origins, channels, ambiguous IDs and
unsupported routes. Unknown query fields, including the existing per-link
`launch` nonce, never enter app navigation. Saved URLs have no expiry.

Electron registers `continue-activity` before asynchronous backend selection.
Browsing activities enter the same bounded startup queue as custom-scheme links;
only `details.webpageURL` is retained. Existing window delivery handles startup
and navigation. The local `deep link routed` log records `transport: universal-link`
or `custom-scheme`, so a browser's fallback cannot masquerade as direct receipt.
Rejected HTTPS destinations emit `deep link rejected` with a fixed reason and
transport, without recording the raw URL or its private identifiers.
Product behavior still uses the shared route table; Web Lab does not claim a
native association.

## Signing prerequisites and rollout

1. Enable Associated Domains for both explicit macOS App IDs in the Apple
   Developer account. Generate **Developer ID** provisioning profiles for each,
   using the existing release signing certificate. A wildcard App ID, App Store
   profile or development profile is not sufficient.
2. Store each profile's base64 encoding in the repository Actions secrets
   `MAC_PROVISION_PROFILE_STABLE` and `MAC_PROVISION_PROFILE_CANARY`. Do not commit
   profiles or signing keys. No certificate rotation is needed.
3. Deploy the website association through the website's normal Vercel main path.
   Verify a 200 JSON response, no redirect/authentication, and Apple's CDN copy:
   `https://app-site-association.cdn-apple.com/a/v1/blume.codes`.
4. Ship the desktop changes through the canonical reviewed release process.
   Release packaging selects only that channel's profile, validates its grant,
   embeds it and checks the **signed** main executable's entitlements. Helpers
   retain their original runtime entitlements and do not claim the association.
   After signing, the actual leaf certificate's SHA-256 must occur in the
   embedded profile's `DeveloperCertificates`; a mismatched certificate fails
   packaging. Certificate extraction uses a temporary directory outside the
   app, preserving sealed bundle bytes and any stapled notarization ticket.
   Missing/expired/wrong-channel profiles fail packaging rather than shipping an
   app that appears to support links but cannot establish trust.
5. On an isolated test installation, launch the signed app once. Verify macOS's
   domain approval and then the source-client matrix below. Keep Stable and
   Canary separate. Never claim a generic unsigned Electron dev build proves
   Universal Links.

Adding an entitlement changes signing. Before merge, the repository's Mac updater
safety gate requires signed/notarized physical update evidence: previous published
production source to the candidate through **Restart to Update**, with exact SHAs,
versions, bundle identities, feed, ZIP/DMG and latest-mac.yml integrity recorded.
Use the approved isolated certification process; a plain install or a future
canary-check promise is not equivalent. This change does not alter updater code,
feed paths, version selection or metadata generation.

For PR #1479 the owner explicitly approved the scoped Canary-first exception on
10 November 2026: “Approve Canary-first”. The preceding question covered merge
after code review/CI, Canary publication, deferred physical link/update tests,
Stable blocked, and possible manual reinstall after a signing failure. See the
agent-reported chat provenance in `docs/plans/universal-links.md`. This exception
applies only to #1479; the ordinary rule above remains unchanged. The
colleague-device test is cancelled. Keep verification issue #1522 open, inspect
the published signed artifacts, and record actual installed association, clicks
and Restart to Update results before any Stable promotion. Until then those
outcomes remain unverified.

The website can deploy first: old apps keep using the fallback. Roll back the
association file to stop future associations, allowing for Apple's/OS caches;
existing installed associations may persist. The fallback remains available.
Do not remove provisioning/signing grants from an otherwise released binary.

## Required click matrix

Record source app/version, macOS version, installed Blume version/source SHA,
signed identifier/profile, association response, initial browser tabs and the
exact saved URL. Use a disposable account and delivery on the selected test
deployment. Obtain a Markdown link in dedicated Codex and Claude Desktop chats
and a clickable URL from Claude Code in a terminal. Record the terminal name,
version and click gesture as well as the Claude Code version. Click each actual
rendered link, not the address bar, `open`, or the native tool.

For each client test Stable and Canary, cold and warm app state, a saved link
clicked twice, and task/workspace navigation. Observe all of:

- No browser tab/window appears as part of the successful direct handoff.
- The correct app/channel becomes visible at the expected destination.
- Its route log reports `transport: universal-link`.
- Older/absent apps and `app=dev` still have a usable website fallback.

If a client opens an embedded browser, record that behavior separately. OS trust,
client routing and user preference can each prevent direct opening. Never change
the system's default browser or reset the person's link preferences just to get a
passing result.

## Initial verification, 9 November 2026

- Codex and Claude Desktop are installed. Claude Code in a terminal is also in
  scope; record its version and terminal during the final matrix.
- The website PR preview serves the expected 817-byte association with HTTP 200
  and `application/json`. This proves serving on the preview, not OS association
  with the production domain.
- The public association endpoint currently returns **404 text/html**.
- This machine reports **0 valid code-signing identities**. Both explicit App IDs
  and Developer ID profiles were subsequently created with owner authorization;
  validated profiles are stored as `MAC_PROVISION_PROFILE_STABLE` and
  `MAC_PROVISION_PROFILE_CANARY` in repository Actions secrets. Each contains only
  the existing release certificate expiring 30 July 2031.
- The real profiles pass the preparation CLI, including Apple's string `*` domain
  grant. Profile/certification regression coverage: 82 passed.
- Existing updater certification uses a disposable bundle ID and trusted main
  signing configuration. It cannot serve as Universal Links click evidence for
  the real Stable/Canary identities; a matching signed candidate is still needed.
- Native parser/startup tests can run locally, but the modified signed app and
  public association are not yet deployed. Codex/Claude direct-click results are
  therefore **not tested**, not passed or failed.
- `swcutil verify` was attempted against the local file, but this macOS install
  requires root and passwordless sudo is unavailable. No system preferences were
  changed.

References: [Apple associated domains](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/supporting-associated-domains),
[Apple Universal Link debugging](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3155-debugging-universal-links),
[Electron continue-activity](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/app#event-continue-activity-macos).
</file>

Compare outcomes before choosing. An unspecified audience or platform can match several qualified outcomes; recency or one local plan file does not select one. Blume records the code diff at each Build and Test checkpoint itself; register code-changes only to add annotations where a line needs a reviewer's attention. A failed check needing a product fix returns to Build, then Test. Before presenting the result, rerun the acceptance checks with your own testing tools and register evidence at the current revision, wait for it to pass, then enter Outcome. Outcome presents the result; it is not human acceptance. Code covers merging, Release each application's release steps. Record actual merges, deployments and live checks as observations before advancing (a deployment names its application, step, url, commit and version: references/review.md); never claim provider confirmation from your own report. Done requires the requested outcome live and verified, or merged when it ships no application, with no unfinished work. A local demo stops at Outcome.

## Several deliveries become one

Choose an existing delivery whose outcome covers the combined work. Reuse its ID; a new chat, branch or implementation PR does not by itself require another delivery. If the intended outcome is ambiguous, ask which work belongs together.

Read only the affected deliveries' plans, open tasks, PR links and revision summaries. Update the destination plan with the combined outcome, acceptance criteria, remaining work and source delivery IDs. Reuse its task IDs; add missing tasks with distinct IDs and preserve a source-to-destination mapping in the plan. Keep completed source work and failures as historical facts. Moving unfinished work is not completing it.

Discover the connected backend's supported delivery operations before changing lifecycle state. The current get/update contract can update plans, tasks, links and facts; it does not merge or delete deliveries. With that contract, record the handoff in the destination plan and continue there, leaving the source deliveries intact. Report that this consolidates ongoing work, not their stored histories. Archiving is a separate list action where supported; it does not mean Done and does not transfer history. Do not delete a delivery merely to tidy the active list.

Evidence, test runs and approvals retain their original delivery, producer and revision. Reference useful source evidence rather than copying it as if it verified the combined revision. Run applicable checks on the integrated code before making that claim. An approval of one source revision never approves the combined work.

## Several agents, one delivery

When coordination is authorized, share the destination ID, plan, task ownership and source-to-destination mapping with the participating agents. Choose one integration owner to update the shared revision and phase. Other agents report progress and evidence at the actual revision they checked; they must not replace the integrated revision with their branch head. Some bridges automatically stamp the current checkout even on a task-only update: use the integration owner for those updates until the backend supports revision-safe collaboration.

Keep implementation PRs and historical deliveries linked from the plan. One delivery can span several PRs. Update its phase to the actual integrated state; a finished component does not make the whole outcome Done.

## One delivery becomes several

Split only when the requested outcomes are independently meaningful. Keep the original delivery for the outcome it still describes, create the other delivery, and record which open tasks moved and why in both plans. Remove moved tasks with a reason only after their replacement is recorded; do not mark them complete. Preserve old evidence and decisions where they were recorded. Each new outcome needs evidence and any required approval for its own revision.

## Resume after a handoff

Use the destination ID and remaining work recorded in the plan. Check the actual revision and relevant new facts before updating progress. If a consolidation attempt failed or the backend lacks the operation, retain the source records and continue the user's work with the explicit plan handoff. Do not invent a successful merge or repeatedly retry an unsupported operation.
`;
const APPROVAL_WORKFLOW = `# Human decisions reported from chat

Ask for an approval with blume_request op ask and approval plan, outcome, merge or release (code is the older merge name): add application and step for a release, and pullRequestUrl when the delivery has several pull requests. A question that is not an approval follows references/questions.md. Blume fills in the code under review and the exact scope, and runs the review flow whether or not approval recording is on. Read the exact review request before recording its answer; existing history stays readable.

Every ask, answer and withdraw needs requestId: a new idempotency key you invent (for example ask-plan-2), reused only for an identical retry. For answer/withdraw, id is the existing request ID returned by ask/get; it is not requestId. Before a plan review, follow references/plan.md and include a registered preview or README link as evidenceIds for UI plans (a link is enough). Before an outcome review, follow the task, commit and current-proof checklist in references/review.md.

Ask for review the same way whatever the workspace's settings. Before Build (approval plan), merging, releasing or calling the outcome accepted, call blume_request op check: it alone says whether Blume allows it now, and why. Other explicit requirements still apply. Bind the report to its request ID, immutable revision and unchanged scope. Outcome, behavior, merge and release decisions are distinct: permission to merge does not authorize a release.

Use \`requestDecision: approved\` or \`changes-requested\` only when the person explicitly answered that request. Preserve their statement and an available conversation/message reference with its occurrence time. A short “yes” needs an unambiguous preceding question identifying the request, code and scope. Praise, silence, an agent's recommendation or a peer's claim is not a decision. If intent is unclear, note the uncertainty in delivery history and clarify the missing scope; do not manufacture an approval report. Do not invent a quotation, speaker, timestamp or source reference.

Record a decision the person gave you in chat on an open approval request with blume_request op answer: its id, decision (approved or changes-requested) and their exact words as quote. It is kept as **reported from chat**, linked to the verified account behind your session. It counts at once as the person's go-ahead, whatever the workspace's settings: do not ask them to approve or confirm it again in Blume. A go-ahead to merge also covers going on past Outcome; Blume records the skipped outcome review and nothing waits for it. If no request is open for that decision yet, ask one with op ask and approval, then answer it with their words: a decision reported without a request is history only, never a go-ahead. A plan go-ahead given in chat counts while plan comments are open; those comments stay the person's feedback, to address or decline in your next plan version (references/plan.md). Before the step it covers, op check says whether to go ahead. A later decision in Blume takes precedence; the report stays in history. When the Blume plugin on the person's computer finds your quote in their own message, it marks the decision matched in chat; only the plugin sets that, so never send captured.

A go-ahead to ship (“just ship it”) covers the reviews still ahead (plan, outcome and code): record it on each one's request with the same quote, and tell the person which reviews it skipped. It never covers the checks: first finish the build and run the plan's acceptance checks, then merge and release without asking again. If a check fails, report it and do not merge. Until they pass, op check for the merge says to run them; the go-ahead stays recorded and counts once they do.

Source lookup in local agent logs may locate a user message, but does not authenticate its contents. Blume links the report to the verified account behind your session and supplies that person's name/avatar; do not send identity fields yourself. Keep agent-reported provenance: knowing the account does not turn a chat report into a direct app approval. Legacy or accountless reports may have only a reported speaker label.

Retry identical mutations with the same requestId. To correct a mistaken report, revoke it with a reason and record the correction; preserve earlier history. A request for older code remains historical even when a report is added later.

## Read and record

Read the selected request and registration schema on demand (replace the illustrative IDs):

\`\`\`json
{"deliveryId":"delivery-id","resource":"review_request","select":"get","id":"request-id"}
\`\`\`

\`\`\`json
{"deliveryId":"delivery-id","resource":"approval","select":"schema","operation":"register"}
\`\`\`

A standalone report of explicitly verified behavior, without a request, goes through blume_delivery_update with resource approval, operation register: the quoted statement, revision, exact scope and source with channel agent-chat/reference/occurredAt. It records history without answering a request, so it is not a go-ahead and op check does not count it. The service derives the linked person and agent recorder; speakerLabel never overrides that identity.

To ask for a decision, use blume_request op ask with approval. The request does not itself approve anything. Creating requests, reporting chat answers, reviewing evidence and granting authenticated app approval remain distinct operations.

const PLAN_FILE_GUIDE = `# The delivery's plan file

Read this when you write or change a delivery's plan. Each delivery has ONE Markdown plan file in the repository, its spec: the source of truth for what you build and how. Name it once with blume_delivery_update, operation update, data.spec: "docs/plans/refunds.md" (or resource plan, data.path). From then on edit it like any file: the Blume plugin syncs every save. Each upload becomes a plan version the person can compare, and the file's acceptance checks, tasks and decisions become the delivery's.

## Checkpoint the work, not just the plan

A plan upload or a task tick does not move the delivery's phase or revision. Use blume_delivery_update with resource delivery, operation update, deliveryId, a fresh requestId and data:

- Before writing the plan: {"phase":"Plan"}.
- After blume_request op check with approval plan allows Build, before editing product code: {"phase":"Build"}.
- Before running checks: {"phase":"Test"}. A product fix returns to Build, then Test.
- After each commit or push, before registering evidence or ending the turn: checkpoint the actual phase again, even if unchanged. Include data.branch from git branch --show-current, especially after a push. The plugin supplies the checkout revision and branch during Build/Test; confirm they match HEAD and the PR head branch so GitHub can attach the PR. Do not invent a revision or use task ticks as a checkpoint.

Committing the finished work on a feature branch is your Build step in a repository that merges changes; do it without asking for a separate go-ahead unless the user or repository explicitly forbids it or requires permission. A README that says to work on a feature branch is the workflow to follow, not a reason to wait. Preserve unrelated changes. Run preliminary checks, then sync only the task ticks whose checks actually passed and commit your code and plan in Build. Checkpoint Test and run final acceptance checks on that commit. Keep the checkout unchanged during final verification (logs and reports outside it); do not create a rerun loop by editing plan ticks after each final run. If a failure needs a fix, return to Build, fix, check, sync ticks and commit again before final verification. Commit, merge and release are separate steps; the latter two still require their review checks.

Read references/tasks.md before writing the checklist. Give each task a stable trailing marker such as {#theme-switch} on the first write, before uploading or asking plan review. A bare #id is part of the title, not an ID; use {#id} or enclose #id in literal backticks as in the template. Resolve planNotes about missing IDs before asking, using the returned IDs rather than inventing replacements. Group multi-step work under a recognizable result with two or more children; put its verification under Test. Include known commit, review, merge and deployment work, and add new work before doing it. A review approval belongs to the person; your preparation and checks are agent tasks. Tick completed children and roll up their parents only after their checks pass.

## Template

\`\`\`md
# Refunds

## Outcome
A person refunds an order from its page, fully or in part.

## Acceptance checks
- A refunded order shows its refund and the amount left — e2e: refund-flow \`#refund-shown\`
- A partial refund never exceeds what is left — unit: refundMath.test.ts \`#refund-cap\`
- The provider records the refund — integration \`#provider-refund\`
- The refund email reads well — manual \`#refund-email\`

## Approach
Refund through the payment provider; record the refund on the order.

## Decisions
- Refunds go back to the original payment method.
- Partial refunds are allowed (the person asked on 12 Oct).

## Tasks
### Plan
- [x] Read the order and payment code \`#read-code\`
### Build
- [~] Refund button \`#refund-button\`
  - [x] Confirm dialog \`#confirm\`
  - [ ] Refund API call \`#refund-call\`
- [-] CSV export \`#csv\` — the person dropped it
### Test
- [ ] Refund end-to-end test \`#refund-e2e\`
### Review
- [ ] Person reviews refunds on staging \`#review\`
\`\`\`

## Acceptance checks

What proves the outcome, one bullet each: the check, then after " — " the evidence type that proves it, and optionally its target after a colon:

- \`e2e\`: an end-to-end check run with your own testing tools and registered as delivery evidence; \`e2e: <scenario id>\` names it.
- \`unit\` or \`integration\`: the project's own tests; \`unit: <test file or name>\` names them.
- \`manual\`: a check you or the person make by hand, recorded with notes (a screenshot when it helps).
- \`agent-evaluation\` (target: evaluator or dataset), \`custom\` (its label): results that pass or fail.
- \`image\`, \`link\`, \`change-summary\`, \`code-changes\`: no result; met once recorded at the current code.

Give every check a trailing \`#id\` and keep it, as for tasks; without one Blume makes it from the text and tells you which to write. A check with no type or an unknown one is read as manual, and Blume tells you.

Gather evidence for each check in Build and Test, and name the checks it covers: acceptanceChecks on the evidence you register (any type but question-context). Without them Blume matches evidence of the check's type by its target. A check is met when evidence of its type passed at the current code; The outcome review needs every check met (a plan without checks needs passing test evidence of some kind). blume_delivery_get shows each check's status under acceptance. Before asking approval outcome, finish and sync every agent Test task. For work to merge, commit first, checkpoint Test at HEAD, then run/register final checks at that code; do not ask with open Test work or stale evidence. See references/review.md for the full checklist.

## Tasks

- Markers: \`[ ]\` open, \`[~]\` in progress, \`[x]\` done, \`[-]\` removed. A removed task gives its reason after " — ".
- A task may name the evidence it needs after " — needs ", as a check names its type: \`- [ ] Make the unit tests pass — needs unit\`. Guidance only: link that evidence to it (workIds); Blume shows whether it is met.
- Give every task a trailing \`#id\`, and keep it: a renamed task with the same id stays the same task. Without one Blume uses the id of the delivery's task with that title, or one made from the title, and tells you which: write that id. Use the ids the delivery's tasks already have; a new id for a known task replaces it.
- Root tasks sit under a \`### <Phase>\` heading: Start, Plan, Build, Test, Review, Release, Done. Review holds two reviews: tasks under \`### Review\` are the outcome review's, tasks under \`### Merge review\` the merge review's (Outcome and Code, the older names, still read). Sub-tasks inherit their root's phase and nest at most two levels deep (indent by two spaces). Group a part of the result's steps under it: references/tasks.md says when and how.
- Keep the list exhaustive and true: mark a task [~] as you begin it and [x] when it is finished (Blume starts and finishes a parent with its sub-tasks); add work as you find it; mark what proved unneeded [-] with a reason. Deleting a line removes its task, but when one save drops most of the list at once (a stash or branch switch) Blume removes none of them.
- Review work and later (the person's reviews) is the person's: their approval completes it. Do not mark it [x] or move it under an earlier phase; Blume leaves it where it is. Once approved it stays done, whatever its line says.
- Only lines you change count. A task changed by a tool call or an approval since your last save keeps that change until you edit its line.
- Blume tells you, with your next call for the delivery, about lines it could not read or apply. Fix them in the file.
- To read the tasks without loading the whole plan: blume_delivery_get with resource task (status open lists what is left).

## Decisions

Record every decision as a bullet under \`## Decisions\`, with why when it matters. Indented lines continue the bullet above. Each new bullet is recorded once on the delivery's current phase.

## Plan versus other phases

Write the plan in Plan, before you build. Keep it current in every phase: when the work or your understanding changes, change the file; the delivery stays in its phase and the change becomes a new version. Re-enter Plan only to re-plan when requirements change. Fenced code in the file is not read as tasks or decisions.

When the project reviews plans, finish the file before you ask (blume_request op ask, approval plan). For a UI or design plan, a relevant preview/Storybook link or URL from the README is enough: register it as link evidence and include its ID in evidenceIds. Attach a screenshot only if you already have one or a browser/test tool you already use can capture it; never build or install image tooling for a plan review. A link in chat or in the plan is not attached to the review. For other plans, attach evidence that helps judge them: today's behaviour or a bug reproduction (failing is fine). Register each first (blume_delivery_update resource evidence) as ${legacyExclusions.PLAN_REVIEW_EVIDENCE_PHRASE}; asking again replaces the request and its evidence. Example: {"op":"ask","requestId":"plan-review-2","deliveryId":"delivery-id","approval":"plan","evidenceIds":["preview-link-id"]}. Use IDs returned by registration; do not copy these placeholders. The person approves the plan's content. Progress ticks ([~] and [x]) do not affect an approved plan. Any other change needs a new approval before Build: a task added, deleted, renamed or marked [-], or a change to an acceptance check, a decision, the outcome or the approach.

## Plan comments

The person may comment on the plan in Blume. Each comment reaches you as a message with its section, the passage and any replacement it suggests; blume_delivery_get resource plan lists the open ones with the plan's first page. Answer every open comment with blume_delivery_update resource plan, data.comments, for example \`{"comments":[{"id":"comment-id","state":"addressed"}]}\`: addressed once you changed the file for it (Blume needs a plan version newer than the comment), or declined with a note saying why. Answer them before you ask for the plan's approval, unless the person already gave their go-ahead in chat: then record it as it stands (references/approvals.md).

Open comments are the person's feedback. One raised after their plan go-ahead ends that go-ahead until they give a fresh one or dismiss it; answering it does not bring it back, so ask again once you have; where the project requires plan review, Build then waits, and blume_request op check says whether it does. In Blume a plan approval does not pass over the approver's own open comments: they dismiss them with it. A go-ahead they give in chat counts with comments open, and those comments stay feedback to answer in your next version.
`;
const FLAT_ROOTS_LIMIT = 8;
const TASKS_GUIDE = `# Breaking work into tasks

Read this when you write or extend a delivery's tasks. The person follows the delivery by them, so the list should read as the work does: a few parts of the result, each with the steps that finish it. A flat list of twenty steps hides which part is done.

## Levels

- **Root**: a part of the result the person would recognise and could check on its own ("Refund button", "Merge review readiness gate"). Name it for what it delivers. Usually 3 to 8 per phase.
- **Child** (indent two spaces): a concrete step that finishes its root, small enough to start and finish in one go, with a clear done ("Confirm dialog", "Refund API call"). Usually 2 to 6 per root.
- **Grandchild** (indent four spaces): only when a step itself has separate parts: one per screen, platform or package, or a design then its build. Rare. Nothing goes deeper.

## When to nest

Give a root children when it needs more than one commit, spans several files or packages, runs as a sequence (design, build, wire up), or its parts can be in progress at different times. Leave a root alone when it is one step.

Do not:
- make a parent with a single child;
- group by phase: the \`### <Phase>\` headings already do;
- put a feature's tests under its Build root. Children take their root's phase, so the tests are a root under \`### Test\`.

## Keeping it true

Mark the children; Blume moves the parent: starting a child starts its parent, finishing the last child finishes it, reopening a child reopens it, and the upload's notes say which parent lines to bring along. A parent can still be [~] before any child starts, for work on that part as a whole. Add children as you find the steps, not only when you plan. When a part proves unneeded, mark the parent and its children [-] with a reason.

## Example

Flat, hard to follow:

\`\`\`md
### Build
- [x] Refund button \`#refund-button\`
- [x] Confirm dialog \`#confirm\`
- [~] Refund API call \`#refund-call\`
- [ ] Refund row on the order page \`#refund-row\`
- [ ] Amount left on the order page \`#amount-left\`
- [ ] Refund email template \`#email-template\`
- [ ] Send the email after a refund \`#email-send\`
\`\`\`

Nested, each part with its steps:

\`\`\`md
### Build
- [~] Refund an order from its page \`#refund-flow\`
  - [x] Refund button \`#refund-button\`
  - [x] Confirm dialog \`#confirm\`
  - [~] Refund API call \`#refund-call\`
- [ ] Order page shows its refunds \`#refund-shown\`
  - [ ] Refund row \`#refund-row\`
  - [ ] Amount left \`#amount-left\`
- [ ] Refund email \`#refund-email\`
  - [ ] Template \`#email-template\`
  - [ ] Send after a refund \`#email-send\`
\`\`\`

Keep each task's \`#id\` when you move it under a parent: it stays the same task.

Blume notes it when a phase has more than ${FLAT_ROOTS_LIMIT} roots and none of them has sub-tasks.
`;
const REVIEW_WORKFLOW = `# Prepare the selected review

Use this reference when preparing evidence or a scoped review request, or responding to the person's evidence preferences. Keep the review tied to its actual revision and purpose:

- **Outcome:** does the delivered behavior achieve the requested outcome?
- **Merge:** review the current pull request head and its target branch.
- **Release:** review one application and environment at the revision being shipped.

These are separate requests. An outcome approval does not approve a merge or release, and one release target does not approve another. Ask with blume_request op ask and approval outcome, code or release: name the application and step for a release, and the pull request when there are several. Blume fills in the revision and the exact scope. A request asks for a decision; it does not grant approval. Before the shipping action, blume_request op check says whether to go ahead; the user's other requirements still apply.

## Before asking for outcome review

Finish the agent's Build and Test tasks, including the actual E2E run; a passing result does not tick the plan's task for you. Read the remaining tasks and acceptance status. Do not ask while a Test task is open or a check is unmet/stale, even if an earlier request was accepted. A successful ask is not proof of readiness: read its notes and blockers.

For work that will be merged, committing the finished, checked code and plan on a feature branch is your Build step, without a separate permission question unless explicitly required by the user or repository. Follow the commit/final-verification sequence in references/plan.md: sync task ticks before that commit, then keep the checkout unchanged during the final run. Checkpoint Test at HEAD with blume_delivery_update resource delivery, operation update, then run the final acceptance checks at that revision and register their evidence. After any further code edit, repeat this sequence. A local uncommitted demo may be reviewed at its exact +wip revision, but must still have passing proof for that revision. Never claim an older run proves newer code.

Once the final checks pass, verify current acceptance and the task ticks already synced before the commit, then ask approval outcome. If you missed a completed task tick, sync it, commit that plan change and rerun once at the new revision; do not edit the plan again merely to record the rerun. Never tick an unmet check. If the person reports an approval was refused, read the request and current blockers, finish the missing work and re-ask; do not merely say you are waiting.

## Existing delivery suites

A test of a delivery's Blume suite is met by e2e or manual evidence at the current revision titled with the test's name, as a Blume run would be; the newest decides. Run it with your own tools and register it; never mark old runs passed.

## Merge review

After the outcome approval, make the pull request merge-ready: pushed and current, its checks finished and green, review bots done and their feedback handled. Then ask the merge review with blume_request op ask, approval merge: it is the person's one "merge this now?" question, so ask it only once nothing else is pending. Never ask whether to merge as a plain question, in Blume or only in chat. While it waits, tell the person what it waits for and end your turn; their answer in Blume reaches you as a message. A push after asking closes the request: once the new head is merge-ready, ask again.

## Revisions

Entering Outcome on new code makes a new revision, which the person reviews by name. Name it with revisionName on the checkpoint that enters Outcome, or with the title of the outcome approval request: a few words on what changed since the last revision. Say what changed in your reply too. Unchanged code keeps its revision. An approval belongs to the revision it was given at: when code review sends the work back, or the code changes for any other reason, rerun the acceptance checks at the new code with your own testing tools and register their evidence, enter Outcome again with the new revision's name and ask for its outcome approval.

## Release steps

A step whose approval is required can be asked for once its application is deployed to the step before it: ask with approval release, its application and step. Check the step before first when you can. If no check of the code passed there yet, the ask still goes through: Blume records the skipped check and shows the person a note, not a blocker. Never drive the person's own app or account to check a step: use an instance of your own (a separate install or profile with its own HOME, or a browser against that step's backend), signed in with a test account you create. One step's approval never covers another. A step that deploys without approval takes no request: deploy and record it. Check the step itself: run checks with your own testing tools against its URL and register evidence with the application's name and the step's exact name, or record a check you ran with blume_delivery_update resource observation, operation register, data kind check, check live, title, outcome, the url you checked, application and step. A localhost target is a local check whatever its label. Record each deploy the same way with kind deployment: application, step, url, commit (the code deployed) and version (the build or version it shipped as).

## Present it as a brief

Every review is asked with a brief: the plan, the outcome, the merge and each release step. A brief is a few slides that argue for the review, citing the evidence. It is about the whole of what is decided (the outcome as agreed, the whole pull request, everything a release ships), written for a person reading it cold; what changed since the last revision is one short part, never its frame. Call blume_request op prepare with the approval kind first; it returns the guide for that kind, the delivery's checks and records with their ids, and a skeleton. Replace every TODO, cite records as figure or evidence blocks and inline as [words](ev:<id>), name checks as [words](check:<id>), then ask with the result as brief (or write it to a JSON file and send briefPath). The review opens on your slides; each slide lists the records it cites beside it, and Blume adds its own Coverage of every check. A refused brief names the slide and field to fix. Every question is asked with one too: 1 to 3 slides of context beside the question (references/questions.md). An ask without a brief is told to prepare one and ask again; asking again replaces it.

Choose the presentation to match the change. For backend work, explain the observed API behavior, assertions or measurements and cite their test evidence; no screenshot is required. Diagrams may explain the design but do not substitute for results.

For screenshot-backed outcome checks, evidence links alone do not show the result, and a brief stays brief. Prepare returns one figure per check a screenshot proves: keep it, choose that proof's most telling view (its evidence id and one-based image number), mark what the check is about, and replace its finding and caption TODOs. The other screenshots stay with the record, one → away; use shots only for a short sequence where the order is the point. Put the figures after the cover and before the checks. Do not infer success from an uploaded image or invent annotations. Nonvisual checks need no images. Read back the saved request to confirm its image blocks remain present.

## Choose and register evidence

Use the evidence that helps answer this review: a change summary or E2E walkthrough for behavior, a code diff or command results for a merge, and checks of the selected deployed target for a release. Image and link evidence show context beside a review or a question: a screenshot, mockup or diagram, or a page such as an issue or a design. They, and question-context, are never results: register them with outcome unknown, and they meet no acceptance check. Use custom evidence (a label and titled sections) only for a check no other type fits, such as a load test or an accessibility audit. Choose the type before loading its registration schema. These schema reads are examples; replace the delivery ID and selected evidence type:

\`\`\`json
{"deliveryId":"delivery-id","resource":"evidence","select":"schema","operation":"register","type":"change-summary"}
\`\`\`

Do not preload every evidence schema or every review kind. Read only the selected evidence's detail when needed. Register the checks actually performed with truthful observed results and supporting artifacts. A typed report, including a type named unit-tests or E2E, is agent-reported evidence; registering it does not execute a test or confirm a provider action; it counts as a Blume run of the same check would. Preserve failures and unknown results. Marking evidence reviewed is separate from its test outcome and from approval.

Use the selected schema for images and annotations. A summary can explain changes with image blocks and marks (box, highlight, arrow or pin, in 0–1 fractions of the image, origin top left; older 0–100 arrows still work). A code-changes report should come from the real diff: send payload.diff with base and head (or a diff file) rather than retyping hunks, and attach annotations to real diff lines. Test results should come from the runner's report file (references/testing.md). Uploaded screenshots support observations; they do not independently prove an assertion passed.

Reuse screenshot URLs already returned by Blume in image slots; they are authenticated evidence, not public download links. Do not download and re-upload them. Use local paths only for screenshots you captured yourself, preserving the originals.

## Apply preferences to future evidence

Before preparing evidence, read only the selected review's effective preferences with blume_delivery_get. The bridge reads the current checkout's .blume/review-preferences.json when enabled and returns the selected settings or defaults. For example:

\`\`\`json

function parsePluginIdentity(value) {
  if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value))
    throw Error("Invalid plugin identity");
  const v2 = value;
  const version = (x2) => {
    if (typeof x2 !== "string" || !/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9.+_-]{0,63}$/.test(x2))
      throw Error("Invalid plugin version");
    return x2;
  };
  if (v2.schemaVersion !== 1 || v2.name !== PLUGIN_IDENTITY_NAME || !["codex", "claude", "portable", "bridge", "source"].includes(String(v2.format)))
    throw Error("Unsupported plugin identity");
  if (typeof v2.fingerprint !== "string" || !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(v2.fingerprint))
    throw Error("Invalid plugin fingerprint");
  if (!Array.isArray(v2.components) || v2.components.length > 6)
    throw Error("Invalid plugin components");
  const ids = /* @__PURE__ */ new Set();
  const components2 = v2.components.map((item) => {
    if (!item || typeof item !== "object") throw Error("Invalid plugin component");
    const c2 = item;
    if (typeof c2.id !== "string" || !["mcp", "skills", "rules", "scripts", "docs", "hooks"].includes(c2.id) || ids.has(c2.id))
      throw Error("Invalid plugin component");
    ids.add(c2.id);
    return {
      id: c2.id,
      version: version(c2.version)
    };
  });
  const toolNames = v2.toolNames ?? [];
  if (!Array.isArray(toolNames) || toolNames.length > 64 || toolNames.some((name) => typeof name !== "string" || !/^blume_[a-z_]{1,64}$/.test(name)) || new Set(toolNames).size !== toolNames.length)
    throw Error("Invalid plugin tool names");
  if (toolNames.length && !ids.has("mcp")) throw Error("Tools require MCP component");
  return {
    toolNames,
    schemaVersion: 1,
    name: PLUGIN_IDENTITY_NAME,
    version: version(v2.version),
    format: v2.format,
    fingerprint: v2.fingerprint,
    components: components2
  };
}

function ledgerGitHubRepositories(state, known = []) {
  const seen = /* @__PURE__ */ new Map();
  for (const project of legacyExclusions.listProjects(state, known))
    for (const repository of project.repositories) {
      const key = githubKey(repository);
      if (key && !seen.has(key)) seen.set(key, repository);
    }
  return [...seen.values()].slice(0, MAX_REPOSITORIES$1);
}
function githubPresenceReport(state, list, login) {
  if (!list) return { presence: { connected: false, repositories: [] } };
  const shared = new Set(list.projects.map((project) => repositoryKey.repositoryMatchKey(project.url) ?? repositoryKey.repositoryMatchKey(`github.com/${project.fullName}`)));
  const repositories = ledgerGitHubRepositories(state).flatMap((repository) => {
    const readable = shared.has(repositoryKey.repositoryMatchKey(repository));
    return readable || !list.truncated ? [{ repository, readable }] : [];
  });
  return { presence: { connected: true, ...login ? { login } : {}, repositories } };
}

const WAKE_HOOK_TIMEOUT_S = 8 * 60 * 60 + 60;
function blumeHooksConfig(command, options = {}) {
  const hooks = [{ type: "command", command, timeout: 15 }];
  const handler = [{ hooks }];
  const stop = options.wake ? [...handler, { hooks: [{ type: "command", command: options.wake, async: true, asyncRewake: true, timeout: WAKE_HOOK_TIMEOUT_S }] }] : handler;
  return { hooks: { SessionStart: handler, UserPromptSubmit: handler, PreToolUse: [{ matcher: "AskUserQuestion|request_user_input|request_user_input_async", hooks }], PostToolUse: handler, Stop: stop } };
}

   * If true, the tool does not modify its environment.
   *
   * Default: false
   */
  readOnlyHint: legacyExclusions.boolean().optional(),
  /**
   * If true, the tool may perform destructive updates to its environment.
   * If false, the tool performs only additive updates.
   *
   * (This property is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint == false`)
   *
   * Default: true
   */
  destructiveHint: legacyExclusions.boolean().optional(),
  /**
   * If true, calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments
   * will have no additional effect on the its environment.
   *
   * (This property is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint == false`)
   *
   * Default: false
   */
  idempotentHint: legacyExclusions.boolean().optional(),
  /**
   * If true, this tool may interact with an "open world" of external
   * entities. If false, the tool's domain of interaction is closed.
   * For example, the world of a web search tool is open, whereas that
   * of a memory tool is not.
   *
   * Default: true
   */
  openWorldHint: legacyExclusions.boolean().optional()

const CallToolResultSchema = ResultSchema.extend({
  /**
   * A list of content objects that represent the result of the tool call.
   *
   * If the Tool does not define an outputSchema, this field MUST be present in the result.
   * For backwards compatibility, this field is always present, but it may be empty.
   */
  content: legacyExclusions.array(ContentBlockSchema).default([]),
  /**
   * An object containing structured tool output.
   *
   * If the Tool defines an outputSchema, this field MUST be present in the result, and contain a JSON object that matches the schema.
   */
  structuredContent: legacyExclusions.record(legacyExclusions.string(), legacyExclusions.unknown()).optional(),
  /**
   * Whether the tool call ended in an error.
   *
   * If not set, this is assumed to be false (the call was successful).
   *
   * Any errors that originate from the tool SHOULD be reported inside the result
   * object, with `isError` set to true, _not_ as an MCP protocol-level error
   * response. Otherwise, the LLM would not be able to see that an error occurred
   * and self-correct.
   *
   * However, any errors in _finding_ the tool, an error indicating that the
   * server does not support tool calls, or any other exceptional conditions,
   * should be reported as an MCP error response.
   */
  isError: legacyExclusions.boolean().optional()
});

  action: legacyExclusions._enum(["accept", "decline", "cancel"]),

   * We normalize null to undefined for leniency while maintaining type compatibility.

  content: legacyExclusions.preprocess((val) => val === null ? void 0 : val, legacyExclusions.record(legacyExclusions.string(), legacyExclusions.union([legacyExclusions.string(), legacyExclusions.number(), legacyExclusions.boolean(), legacyExclusions.array(legacyExclusions.string())])).optional())

          if (JSON.stringify(record.chat) !== JSON.stringify(next2)) {
            const previous = record.chat;
            record.chat = next2;
            try {
              await save();
            } catch (error) {
              record.chat = previous;
              throw error;
            }
          }
          record.chat = next2;
          return {
            ...structuredClone(record.chat),
            ...availableModels ? { availableModels } : {}
          };
        } catch (error) {
          connections.delete(id2);
          reconnectAfter.set(id2, Date.now() + 3e4);
          throw error;
        }
      });
      jobs.set(id2, next);
      try {
        return await next;
      } catch (error) {
        if (unavailable && request.action === "get" && !explicitWake && cached && !abort.signal.aborted)
          return {
            ...structuredClone(cached),
            status: "error",
            error: "Cloud connection unavailable. Showing the saved conversation; send a message to reconnect.",
            approvals: [],
            mcpReady: false
          };
        throw error;
      } finally {
        if (jobs.get(id2) === next) jobs.delete(id2);
      }
    },
    async close() {
      abort.abort();
      await Promise.allSettled([...jobs.values()]);
      await writing;
      connections.clear();
    }
  };
  return runtime;
}

function cloudSubscriptions(root, env = process.env, security) {
  const credentialFor = security?.credential ?? cloudProviderCredential;
  const purpose = (harness) => `${security?.scope}:subscription:${harness}`;
  const directory = _n.join(root, "subscriptions");
  const path = (harness) => _n.join(directory, `${harness}.json`);
  const read = async (harness) => {
    try {
      if ((await require$$0.stat(path(harness))).size > 96 * 1024)
        throw Error("Saved agent sign-in is too large");

      try {
        const content = await require$$0.readFile(path(harness), "utf8");
        value = JSON.parse(
          security ? security.box.open(content, purpose(harness)) : content
        );
      } catch {
        throw Error("Import the agent sign-in again");
      }
      if (value.harness !== harness || !value.version || !value.credential?.content)
        throw Error("Import the agent sign-in again");

    } catch (cause) {
      if (cause.code === "ENOENT") return void 0;
      throw cause;
    }
  };

    ["codex", "claude"].map(async (harness) => {

      return {
        harness,
        configured: Boolean(saved),
        ...saved ? { source: saved.source, updatedAt: saved.updatedAt } : {}
      };
    })
  );
  let pending = Promise.resolve();
  return {
    read,
    // A first workspace import must not become an instruction to reauthorize older workspaces.
    async forProvisioning(harness) {
      return (await read(harness))?.credential ?? credentialFor(harness, env);
    },
    async request(value) {
      const request = pullRequestContent.validateCloudSubscriptionRequest(value);
      if (request.action === "status") return status();
      if (request.action === "disconnect")
        throw Error("Disconnect is available through the hosted cloud owner");
      if (request.action === "reconnect")
        throw Error("Reconnect cloud access through the desktop hosted-cloud connection");
      const operation = pending.then(async () => {
        const credential = request.action === "token" ? { path: "claude-token", content: request.token } : await credentialFor(request.harness, env);
        const previous = await read(request.harness);
        const saved = {
          harness: request.harness,
          version: require$$0$1.randomUUID(),
          source: request.action === "token" ? "subscription-token" : "local-sign-in",
          updatedAt: Math.max(Date.now(), (previous?.updatedAt ?? 0) + 1),
          credential
        };

        const temporary = `${path(request.harness)}.${saved.version}.tmp`;
        await require$$0.writeFile(
          temporary,
          security ? security.box.seal(JSON.stringify(saved), purpose(request.harness)) : JSON.stringify(saved),
          { mode: 384, flag: "wx" }
        );
        await require$$0.rename(temporary, path(request.harness));
        return status();
      });
      pending = operation.catch(() => {
      });
      return operation;
    }
  };
}

function githubFetchUrl(repository) {

    throw Error(INVALID);
  return `${repository.replace(/\.git$/, "")}.git`;
}
function target(value) {

    throw Error(INVALID);

  return { requestId: v2.requestId, repository: v2.repository, revision: v2.revision };
}
function parseCloudRepositoryChallenge(value, now = Date.now()) {

async function readCloudRepositoryChallenge(response) {
  const reader = response.body?.getReader();
  if (!reader) throw Error(INVALID);
  const chunks = [];
  let bytes = 0;
  try {
    for (; ; ) {
      const next = await reader.read();
      if (next.done) break;
      bytes += next.value.byteLength;
      if (bytes > 8192) throw Error(INVALID);
      chunks.push(next.value);
    }
    const value = JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8"));
    if (value?.code !== "cloud_repository_access_required") throw Error(INVALID);
    return new CloudRepositoryAccessRequired(value.challenge);
  } catch {
    throw Error(INVALID);
  } finally {
    await reader.cancel().catch(() => {

  }

function validateLinkGraph(files) {

        resolved.pop();

      }

    }
  }

const COLD_START_BUDGET_MS = 4e4;
const ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS = { local: 12e3, remote: 2e4 };
function createControlPlaneClient(input, transport = fetch, wait = (ms2) => new Promise((resolve2) => setTimeout(resolve2, ms2))) {
  const endpoint = new URL(input.endpoint);
  if (endpoint.username || endpoint.password || endpoint.pathname !== "/" || endpoint.search || endpoint.hash)
    throw Error("Ledger endpoint must be an exact origin without credentials");
  if (input.remote ? endpoint.protocol !== "https:" : !(endpoint.protocol === "http:" && ["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]"].includes(endpoint.hostname)))
    throw Error(
      input.remote ? "Remote ledger requires HTTPS" : "Local ledger requires loopback HTTP"
    );
  const secret = input.cookie ?? input.token ?? "";
  if (Boolean(input.cookie) === Boolean(input.token))
    throw Error("One account credential is required");
  if (secret.length < 32 || secret.length > 4096 || (input.cookie ? /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/ : /[\u0000-\u0020\u007f]/).test(secret))
    throw Error("Ledger token must be a bounded header-safe secret");
  const paths = {
    /** What changed after a cursor, as the signed-in person may see it. */
    changes: "/control/changes",
    call: "/control/call",
    connect: "/control/connect",
    installations: "/control/installations",
    /** Workspaces, members and plan: answered by Auth for the session, not by a ledger. */
    workspace: "/control/workspace",
    /** Verified account/workspace identity for trusted server adapters; no session secrets. */
    identity: "/control/identity",
    /** GitHub sync worker only; Electron main never forwards this operation from the renderer. */
    githubSync: "/control/github-sync"
  };
  return {
    async request(operation, data = {}) {
      const path = Object.hasOwn(paths, operation) ? paths[operation] : void 0;
      if (!path) throw Error("Unknown ledger operation");
      const body = operation === "changes" ? void 0 : JSON.stringify(data);
      if (body && Buffer.byteLength(body) > 64 * 1024) throw Error("Request exceeds 64 KiB");
      const url2 = new URL(path, endpoint);
      if (operation === "changes") {
        const { cursor = 0, ledger } = data;
        if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cursor) || cursor < 0) throw Error("Invalid change cursor");
        if (ledger !== void 0 && (typeof ledger !== "string" || !/^[a-f0-9]{1,64}$/.test(ledger)))
          throw Error("Invalid ledger");
        url2.searchParams.set("cursor", String(cursor));
        if (ledger !== void 0) url2.searchParams.set("ledger", ledger);
      }
      const started = Date.now();
      for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
        const response = await transport(url2, {
          method: body === void 0 ? "GET" : "POST",
          headers: {
            ...input.cookie ? { Cookie: input.cookie } : { Authorization: `Bearer ${input.token}` },
            "Content-Type": "application/json"
          },
          ...body === void 0 ? {} : { body },
          redirect: "error",
          signal: AbortSignal.timeout(ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS[input.remote ? "remote" : "local"])
        });
        if (response.status === 401) {
          await response.body?.cancel();
          throw Error("Account session expired. Sign in again.");
        }
        const maximum = CONTROL_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES;
        const declared = Number(response.headers.get("content-length"));
        if (Number.isFinite(declared) && declared > maximum) {
          await response.body?.cancel();
          throw Error("Ledger response exceeds 12 MB");
        }
        const reader = response.body?.getReader();
        if (!reader) throw Error("Empty ledger response");
        const chunks = [];
        let size2 = 0;
        try {
          while (true) {
            const next = await reader.read();
            if (next.done) break;
            size2 += next.value.byteLength;
            if (size2 > maximum) throw Error("Ledger response exceeds 12 MB");
            chunks.push(next.value);
          }
        } finally {
          await reader.cancel().catch(() => {
          });
          reader.releaseLock();
        }
        const text2 = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8");
        const busy = text2 === "Account runtime is busy";
        const coldStart = text2 === "Account runtime is starting" || text2 === "Runtime unavailable" && body === void 0;
        if (input.remote && response.status === 503 && (coldStart || busy || text2 === "Runtime unavailable")) {
          const delay = Math.min(Math.max(Number(response.headers.get("retry-after")) || 2, 1), 5) * 1e3;
          const retry = coldStart || busy && operation !== "githubSync";
          if (retry && attempt < 8 && Date.now() - started + delay <= COLD_START_BUDGET_MS) {
            await wait(delay);
            continue;
          }
          throw Error(busy ? "Blume is busy right now. Try again in a moment." : "Your Blume account is still starting. Try again in a moment.");
        }
        let result;
        try {
          result = JSON.parse(text2);
        } catch {
          throw Error(`Invalid ledger response (${response.status})`);
        }
        if (!response.ok) {
          const error = result && typeof result === "object" && "error" in result ? result.error : void 0;
          throw new ControlPlaneRequestError(
            typeof error === "string" ? error.slice(0, 2e3) : `Ledger request failed (${response.status})`,
            response.status
          );
        }
        if (operation === "changes" && result && typeof result === "object" && Array.isArray(result.deliveries))
          normalizeControlPhases({ deliveries: result.deliveries, tests: { executions: result.executions ?? [] } });
        return pullRequestContent.resolveControlEvidenceUrls(result, endpoint.origin);
      }
    }
  };

function createLedgerCopy() {
  let held;
  let catching;
  async function catchUp(credential, client) {
    if (held?.credential !== credential) held = { credential, state: emptyLedgerState() };
    const copy = held;
    for (let page = 0; page < 1e4; page++) {
      const batch = await client.request("changes", { cursor: copy.state.version, ...copy.ledger ? { ledger: copy.ledger } : {} });
      if (copy.ledger !== void 0 && batch.ledger !== void 0 && batch.ledger !== copy.ledger) copy.state = emptyLedgerState();
      copy.ledger = batch.ledger;
      copy.state = applyControlChanges(copy.state, batch);
      if (!batch.more) return copy.state;
    }
    throw Error("The ledger kept changing while it was read");
  }
  return {
    /** The ledger now, read with `client` under `credential` (the session it signs in with). */
    async read(credential, client) {
      if (catching?.credential !== credential) {
        const done = catchUp(credential, client).finally(() => {
          if (catching?.done === done) catching = void 0;
        });
        catching = { credential, done };
      }
      return structuredClone(await catching.done);
    },
    /** Forgets the copy (signed out, account changed). */
    clear() {
      held = void 0;
      catching = void 0;
    }
  };
}
function emptyLedgerState() {
  return { version: 0, deliveries: [], threads: [], messages: [], clusters: [], improvements: [], receipts: {} };
}

function comparePluginVersions(a2, b2) {
  const left = VERSION.exec(a2);
  const right = VERSION.exec(b2);
  if (!left || !right) return null;
  for (let index2 = 1; index2 <= 3; index2++) {
    const difference = Number(left[index2]) - Number(right[index2]);
    if (difference) return Math.sign(difference);
  }
  const [preLeft, preRight] = [left[4], right[4]];
  if (preLeft === preRight) return 0;
  if (preLeft === void 0) return 1;
  if (preRight === void 0) return -1;
  return preLeft < preRight ? -1 : 1;
}

function ownLedger(record, context) {

function pluginUpdateDecision(record, context) {
  if (!context.enabled) return { update: false, reason: "disabled" };
  if (!context.autoUpdate) return { update: false, reason: "opted-out" };
  if (!record) return { update: false, reason: "not-installed" };
  const ledger = ownLedger(record, context);
  if (!ledger) return { update: false, reason: "other-channel" };
  const { moved } = ledger;
  if (moved && ledger.forward !== true) return { update: false, reason: ledger.forward === null ? "unknown-runtime" : "newer-runtime" };
  const order = record.version ? comparePluginVersions(record.version, context.latest) : null;
  if (order === null || !record.version) return { update: false, reason: "unknown-version" };
  if (order > 0) return { update: false, reason: "newer" };
  if (moved) return { update: true, from: record.version, to: context.latest, moveTo: context.endpoint };
  if (order === 0 && context.flower && record.flower !== context.flower)
    return { update: true, from: record.version, to: context.latest };
  if (order === 0) return { update: false, reason: "current" };
  return { update: true, from: record.version, to: context.latest };
}
function pluginMoveDecision(record, context) {
  if (!record) return { move: false, reason: "not-installed" };
  const ledger = ownLedger(record, context);
  if (!ledger) return { move: false, reason: "other-channel" };
  if (!ledger.moved) return { move: false, reason: "same-runtime" };
  if (ledger.forward !== true) return { move: false, reason: ledger.forward === null ? "unknown-runtime" : "newer-runtime" };
  const order = record.version ? comparePluginVersions(record.version, context.latest) : null;
  if (order === null || !record.version) return { move: false, reason: "unknown-version" };
  if (order > 0) return { move: false, reason: "newer" };
  return { move: true, from: record.endpoint, to: context.endpoint, version: record.version };
}

const MOVE_JOURNAL = "move-journal.json";
function createScanner(text2, ignoreTrivia = false) {
  const len = text2.length;
  let pos = 0, value = "", tokenOffset = 0, token = 16, lineNumber = 0, lineStartOffset = 0, tokenLineStartOffset = 0, prevTokenLineStartOffset = 0, scanError = 0;
  function scanHexDigits(count, exact) {
    let digits = 0;
    let value2 = 0;
    while (digits < count || false) {
      let ch = text2.charCodeAt(pos);
      if (ch >= 48 && ch <= 57) {
        value2 = value2 * 16 + ch - 48;
      } else if (ch >= 65 && ch <= 70) {
        value2 = value2 * 16 + ch - 65 + 10;
      } else if (ch >= 97 && ch <= 102) {
        value2 = value2 * 16 + ch - 97 + 10;
      } else {
        break;
      }
      pos++;
      digits++;
    }
    if (digits < count) {
      value2 = -1;
    }
    return value2;
  }
  function setPosition(newPosition) {
    pos = newPosition;
    value = "";
    tokenOffset = 0;
    token = 16;
    scanError = 0;
  }
  function scanNumber() {
    let start = pos;
    if (text2.charCodeAt(pos) === 48) {
      pos++;
    } else {
      pos++;
      while (pos < text2.length && isDigit(text2.charCodeAt(pos))) {
        pos++;
      }
    }
    if (pos < text2.length && text2.charCodeAt(pos) === 46) {
      pos++;
      if (pos < text2.length && isDigit(text2.charCodeAt(pos))) {
        pos++;
        while (pos < text2.length && isDigit(text2.charCodeAt(pos))) {
          pos++;
        }
      } else {
        scanError = 3;
        return text2.substring(start, pos);
      }
    }
    let end = pos;
    if (pos < text2.length && (text2.charCodeAt(pos) === 69 || text2.charCodeAt(pos) === 101)) {
      pos++;
      if (pos < text2.length && text2.charCodeAt(pos) === 43 || text2.charCodeAt(pos) === 45) {
        pos++;
      }
      if (pos < text2.length && isDigit(text2.charCodeAt(pos))) {
        pos++;
        while (pos < text2.length && isDigit(text2.charCodeAt(pos))) {
          pos++;
        }
        end = pos;
      } else {
        scanError = 3;
      }
    }
    return text2.substring(start, end);
  }
  function scanString() {
    let result = "", start = pos;
    while (true) {
      if (pos >= len) {
        result += text2.substring(start, pos);
        scanError = 2;
        break;
      }
      const ch = text2.charCodeAt(pos);
      if (ch === 34) {
        result += text2.substring(start, pos);
        pos++;
        break;
      }
      if (ch === 92) {
        result += text2.substring(start, pos);
        pos++;
        if (pos >= len) {
          scanError = 2;
          break;
        }
        const ch2 = text2.charCodeAt(pos++);
        switch (ch2) {
          case 34:
            result += '"';
            break;
          case 92:
            result += "\\";
            break;
          case 47:
            result += "/";
            break;
          case 98:
            result += "\b";
            break;
          case 102:
            result += "\f";
            break;
          case 110:
            result += "\n";
            break;
          case 114:
            result += "\r";
            break;
          case 116:
            result += "	";
            break;
          case 117:
            const ch3 = scanHexDigits(4);
            if (ch3 >= 0) {
              result += String.fromCharCode(ch3);
            } else {
              scanError = 4;
            }
            break;
          default:
            scanError = 5;
        }
        start = pos;
        continue;
      }
      if (ch >= 0 && ch <= 31) {
        if (isLineBreak(ch)) {
          result += text2.substring(start, pos);
          scanError = 2;
          break;
        } else {
          scanError = 6;
        }
      }
      pos++;
    }
    return result;
  }
  function scanNext() {
    value = "";
    scanError = 0;
    tokenOffset = pos;
    lineStartOffset = lineNumber;
    prevTokenLineStartOffset = tokenLineStartOffset;
    if (pos >= len) {
      tokenOffset = len;
      return token = 17;
    }
    let code2 = text2.charCodeAt(pos);
    if (isWhiteSpace(code2)) {
      do {
        pos++;
        value += String.fromCharCode(code2);
        code2 = text2.charCodeAt(pos);
      } while (isWhiteSpace(code2));
      return token = 15;
    }
    if (isLineBreak(code2)) {
      pos++;
      value += String.fromCharCode(code2);
      if (code2 === 13 && text2.charCodeAt(pos) === 10) {
        pos++;
        value += "\n";
      }
      lineNumber++;
      tokenLineStartOffset = pos;
      return token = 14;
    }
    switch (code2) {
      // tokens: []{}:,
      case 123:
        pos++;
        return token = 1;
      case 125:
        pos++;
        return token = 2;
      case 91:
        pos++;
        return token = 3;
      case 93:
        pos++;
        return token = 4;
      case 58:
        pos++;
        return token = 6;
      case 44:
        pos++;
        return token = 5;
      // strings
      case 34:
        pos++;
        value = scanString();
        return token = 10;
      // comments
      case 47:
        const start = pos - 1;
        if (text2.charCodeAt(pos + 1) === 47) {
          pos += 2;
          while (pos < len) {
            if (isLineBreak(text2.charCodeAt(pos))) {
              break;
            }
            pos++;
          }
          value = text2.substring(start, pos);
          return token = 12;
        }
        if (text2.charCodeAt(pos + 1) === 42) {
          pos += 2;
          const safeLength = len - 1;
          let commentClosed = false;
          while (pos < safeLength) {
            const ch = text2.charCodeAt(pos);
            if (ch === 42 && text2.charCodeAt(pos + 1) === 47) {
              pos += 2;
              commentClosed = true;
              break;
            }
            pos++;
            if (isLineBreak(ch)) {
              if (ch === 13 && text2.charCodeAt(pos) === 10) {
                pos++;
              }
              lineNumber++;
              tokenLineStartOffset = pos;
            }
          }
          if (!commentClosed) {
            pos++;
            scanError = 1;
          }
          value = text2.substring(start, pos);
          return token = 13;
        }
        value += String.fromCharCode(code2);
        pos++;
        return token = 16;
      // numbers
      case 45:
        value += String.fromCharCode(code2);
        pos++;
        if (pos === len || !isDigit(text2.charCodeAt(pos))) {
          return token = 16;
        }
      // found a minus, followed by a number so
      // we fall through to proceed with scanning
      // numbers
      case 48:
      case 49:
      case 50:
      case 51:
      case 52:
      case 53:
      case 54:
      case 55:
      case 56:
      case 57:
        value += scanNumber();
        return token = 11;
      // literals and unknown symbols
      default:
        while (pos < len && isUnknownContentCharacter(code2)) {
          pos++;
          code2 = text2.charCodeAt(pos);
        }
        if (tokenOffset !== pos) {
          value = text2.substring(tokenOffset, pos);
          switch (value) {
            case "true":
              return token = 8;
            case "false":
              return token = 9;
            case "null":
              return token = 7;
          }
          return token = 16;
        }
        value += String.fromCharCode(code2);
        pos++;
        return token = 16;
    }
  }
  function isUnknownContentCharacter(code2) {
    if (isWhiteSpace(code2) || isLineBreak(code2)) {
      return false;
    }
    switch (code2) {
      case 125:
      case 93:
      case 123:
      case 91:
      case 34:
      case 58:
      case 44:
      case 47:
        return false;
    }
    return true;
  }
  function scanNextNonTrivia() {
    let result;
    do {
      result = scanNext();
    } while (result >= 12 && result <= 15);
    return result;
  }
  return {
    setPosition,
    getPosition: () => pos,
    scan: ignoreTrivia ? scanNextNonTrivia : scanNext,
    getToken: () => token,
    getTokenValue: () => value,
    getTokenOffset: () => tokenOffset,
    getTokenLength: () => pos - tokenOffset,
    getTokenStartLine: () => lineStartOffset,
    getTokenStartCharacter: () => tokenOffset - prevTokenLineStartOffset,
    getTokenError: () => scanError
  };

      if (_scanner.getToken() === 5) {
        if (!needsComma) {
          handleError(4, [], []);
        }
        onSeparator(",");
        scanNext();
        if (_scanner.getToken() === 2 && allowTrailingComma) {
          break;
        }
      } else if (needsComma) {
        handleError(6, [], []);
      }

        ]);
      }
      needsComma = true;
    }
    onObjectEnd();
    if (_scanner.getToken() !== 2) {
      handleError(7, [
        2
        /* SyntaxKind.CloseBraceToken */
      ], []);
    } else {
      scanNext();
    }
    return true;
  }
  function parseArray() {
    onArrayBegin();
    scanNext();
    let isFirstElement = true;
    let needsComma = false;
    while (_scanner.getToken() !== 4 && _scanner.getToken() !== 17) {
      if (_scanner.getToken() === 5) {
        if (!needsComma) {
          handleError(4, [], []);
        }
        onSeparator(",");
        scanNext();
        if (_scanner.getToken() === 4 && allowTrailingComma) {
          break;
        }
      } else if (needsComma) {
        handleError(6, [], []);
      }
      if (isFirstElement) {
        _jsonPath.push(0);
        isFirstElement = false;
      } else {
        _jsonPath[_jsonPath.length - 1]++;
      }
      if (!parseValue()) {
        handleError(4, [], [
          4,
          5
          /* SyntaxKind.CommaToken */
        ]);
      }
      needsComma = true;
    }
    onArrayEnd();
    if (!isFirstElement) {
      _jsonPath.pop();
    }
    if (_scanner.getToken() !== 4) {
      handleError(8, [
        4
        /* SyntaxKind.CloseBracketToken */
      ], []);
    } else {
      scanNext();
    }
    return true;
  }
  function parseValue() {
    switch (_scanner.getToken()) {
      case 3:
        return parseArray();
      case 1:
        return parseObject();
      case 10:
        return parseString(true);
      default:
        return parseLiteral();
    }
  }
  scanNext();
  if (_scanner.getToken() === 17) {
    if (options.allowEmptyContent) {
      return true;
    }
    handleError(4, [], []);
    return false;
  }
  if (!parseValue()) {
    handleError(4, [], []);
    return false;
  }
  if (_scanner.getToken() !== 17) {
    handleError(9, [], []);
  }
  return true;
}
function getNodeType(value) {
  switch (typeof value) {
    case "boolean":
      return "boolean";
    case "number":
      return "number";
    case "string":
      return "string";
    case "object": {
      if (!value) {
        return "null";
      } else if (Array.isArray(value)) {
        return "array";
      }
      return "object";
    }
    default:
      return "null";
  }
}

function withFormatting(text2, edit2, options) {

    return [edit2];
  }

    while (begin > 0 && !isEOL(newText, begin - 1)) {
      begin--;

    while (end < newText.length && !isEOL(newText, end)) {
      end++;
    }
  }
  const edits = format(newText, { offset: begin, length: end - begin }, { ...options.formattingOptions, keepLines: false });
  for (let i2 = edits.length - 1; i2 >= 0; i2--) {
    const edit3 = edits[i2];
    newText = applyEdit(newText, edit3);
    begin = Math.min(begin, edit3.offset);
    end = Math.max(end, edit3.offset + edit3.length);
    end += edit3.content.length - edit3.length;
  }
  const editLength = text2.length - (newText.length - end) - begin;
  return [{ offset: begin, length: editLength, content: newText.substring(begin, end) }];
}
function applyEdit(text2, edit2) {

function applyEdits(text2, edits) {

    const diff = a2.offset - b2.offset;
    if (diff === 0) {

    }
    return diff;
  });

      text2 = applyEdit(text2, e2);
    } else {
      throw new Error("Overlapping edit");
    }
    lastModifiedOffset = e2.offset;
  }
  return text2;
}

const nested = (path, value) => path.reduceRight((inner, key) => ({ [key]: inner }), value);
function merge(into, value) {
  if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) return into;
  for (const [key, inner] of Object.entries(value)) {
    const current = into[key];
    if (Array.isArray(current) && Array.isArray(inner)) into[key] = [...current, ...inner];
    else if (current && typeof current === "object" && inner && typeof inner === "object" && !Array.isArray(inner))
      into[key] = merge({ ...current }, inner);
    else into[key] = inner;
  }
  return into;
}

function settle(child, timeoutMs, running2) {

      resolve2(code2);
    };

        if (child.pid && process.platform !== "win32") process.kill(-child.pid, name);
        else child.kill(name);
      } catch {
      }
    };
    const stop = () => {
      signal("SIGTERM");
      setTimeout(() => signal("SIGKILL"), 2e3).unref?.();
      finish(null);
    };
    const deadline = setTimeout(stop, timeoutMs);

              );
