<file path="plans/SIGNAL_BASED_SUGGESTIONS_V1.md">
# Signal-Based Suggestions V1 — Implementation Plan

> Status: in progress. This file is the working plan for the feature. The
> product spec is reproduced at the bottom (verbatim) under **Appendix: Spec**.
> The sections above it describe **how we are actually building it** in this
> codebase and the decisions that shaped the first testable pass.

## Goal (for this pass)

Finish a slice that the user can **run with `pnpm dev` and inspect quickly**.
The whole pipeline is wired with **real local-harness calls** (Claude / Codex
CLI), and progress is observable so a multi-minute run isn't a black box.

### Decisions locked with the user
- **Real harness calls are fine even if slow.** No mocking of the CLI on the
  real path. (A `fixture` adapter still exists as a selectable, instant option
  for sanity-checking the UI without burning CLI time — it implements the same
  adapter contract.)
- **Trigger = a Dev "Run now" button** that lets the user **pick which
  conversation** to analyze (maps to the spec's `insights:runForConversation`).
  The automatic 10-minute-inactivity trigger is also wired but is not the
  primary way to test.
- **Show progress on the Dev page**: current stage, run status, and harness
  stdout/stderr snippets, updated live as the run advances.
- **Single-conversation promotion behind a dev flag** so one Run-now actually
  produces a visible suggestion. The spec forbids single-conversation promotion
  in normal V1 and explicitly allows it behind a dev/debug flag — this is that
  flag, default ON in dev.

## How it maps onto the existing app

- **DB**: SQLite behind `@blume/storage-port` / `@blume/storage-sqlite`.
  Historical desktop migrations are package-owned by `@blume/storage-sqlite`;
  Improve row DTOs and persistence live in the shared storage packages.
- **Conversation data**: read via `getTranscript(ref)` / `listEventsForConversation`
  (`src/main/conversations`). Transcript hash computed locally (not stored on
  the conversations row).
- **Harness spawn**: re-implements the reference worktree's untracked
  `runPrompt.ts` skeleton — `spawn('/bin/zsh', ['-lc', cmd])`, prompt written to
  a temp file and redirected to stdin, stdout/stderr to temp files,
  SIGTERM→SIGKILL timeout. Adds strict-JSON parsing + secret-scrubbed env, which
  the reference did not have. (See "Electron spawn EBADF" project memo — login
  shell + `stdio:'ignore'` + temp-file redirect is required in the packaged app.)
- **IPC**: `handleIpc('insights:…')` in `src/main/index.ts`; preload wrappers in
  `src/preload/index.ts`; `Api` contract in `src/preload/index.d.ts`; renderer
  calls `window.api.*`. Progress is pushed over a `insights:progress` channel
  (mirrors `conversations:changed` + `onConversationsChanged`).
- **UI**: new top-level **Suggestions** tab (`MainTab 'suggestions'`, route
  `/suggestions`) rendered by `SuggestionsView.tsx`, styled with the existing
  `Card` / `Button` primitives. Dev diagnostics live as a new page inside
  `DevView.tsx`.
- **Web Lab parity**: every new shared host capability is implemented through
  both Electron and Web Lab adapters so the same shared UI can test it.

## Legacy module layout sketch

```
src/main/insights/
  types.ts            # Signal, SuggestionOperation, Suggestion, adapter contract, progress events
  config.ts           # promotion thresholds + dev flags (constants)
  packet.ts           # build cleaned conversation packet + synthetic filtering + transcript hash
  setup context       # capped, read-only setup context (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, rule files)
  prompts.ts          # the 3 prompt templates (extraction / clustering / planning)
  retrieval.ts        # recall-oriented candidate-cluster retrieval
  promotion.ts        # threshold evaluation
  apply.ts            # base-hash check + create/update/remove guidance files
  pipeline.ts         # orchestrator: runForConversation(...) + progress emitter
  queue.ts            # bounded (concurrency 1) run queue + dedupe by transcript hash + inactivity scan
  harness/
    adapter.ts        # InsightHarnessAdapter type + registry + JSON extraction helpers
    runProcess.ts     # zsh -lc spawn + temp-file redirect + timeout (ported skeleton)
    claude.ts         # claude --print … adapter
    codex.ts          # codex exec … adapter
    fixture.ts        # deterministic instant adapter (dev/testing)
    index.ts          # getAdapter(harnessId), listAvailableAdapters()
  index.ts            # public surface used by IPC layer

packages/storage/sqlite/src/desktopMigrations.ts
packages/storage/sqlite/src/desktopImprove.ts

src/renderer/src/SuggestionsView.tsx
src/renderer/src/components/insights/SuggestionCard.tsx
src/renderer/src/components/insights/InsightsDevPanel.tsx   # picker + run now + progress + diagnostics
```

This sketch predates the shared-product migration. Most product modules listed
above now live in `@blume/app-core` or shared domain packages; desktop main keeps
only native adapter composition.

## Pipeline stages (and the progress events they emit)

`runForConversation({ conversationId | ref, harnessId, dev })`:

1. `queued` → `building-packet`: build conversation packet (synthetic-filtered),
   setup context, metadata; compute `transcript_hash`. Dedupe: skip if a
   completed run exists for `conversation_id + transcript_hash` (unless forced).
2. `extracting`: harness call #1 (extraction prompt). Store every valid signal,
   including weak one-offs. Record an `insight_runs` row with stdout/stderr
   snippets and timing.
3. `retrieving`: local candidate-cluster retrieval (≤25) — exact key, shared
   command/path/code tokens, shared setup refs, lexical overlap; project/scope/
   harness as boosts.
4. `clustering`: harness call #2 (batch clustering). Assign each new signal once;
   create/extend clusters; record duplicate-cluster candidates.
5. `promoting`: recompute cluster stats; evaluate thresholds (dev flag allows
   single-conversation promotion).
6. `planning`: harness call #3 per newly-promoted cluster (capped; the cap is
   logged, never silent). Store suggestions with operations + patch previews +
   base hashes.
7. `done` (or `failed` with an error snippet).

Each transition is persisted on the run row **and** pushed to the renderer over
`insights:progress` so the Dev page updates live.

## Harness adapter contract (as built)

```ts
type InsightHarnessAdapter = {
  harnessId: string                       // 'claude' | 'codex' | 'fixture'
  label: string
  isAvailable(): Promise<boolean>
  runJsonAnalysis(input: {
    prompt: string
    schemaName: string                    // which stage (for fixture + logging)
    cwd: string
    timeoutMs: number
  }): Promise<{
    json: unknown
    stdoutSnippet: string
    stderrSnippet: string
    exitCode: number | null
    durationMs: number
  }>
}
```

CLI flags (from the reference runner):
- Claude one-shot: `claude --print --output-format text --model opus` (prompt
  on stdin; we parse strict JSON out of the text, tolerating ```json fences).
- Codex one-shot: `codex exec --color never --skip-git-repo-check
  --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules -m gpt-5-codex -`.
- Env is scrubbed (drop `*KEY*`, `*TOKEN*`, `*SECRET*`, `*PASSWORD*`,
  `*COOKIE*`, AWS creds, etc.) before spawn; output snippets are capped.

## IPC surface

```
insights:listSuggestions()                       -> Suggestion list (UI cards)
insights:listSignals({ conversationId? })        -> signals (diagnostics)
insights:listClusters({ status? })               -> clusters + promotion progress (diagnostics)
insights:listDuplicateClusters()                 -> duplicate-cluster candidates (diagnostics)
insights:listRuns({ limit? })                    -> recent runs (diagnostics)
insights:runForConversation({ ref, harnessId, dev }) -> run id (async; progress via channel)
insights:applySuggestion({ id })                 -> { status: 'applied' | 'needs_review' | ... }
insights:snoozeSuggestion({ id, until? })
insights:dismissSuggestion({ id })
insights:archiveSuggestion({ id })
insights:listHarnesses()                         -> [{ harnessId, label, available }]
insights:onProgress(cb)                          -> subscription (unsubscribe fn)
```

## Suggestions tab (what the user sees)
- Card per suggestion: title, summary, the files/artifacts it changes, planned
  operations + patch preview, artifact scope + harness applicability.
- **Apply / Snooze / Dismiss** buttons.
- **See evidence** from the preview page: users can inspect the raw captured
  excerpts that caused a suggestion, with conversation/project/date context.
- Empty state explains how to generate suggestions (Dev → Insights → Run now).

## Dev page (Insights)
- Conversation picker (recent conversations), harness picker (claude/codex/
  fixture, with availability), **Run now**.
- Live progress: stage, status, elapsed, last stdout/stderr snippet.
- Diagnostics: recent runs; clusters with progress-toward-promotion; signals for
  the selected conversation; duplicate-cluster candidates. Raw harness traces
  stay here.

## Test plan for this pass (manual, fast)
1. `pnpm dev`. Confirm the **Suggestions** tab appears and shows the empty state.
2. Open **Dev → Insights**. Pick a recent conversation. Pick the **fixture**
   harness first → **Run now**: progress should march through the stages in ~a
   second and a suggestion should appear in the Suggestions tab. This proves the
   whole pipeline + UI without waiting on a CLI.
3. Switch the harness to **claude** (or codex) → **Run now** on a real
   conversation: watch the live progress through extraction → clustering →
   planning (minutes), then a real suggestion lands.
4. On a suggestion, click **Apply** → confirm the target guidance file is
   written (or `needs_review` if the base hash no longer matches), **Snooze** →
   it hides, **Dismiss** → it hides and is suppressed.

Automated tests (`__test/regressions/insights.test.ts`, 15 cases) cover the
riskiest DB-free logic: untrusted-harness-JSON extraction (`extractJson`),
the extraction/planning validators (`parseExtraction`/`parsePlanning`), and the
all-or-nothing Apply with its base-hash safety (applies on match, `needs_review`
without overwrite on mismatch, create/remove). `db-migrations.test.ts` is
updated for schema v9. The DB-dependent fixtures from the spec's Test Plan
(synthetic filtering, retrieval overlap, promotion thresholds) are deferred:
those modules import the repository layer, and `better-sqlite3` is built for
Electron's ABI, so they need an Electron test runner or a thin DB seam — tracked
as a follow-up.

## Deviations from the spec (called out)
- `fixture` harness adapter added (not in spec) purely as a fast/deterministic
  dev path; the real Claude/Codex adapters are the spec's "initial
  implementations."
- `SuggestionOperation` carries an internal `newContent?` field (used by Apply
  to write the resulting file) in addition to the spec's human-facing
  `patchPreview`. Apply needs concrete bytes; the diff stays for display.
- Dev single-conversation promotion flag defaults ON in dev so a single Run-now
  yields a suggestion. Thresholds for "normal" promotion are unchanged config
  constants.
- Planning is capped to a small number of promoted clusters per run in dev; the
  cap is logged, not silent.

## Planner guidance (artifact-selection rubric)

Suggestions must not default to "rule" artifacts — rules (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md /
Cursor "Always") are loaded into an agent's context on **every turn**, so
overusing them is a standing context tax. The planner is steered by an editable
guidance doc that encodes a context-cost ladder and a per-signal-kind rubric:

- **Ladder (cheapest → most expensive):** hook (zero context, deterministic) ▸
  doc (read on demand) ▸ skill (name+description always on; body on trigger —
  "progressive disclosure") ▸ rule/memory (always on). Default bias is *down* the
  ladder; land on a rule only when the guidance is short and needed every turn.
- Mapping examples: `permission` → hook (enforced, not advisory); `workflow` →
  skill; `domain` → doc/skill reference; `command` → hook if it must run, else a
  short AGENTS.md line; `preference` → skill if situational, rule only if
  universal+short.
- Operation bias: prefer `update` over `create`; `remove` stale/conflicting
  guidance; keep rule edits tiny.

Mechanism (the "how we use it"):
- Default lives in the repo at `packages/app/core/src/features/improve/defaultPlanningGuidance.ts`.
  A per-machine override can be written to
  `<blumeRoot>/insights/planning-guidance.md` (`getPlanningGuidance()` prefers it).
- It is injected **only** into the planning prompt as a `<planning_guidance>`
  block (`buildPlanningPrompt`) — it is never installed into a project or loaded
  into any analyzed agent's runtime context. This is the key distinction: it's
  authoring-time guidance for the suggestion *generator*, not a runtime rule.
- Inspectable in **Dev → Insights → Planning guidance** (shows the active text +
  the override path), via `insights:getPlanningGuidance`.
- Grounded in current (2026) docs: Claude Code memory/skills/hooks loading
  semantics, Cursor rule types (Always/Auto-Attached/Agent-Requested/Manual), and
  the AGENTS.md standard (progressive disclosure; pair every "don't" with a "do").

---

## Appendix: Spec

(The full product spec as provided is the source of truth for behavior; this
plan implements it with the deviations noted above. See the original task
description for the complete prompt templates, data model, promotion rules,
public interfaces, queue behavior, and test plan.)

<file path="scripts/dev-account-session-helper.cjs">
const { readFileSync } = require('node:fs')
const { DatabaseSync } = require('node:sqlite')
const { app, safeStorage } = require('electron')

const ACCOUNT_SETTING_PREFIX = 'account.'
const ENC_PREFIX = 'enc:v1:'
const MAX_ACCOUNT_SETTINGS = 32
const MAX_ACCOUNT_SETTING_LENGTH = 1_000_000

const mode = process.argv[2]
const appName = process.argv[3]
app.setName(appName)

function validSettings(value) {
  if (!Array.isArray(value) || value.length > MAX_ACCOUNT_SETTINGS) {
    throw new Error('Invalid account session payload')
  }
  return value.map((entry) => {
    if (
      !entry ||
      typeof entry !== 'object' ||
      typeof entry.key !== 'string' ||
      !entry.key.startsWith(ACCOUNT_SETTING_PREFIX) ||
      typeof entry.value !== 'string' ||
      entry.value.length > MAX_ACCOUNT_SETTING_LENGTH
    ) {
      throw new Error('Invalid account session setting')
    }
    return { key: entry.key, value: entry.value }
  })
}

function readEncryptedSettings(dbPath) {
  let db
  try {
    db = new DatabaseSync(dbPath, { readOnly: true })
    return validSettings(
      db
        .prepare(
          `SELECT key, value FROM settings
           WHERE key LIKE 'account.%' AND value != ''
           ORDER BY key
           LIMIT ${MAX_ACCOUNT_SETTINGS + 1}`
        )
        .all()
    )
  } finally {
    db?.close()
  }
}

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  try {
    if (!safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) {
      throw new Error('OS secure storage is unavailable')
    }
    if (mode === 'decrypt') {
      const settings = readEncryptedSettings(process.argv[4]).map(({ key, value }) => {
        if (!value.startsWith(ENC_PREFIX)) throw new Error('Account setting is not encrypted')
        return {
          key,
          value: safeStorage.decryptString(Buffer.from(value.slice(ENC_PREFIX.length), 'base64'))
        }
      })
      process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(settings))
    } else if (mode === 'encrypt') {
      const settings = validSettings(JSON.parse(readFileSync(0, 'utf8'))).map(({ key, value }) => ({
        key,
        value: ENC_PREFIX + safeStorage.encryptString(value).toString('base64')
      }))
      process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(settings))
    } else {
      throw new Error('Unknown account session helper mode')
    }
    app.quit()
  } catch (error) {
    process.stderr.write(`${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}\n`)
    app.exit(1)
  }
})

<file path="scripts/dev-account-session.mjs">
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite'
import { join } from 'node:path'

const ACCOUNT_COOKIE_KEY = 'account.blume-account.cookie'

export function devAccountSessionDatabaseCandidates({ homeDir, stableDbPath }) {
  return [
    { source: 'stable', dbPath: stableDbPath ?? join(homeDir, '.blume', 'blume.sqlite') },
    { source: 'canary', dbPath: join(homeDir, '.blume', '.canary', 'blume.sqlite') }
  ]
}

function hasAccountSession(dbPath) {
  if (!existsSync(dbPath)) return false
  let db
  try {
    db = new DatabaseSync(dbPath, { readOnly: true })
    const hasSettings = db
      .prepare("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'settings'")
      .get()
    if (!hasSettings) return false
    const row = db
      .prepare('SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = ? AND value != ? LIMIT 1')
      .get(ACCOUNT_COOKIE_KEY, '')
    return typeof row?.value === 'string' && row.value.length > 0
  } catch {
    return false
  } finally {
    db?.close()
  }
}

export function findDevAccountSessionSource(candidates) {
  return candidates.find((candidate) => hasAccountSession(candidate.dbPath)) ?? null
}

export async function validateDevAccountSession(settings, authUrl, fetchImpl = fetch) {
  const cookie = settings.find(
    (entry) => entry?.key === ACCOUNT_COOKIE_KEY && typeof entry.value === 'string'
  )?.value
  if (!cookie) return 'invalid'

  try {
    const response = await fetchImpl(`${authUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '')}/api/auth/get-session`, {
      headers: { Cookie: cookie },
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3_000)
    })
    if (!response.ok) return 'unknown'
    const body = await response.json().catch(() => null)
    return body?.session && body?.user ? 'authenticated' : 'invalid'
  } catch {
    // Offline development should still inherit a locally present session. The
    // account client will validate it when the service becomes reachable.
    return 'unknown'
  }
}

<file path="scripts/dev-label.mjs">
/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/explicit-function-return-type */

import { existsSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs'
import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite'
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'

const CONVERSATION_TITLE_FLAGS = ['--conversation-title', '--conversation']
const REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT_FLAG = '--remoteDebuggingPort'
const DEV_PROFILE_FLAG = '--profile'
const DEV_PROFILES = new Set(['full', 'ui', 'conversations', 'native'])
const STATIC_RUNNER_FLAGS = new Set(['--static', '--no-hmr'])
const SIGNED_OUT_FLAG = '--signed-out'

function normalizeDevProfile(value) {
  const profile = value?.trim() || 'full'
  if (!DEV_PROFILES.has(profile)) {
    throw new Error(`${DEV_PROFILE_FLAG} must be one of: ${[...DEV_PROFILES].join(', ')}`)
  }
  return profile
}
function normalizeRemoteDebuggingPort(value) {
  const trimmed = value?.trim()
  if (!trimmed || !/^\d+$/.test(trimmed)) return null
  const port = Number(trimmed)
  return Number.isSafeInteger(port) && port >= 1 && port <= 65_535 ? port : null
}

export function readRemoteDebuggingPortParameter(args) {
  let port = null
  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index += 1) {
    const argument = args[index]
    if (argument === REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT_FLAG) {
      const parsed = normalizeRemoteDebuggingPort(args[index + 1])
      if (parsed !== null) port = parsed
      index += 1
      continue
    }
    if (argument.startsWith(`${REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT_FLAG}=`)) {
      const parsed = normalizeRemoteDebuggingPort(
        argument.slice(REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT_FLAG.length + 1)
      )
      if (parsed !== null) port = parsed
    }
  }
  return port
}

/**
 * Keep launcher-only identity flags out of electron-vite while forwarding its
 * own CLI options (for example `--remoteDebuggingPort 9223`). This lets CDP
 * runs use the normal launcher, including DB-backed task labels, parser prep,
 * native dependency rebuilds, sandbox selection, and process cleanup.
 */
export function parseDevLauncherArguments(args, env = process.env) {
  let conversationTitle = null
  let runtimeProfile = null
  let runnerMode = env.BLUME_DEV_RUNNER?.trim() === 'static' ? 'static' : 'hmr'
  let signedOut = env.BLUME_DEV_SIGNED_OUT === '1'
  const electronViteArgs = []

  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index += 1) {
    const argument = args[index]
    if (index === 0 && argument === '--') continue
    if (STATIC_RUNNER_FLAGS.has(argument)) {
      runnerMode = 'static'
      continue
    }
    if (argument === DEV_PROFILE_FLAG) {
      const value = args[index + 1]?.trim()
      if (!value || value.startsWith('--')) {
        throw new Error(`${DEV_PROFILE_FLAG} requires a non-empty profile`)
      }
      runtimeProfile = normalizeDevProfile(value)
      index += 1
      continue
    }
    if (argument.startsWith(`${DEV_PROFILE_FLAG}=`)) {
      const value = argument.slice(DEV_PROFILE_FLAG.length + 1).trim()
      if (!value) throw new Error(`${DEV_PROFILE_FLAG} requires a non-empty profile`)
      runtimeProfile = normalizeDevProfile(value)
      continue
    }
    if (argument === SIGNED_OUT_FLAG) {
      signedOut = true
      continue
    }
    let matchedTitleFlag = false
    for (const flag of CONVERSATION_TITLE_FLAGS) {
      if (argument === flag) {
        const value = args[index + 1]?.trim()
        if (!value || value.startsWith('--')) {
          throw new Error(`${flag} requires a non-empty title`)
        }
        if (conversationTitle === null) conversationTitle = value
        index += 1
        matchedTitleFlag = true
        break
      }
      if (argument.startsWith(`${flag}=`)) {
        const value = argument.slice(flag.length + 1).trim()
        if (!value) throw new Error(`${flag} requires a non-empty title`)
        if (conversationTitle === null) conversationTitle = value
        matchedTitleFlag = true
        break
      }
    }
    if (!matchedTitleFlag) electronViteArgs.push(argument)
  }

  return {
    conversationTitle: conversationTitle ?? (env.BLUME_DEV_CONVERSATION_TITLE?.trim() || null),
    runtimeProfile: runtimeProfile ?? normalizeDevProfile(env.BLUME_DEV_PROFILE),
    runnerMode,
    signedOut,
    electronViteArgs,
    cdpPort: readRemoteDebuggingPortParameter(electronViteArgs)
  }
}

export function readConversationTitleParameter(args, env = process.env) {
  return parseDevLauncherArguments(args, env).conversationTitle
}

export function devRunnerArguments(runnerMode, electronViteArgs) {
  if (runnerMode !== 'static') return ['dev', ...electronViteArgs]
  const previewArgs = ['preview', '--skipBuild']
  for (let index = 0; index < electronViteArgs.length; index += 1) {
    const argument = electronViteArgs[index]
    if (argument === REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT_FLAG) {
      index += 1
      continue
    }
    if (argument.startsWith(`${REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT_FLAG}=`)) continue
    previewArgs.push(argument)
  }
  return previewArgs
}

export function resolveLaunchPath(value) {
  const absolute = resolve(value)
  if (!existsSync(absolute)) return absolute.replace(/\\/g, '/')
  return realpathSync.native(absolute).replace(/\\/g, '/')
}

export function devSandboxSlug(appPath) {
  return appPath.replace(/^\//, '').replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+/g, '_')
}

/**
 * Ordered databases used only to discover the label for a dev launch. Packaged
 * canary is checked before stable because it is where the active task is most
 * likely to have been ingested, while the checkout's own dev sandbox is the
 * final fallback for a conversation that has only been seen by that worktree.
 */
export function devLabelDatabaseCandidates({ homeDir, devAppPath, stableDbPath }) {
  const blumeRoot = join(homeDir, '.blume')
  return [
    { source: 'canary', dbPath: join(blumeRoot, '.canary', 'blume.sqlite') },
    { source: 'stable', dbPath: stableDbPath ?? join(blumeRoot, 'blume.sqlite') },
    {
      source: 'dev-worktree',
      dbPath: join(blumeRoot, '.dev', devSandboxSlug(devAppPath), 'blume.sqlite')
    }
  ]
}

export function inferWorktreeName(path) {
  const normalized = path.replace(/\\/g, '/')
  const codex = normalized.match(/\/(?:\.codex)\/worktrees\/([^/]+)(?:\/|$)/)
  if (codex?.[1]) return codex[1]
  const harness = normalized.match(
    /\/(?:\.claude|\.cursor|\.pi|\.omp)\/(?:worktrees|workspaces|worktree)\/([^/]+)(?:\/|$)/
  )
  return harness?.[1] ?? null
}

export function findConversationForWorkingDirectory({ dbPath, workingDirectory }) {
  if (!existsSync(dbPath)) {
    return { error: `main Blume database not found at ${dbPath}` }
  }
  let db
  try {
    db = new DatabaseSync(dbPath, { readOnly: true })
    const normalizedCwd = "replace(coalesce(cwd, ''), '\\', '/')"
    const row = db
      .prepare(
        `SELECT coalesce(nullif(trim(title), ''), nullif(trim(provider_title), '')) AS conversation_name,
              workspace, workspace_kind
         FROM conversations
         WHERE (thread_source IS NULL OR thread_source NOT IN ('subagent', 'guardian_review'))
           AND (${normalizedCwd} = ?
                OR (${normalizedCwd} != '' AND substr(${normalizedCwd}, 1, length(?) + 1) = ? || '/'))
         ORDER BY CASE WHEN ${normalizedCwd} = ? THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
                  last_activity_ts DESC
         LIMIT 1`
      )
      .get(workingDirectory, workingDirectory, workingDirectory, workingDirectory)
    if (!row) {
      return {
        error: `no user-owned conversation has working directory ${workingDirectory} in the main Blume database`
      }
    }
    const conversationName = String(row.conversation_name ?? '').trim()
    if (!conversationName) {
      return {
        error: `the latest user-owned conversation for ${workingDirectory} does not have a title yet`
      }
    }
    return {
      conversationName,
      worktreeName:
        row.workspace_kind && String(row.workspace ?? '').trim()
          ? String(row.workspace).trim()
          : null
    }
  } catch (error) {
    return { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) }
  } finally {
    db?.close()
  }
}

export function resolveDevLabel({ dbCandidates, launchPath, workingDirectory, conversationTitle }) {
  if (conversationTitle) {
    return {
      conversationName: conversationTitle,
      worktreeName: inferWorktreeName(launchPath),
      source: 'parameter',
      error: null
    }
  }

  const failures = []
  for (const candidate of dbCandidates) {
    const conversation = findConversationForWorkingDirectory({
      dbPath: candidate.dbPath,
      workingDirectory
    })
    if (!('error' in conversation)) {
      return {
        conversationName: conversation.conversationName,
        worktreeName: conversation.worktreeName || inferWorktreeName(launchPath),
        source: candidate.source,
        error: null
      }
    }
    failures.push(`${candidate.source}: ${conversation.error}`)
  }

  return {
    conversationName: null,
    worktreeName: inferWorktreeName(launchPath),
    source: 'missing',
    error: `${failures.join('; ')}. Start with --conversation-title "<conversation name>". Choose a short, descriptive title for the work being done.`
  }
}

<file path="scripts/dev-process-guard.mjs">
/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/explicit-function-return-type */
// Process bookkeeping for `pnpm dev`: which wrapper owns a checkout's dev app, which Electron
// processes are true strays, and a durable record of why a dev app stopped.
//
// Every `pnpm dev` wrapper claims apps/desktop/.dev/dev.pid in its own checkout while it runs.
// The claim is per checkout, not per HOME, so a fresh-home run and a normal run of the same
// checkout still see each other. A recorded pid counts only while that process runs
// `scripts/dev.mjs` from this checkout's apps/desktop, so a stale or reused pid owns nothing.
// Electron processes that descend from another live wrapper are never strays. Each signal or exit
// is appended to dev-exits.log in the dev sandbox, so the next unexpected quit names its cause.
import { execFileSync, execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import {
  appendFileSync,
  closeSync,
  linkSync,
  mkdirSync,
  openSync,
  readFileSync,
  rmSync,
  statSync,
  writeFileSync
} from 'node:fs'
import { homedir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'

import { devSandboxSlug } from './dev-label.mjs'

export const WRAPPER_MARKER = 'scripts/dev.mjs'

/** The checkout's dev sandbox directory (~/.blume/.dev/<slug>), where logs are kept. */
export function devSandboxDir(projectRoot, home = homedir()) {
  return join(home, '.blume', '.dev', devSandboxSlug(projectRoot))
}

/** The per-checkout ownership record, independent of HOME. */
export function wrapperRecordPath(projectRoot) {
  return join(projectRoot, '.dev', 'dev.pid')
}

/** The marker the wrapper writes once electron-vite is running. */
export function launchedRecordPath(projectRoot) {
  return join(projectRoot, '.dev', 'dev.launched')
}

/** Parse `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,command=` into a pid → { ppid, command } map. */
export function parseProcessTable(output) {
  const table = new Map()
  for (const line of output.split('\n')) {
    const match = line.match(/^\s*(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(.*)$/)
    if (match) table.set(Number(match[1]), { ppid: Number(match[2]), command: match[3] })
  }
  return table
}

export function readProcessTable() {
  try {
    return parseProcessTable(execSync('ps -axo pid=,ppid=,command=', { encoding: 'utf-8' }))
  } catch {
    return new Map()
  }
}

/** A process's working directory, or undefined when it cannot be read. */
export function processCwd(pid) {
  try {
    const out = execFileSync('lsof', ['-a', '-p', String(pid), '-d', 'cwd', '-Fn'], {
      encoding: 'utf-8',
      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore']
    })
    const line = out.split('\n').find((entry) => entry.startsWith('n'))
    return line ? line.slice(1) : undefined
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

/**
 * Whether `pid` is a live dev wrapper of this checkout: it runs `scripts/dev.mjs` and its working
 * directory is this checkout's apps/desktop. An unreadable working directory counts as live, so
 * the guard errs towards refusing and never towards killing.
 */
export function isLiveWrapper(pid, { projectRoot, table, cwdOf = processCwd }) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return false
  const entry = table.get(pid)
  if (!entry || !entry.command.includes(WRAPPER_MARKER)) return false
  const cwd = cwdOf(pid)
  return cwd === undefined || cwd === projectRoot
}

/** Whether `pid` is an ancestor of (or is) `descendant` in the table. */
function descendsFrom(descendant, pid, table) {
  const seen = new Set()
  for (
    let current = descendant;
    current && !seen.has(current);
    current = table.get(current)?.ppid
  ) {
    if (current === pid) return true
    seen.add(current)
  }
  return false
}

/**
 * Split this checkout's Electron processes into strays (safe to kill) and ones owned by another
 * live wrapper (never killed). Matching is unchanged from before: the command line must reference
 * this checkout's app path.
 */
export function classifyElectronProcesses(table, { projectRoot, selfPid, ownerPid }) {
  const strays = []
  const owned = []
  for (const [pid, { command }] of table) {
    if (pid === selfPid) continue
    if (!command.includes(projectRoot) || !/Electron(\.app|\s+Helper)/.test(command)) continue
    if (ownerPid && descendsFrom(pid, ownerPid, table)) owned.push({ pid, command })
    else strays.push({ pid, command })
  }
  return { strays, owned }
}

function readPid(path) {
  try {
    const pid = Number(readFileSync(path, 'utf8').trim())
    return Number.isInteger(pid) && pid > 0 ? pid : null
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

export function readRecordedWrapper(projectRoot) {
  return readPid(wrapperRecordPath(projectRoot))
}

/** The live wrapper recorded for this checkout, unless it is `selfPid`. */
export function liveWrapper(projectRoot, { selfPid, table = readProcessTable(), cwdOf } = {}) {
  const pid = readRecordedWrapper(projectRoot)
  if (pid === null || pid === selfPid) return null
  return isLiveWrapper(pid, { projectRoot, table, cwdOf }) ? pid : null
}

// Replacing a stale record takes milliseconds, so a reclaim lock older than this was left by a
// killed wrapper.
const RECLAIM_LOCK_STALE_MS = 10_000

/**
 * Remove a stale record under a short reclaim lock, re-reading it first: only a wrapper holding
 * the lock removes a record, and a live owner's record is never removed by anyone but that owner,
 * so the re-read cannot go stale before the removal.
 */
function reclaimStale(projectRoot, { table, cwdOf }) {
  const path = wrapperRecordPath(projectRoot)
  const lock = `${path}.reclaim`
  let fd
  try {
    fd = openSync(lock, 'wx')
  } catch (error) {
    if (error?.code !== 'EEXIST') throw error
    try {
      if (Date.now() - statSync(lock).mtimeMs > RECLAIM_LOCK_STALE_MS) rmSync(lock, { force: true })
    } catch {
      /* already gone */
    }
    return
  }
  try {
    const owner = readPid(path)
    if (owner === null || !isLiveWrapper(owner, { projectRoot, table, cwdOf }))
      rmSync(path, { force: true })
  } finally {
    closeSync(fd)
    rmSync(lock, { force: true })
  }
}

/**
 * Atomically claim this checkout's dev app for `pid`. A record whose process is not a live
 * wrapper of this checkout is replaced under the reclaim lock; a live one is returned as the owner
 * and left alone.
 */
export function claimWrapper(projectRoot, pid, { table = readProcessTable(), cwdOf } = {}) {
  const path = wrapperRecordPath(projectRoot)
  mkdirSync(join(projectRoot, '.dev'), { recursive: true })
  const pending = `${path}.${pid}`
  writeFileSync(pending, `${pid}\n`)
  try {
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 20; attempt += 1) {
      try {
        // link() fails if a record exists, so two wrappers cannot both create it.
        linkSync(pending, path)
        return { ok: true }
      } catch (error) {
        if (error?.code !== 'EEXIST') throw error
        const owner = readPid(path)
        if (owner === pid) return { ok: true }
        if (owner !== null && isLiveWrapper(owner, { projectRoot, table, cwdOf }))
          return { ok: false, owner }
        reclaimStale(projectRoot, { table, cwdOf })
        Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, 25)
      }
    }
    return { ok: false, owner: readPid(path) }
  } finally {
    rmSync(pending, { force: true })
  }
}

/** Every live descendant of `pid` in the table, deepest first. */
export function descendantsOf(pid, table) {
  const children = new Map()
  for (const [child, { ppid }] of table) {
    if (!children.has(ppid)) children.set(ppid, [])
    children.get(ppid).push(child)
  }
  const out = []
  const walk = (parent) => {
    for (const child of children.get(parent) ?? []) {
      walk(child)
      out.push(child)
    }
  }
  walk(pid)
  return out
}

/** Remove the claim and launch marker only while they still name `pid`. */
export function releaseWrapper(projectRoot, pid) {
  if (readPid(launchedRecordPath(projectRoot)) === pid)
    rmSync(launchedRecordPath(projectRoot), { force: true })
  if (readRecordedWrapper(projectRoot) === pid)
    rmSync(wrapperRecordPath(projectRoot), { force: true })
}

export function markLaunched(projectRoot, pid) {
  writeFileSync(launchedRecordPath(projectRoot), `${pid}\n`)
}

export function readLaunched(projectRoot) {
  return readPid(launchedRecordPath(projectRoot))
}

/** Describe the parent process, so a signal record says who was above the wrapper. */
export function describeParent(table, ppid) {
  const parent = table.get(ppid)
  return parent ? `${ppid} ${parent.command.slice(0, 160)}` : `${ppid} (gone)`
}

/** Append one JSON line to dev-exits.log; bookkeeping must never break the dev run. */
export function appendExitRecord(sandboxDir, record) {
  try {
    mkdirSync(sandboxDir, { recursive: true })
    appendFileSync(
      join(sandboxDir, 'dev-exits.log'),
      `${JSON.stringify({ at: new Date().toISOString(), ...record })}\n`
    )
  } catch {
    /* best effort */
  }
}

<file path="scripts/dev.mjs">
#!/usr/bin/env node
/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/explicit-function-return-type */
// scripts/dev.mjs
//
// Wraps `electron-vite dev` so the macOS Dock entry never lingers after a
// dev session. The in-process JS handlers in src/main/index.ts cover graceful
// shutdown paths (SIGTERM/SIGINT/uncaught exceptions), but they can't catch
// SIGKILL or native crashes — and when Electron's main process dies that way,
// the renderer/GPU/Helper subprocesses survive and macOS keeps "Electron"
// pinned in the Dock until something kills them.
//
// This wrapper:
//   1. Sweeps stray Electron processes from prior dev runs of THIS project
//      before launching.
//   2. Forwards signals to the electron-vite child and re-sweeps on exit
//      so Ctrl+C / kill of `pnpm dev` always leaves a clean Dock.
//   3. Refuses to start while another `pnpm dev` of this checkout runs, never
//      kills that wrapper's app, and logs every signal and exit to
//      ~/.blume/.dev/<slug>/dev-exits.log (see dev-process-guard.mjs).
//
// Scoped by absolute project path, so it never touches Electron apps from
// unrelated checkouts/worktrees. To keep a dev app alive after the agent
// session or terminal that started it ends, use `pnpm dev:detached`.

import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { spawn, execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { existsSync, lstatSync, readFileSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { constants as osConstants, homedir } from 'node:os'
import { dirname, isAbsolute, join, resolve } from 'node:path'

import { replaceWorkspacePackageLink } from '../../../scripts/link-workspace-packages.mjs'
import { findWorkspacePackages } from '../../../scripts/workspace-packages.mjs'
import {
  devLabelDatabaseCandidates,
  devRunnerArguments,

  resolveDevLabel,
  resolveLaunchPath
} from './dev-label.mjs'
import { applyPullRequestPreviewEnvironment } from './previewEnvironment.mjs'
import { configureRecordedLedger } from './recordedLedgerEnvironment.mjs'

  appendExitRecord,
  claimWrapper,
  classifyElectronProcesses,
  describeParent,
  devSandboxDir,
  liveWrapper,
  markLaunched,
  readProcessTable,
  releaseWrapper
} from './dev-process-guard.mjs'
import {
  devAccountSessionDatabaseCandidates,
  findDevAccountSessionSource,
  validateDevAccountSession
} from './dev-account-session.mjs'

const projectRoot = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..')
const workspaceRoot = resolve(projectRoot, '../..')
const devSlug = devSandboxSlug(projectRoot)
const defaultElectronUserDataDir = join(homedir(), '.blume', '.dev', devSlug, 'electron-user-data')
const electronUserDataDir = process.env.ELECTRON_USER_DATA_DIR ?? defaultElectronUserDataDir

// Claim this checkout's dev app before anything else. A second `pnpm dev` of the same checkout
// (also one with another HOME) used to share its app and silently quit the first one's Electron
// in the stray sweep; now it refuses and says how to stop the running one.
const devSandbox = devSandboxDir(projectRoot)
const claim = claimWrapper(projectRoot, process.pid)
if (!claim.ok) {
  console.error(
    `[pre-dev] another pnpm dev (pid ${claim.owner}) is already running this checkout's dev app.\n` +
      `[pre-dev] Electron web tests and dev:e2e: run them from another worktree; do not stop that app, ` +
      `someone may be using it.\n` +
      `[pre-dev] Restarting your own app: stop it first (pnpm dev:detached --stop, or kill ${claim.owner}).`
  )
  process.exit(1)
}

// Every stop is recorded from here on, including signals and exits before Electron launches.
// SIGKILL cannot be observed; a missing record after a quit therefore means SIGKILL or a crash.
let child = null
let exitRecorded = false
function recordStop(reason) {
  if (exitRecorded) return
  exitRecorded = true
  appendExitRecord(devSandbox, {
    event: 'dev-stopped',
    ...reason,
    wrapperPid: process.pid,
    parent: describeParent(readProcessTable(), process.ppid)
  })
}
// A signal names who stopped the app: SIGHUP is a closed terminal or an ended session, SIGTERM a
// kill or a stopped preview server.
for (const signal of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) {
  process.on(signal, () => {
    console.warn(
      `[dev] received ${signal}; stopping the dev app (record in ${devSandbox}/dev-exits.log)`
    )
    if (child) void finalize(0, { signal })
    else {
      recordStop({ signal, phase: 'pre-launch' })
      process.exit(128 + (osConstants.signals[signal] ?? 0))
    }
  })
}
process.on('exit', (code) => {
  recordStop({ exitCode: code })
  releaseWrapper(projectRoot, process.pid)
})

function findPrimaryWorktreeRoot() {
  try {
    const out = execFileSync('git', ['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'], {
      cwd: workspaceRoot,
      encoding: 'utf8',
      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore']
    })
    for (const line of out.split(/\r?\n/)) {
      const match = line.match(/^worktree (.+)$/)
      if (match) return resolve(match[1])
    }
  } catch {
    /* Not a git checkout, or git is unavailable. */
  }
  return workspaceRoot
}

const primaryWorkspaceRoot = findPrimaryWorktreeRoot()

function findWorkspacePackageDirs() {
  const packages = findWorkspacePackages(
    ['packages', 'apps', 'services'].map((base) => join(workspaceRoot, base))
  )
  return new Map([...packages].map(([name, { dir }]) => [name, dir]))
}

function ensureWorkspacePackageLinks() {
  const nodeModules = join(workspaceRoot, 'node_modules')
  if (!existsSync(nodeModules)) {
    throw new Error('node_modules is missing; run pnpm install before pnpm dev')
  }
  if (lstatSync(nodeModules).isSymbolicLink()) {
    throw new Error(
      `node_modules is shared through a symlink (${realpathSync(nodeModules)}). ` +
        'Use a checkout-local pnpm install before running Electron from this worktree.'
    )
  }

  let repaired = 0
  for (const [name, packageDir] of findWorkspacePackageDirs()) {
    const linkPath = join(nodeModules, name)
    let currentTarget = null
    try {
      currentTarget = realpathSync(linkPath)
    } catch {
      /* missing or broken workspace link */
    }
    if (currentTarget === realpathSync(packageDir)) continue
    replaceWorkspacePackageLink(nodeModules, linkPath, packageDir)
    repaired += 1
  }
  if (repaired > 0) {
    console.log(`[pre-dev] repaired ${repaired} stale workspace package link(s)`)
  }
}

// Electron processes of this checkout, split into true strays and ones that belong to another
// live `pnpm dev` (another session's app). Only strays are ever killed, loudly.
async function killStrays(label) {
  const table = readProcessTable()
  const ownerPid = liveWrapper(projectRoot, { selfPid: process.pid, table })
  const { strays, owned } = classifyElectronProcesses(table, {
    projectRoot,
    selfPid: process.pid,
    ownerPid
  })
  if (owned.length > 0)
    console.warn(
      `[${label}] leaving ${owned.length} Electron process(es) alone: they belong to the running pnpm dev (pid ${ownerPid})`
    )
  if (strays.length === 0) return
  console.warn(`[${label}] killing ${strays.length} stray Electron process(es) of this checkout:`)
  for (const { pid, command } of strays)
    console.warn(`[${label}]   ${pid} ${command.slice(0, 160)}`)
  appendExitRecord(devSandbox, {
    event: 'killed-strays',
    label,
    wrapperPid: process.pid,
    pids: strays.map(({ pid }) => pid)
  })
  for (const { pid } of strays) {
    try {
      process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM')
    } catch {
      /* already gone */
    }
  }
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))
  for (const { pid } of strays) {
    try {
      // probe — throws if dead, so we don't SIGKILL a recycled pid
      process.kill(pid, 0)
      process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL')
    } catch {
      /* gone */
    }
  }
}

// Allow `pnpm dev --onboarding` (or `BLUME_ONBOARDING=1 pnpm dev`) to force the
// first-run onboarding guide to show even when it was already completed. The
// flag is forwarded to the Electron main process via an env var.
const forceOnboarding =
  process.argv.slice(2).some((arg) => arg === '--onboarding' || arg === '--onboard') ||
  process.env.BLUME_ONBOARDING === '1'
if (forceOnboarding) {
  console.log('[pre-dev] onboarding guide forced on for this dev session')
}

function parseEnvLine(line) {
  const match = line.match(/^\s*(?:export\s+)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=\s*(.*)?\s*$/)
  if (!match) return null

  const key = match[1]
  let value = match[2] ?? ''
  value = value.trim()

  const quoted = value.match(/^(['"])([\s\S]*)\1(?:\s+#.*)?$/)
  if (quoted) {
    const quote = quoted[1]
    value = quoted[2]
    if (quote === '"') {
      value = value
        .replace(/\\n/g, '\n')
        .replace(/\\r/g, '\r')
        .replace(/\\t/g, '\t')
        .replace(/\\"/g, '"')
        .replace(/\\\\/g, '\\')
    }
  } else {
    value = value.replace(/\s+#.*$/, '').trimEnd()
  }

  return [key, value]
}

function loadEnvFiles() {
  const env = { ...process.env }
  const shellKeys = new Set(Object.keys(process.env))
  const files = []
  const loaded = []

  function addWorkspaceEnvFiles(root, label) {
    const entries = [
      ['.env', resolve(root, '.env')],
      ['.env.local', resolve(root, '.env.local')],
      ['.env.development', resolve(root, '.env.development')],
      ['.env.development.local', resolve(root, '.env.development.local')],
      ['apps/desktop/.env', resolve(root, 'apps', 'desktop', '.env')],
      ['apps/desktop/.env.local', resolve(root, 'apps', 'desktop', '.env.local')],
      ['apps/desktop/.env.development', resolve(root, 'apps', 'desktop', '.env.development')],
      [
        'apps/desktop/.env.development.local',
        resolve(root, 'apps', 'desktop', '.env.development.local')
      ]
    ]
    files.push(
      ...entries.map(([name, file]) => ({
        file,
        label: `${label}:${name}`
      }))
    )
  }

  if (primaryWorkspaceRoot !== workspaceRoot) {
    addWorkspaceEnvFiles(primaryWorkspaceRoot, 'primary-worktree')
  }

  addWorkspaceEnvFiles(workspaceRoot, 'current-worktree')

  for (const { file, label } of files) {
    if (!existsSync(file)) continue
    loaded.push(label)
    const text = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')
    for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
      const parsed = parseEnvLine(line)
      if (!parsed) continue
      const [key, value] = parsed
      if (shellKeys.has(key)) continue
      env[key] = value
    }
  }

  return { env, loaded }
}

    stdio: 'inherit',

  })

  'electron-vite',
  devRunnerArguments(launcherArgs.runnerMode, launcherArgs.electronViteArgs),
  {
    stdio: 'inherit',

      ...childEnvironment,
      ...(launcherArgs.runnerMode === 'static'
        ? { NODE_ENV: 'development', VITE_BLUME_STATIC_DEV: '1' }
        : {})
    }
  }

let finalizing = false
async function finalize(code, reason) {
  if (finalizing) return
  finalizing = true
  recordStop(reason)
  if (child.exitCode === null && !child.killed) {
    try {
      child.kill('SIGTERM')
    } catch {
      /* gone */
    }
    // Give electron-vite a beat to tear down its Electron child cleanly.
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 800))
  }
  await killStrays('post-dev')
  releaseWrapper(projectRoot, process.pid)
  process.exit(code)
}

markLaunched(projectRoot, process.pid)
child.on(
  'exit',
  (code, signal) => void finalize(code ?? 0, { childExit: code, childSignal: signal })
)

<file path="scripts/electron-vite-build.mjs">
import { spawn, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

const isWindows = process.platform === 'win32'
const command = isWindows ? (process.env.ComSpec ?? 'cmd.exe') : 'pnpm'
const args = isWindows
  ? ['/d', '/s', '/c', 'pnpm exec electron-vite build']
  : ['exec', 'electron-vite', 'build']
// The renderer bundle outgrows Node's default heap (about 2 GB); keep a caller's own limit.
const nodeOptions = process.env.NODE_OPTIONS ?? ''
const heap = /--max-old-space-size/.test(nodeOptions)
  ? nodeOptions
  : `${nodeOptions} --max-old-space-size=6144`.trim()
const child = spawn(command, args, {
  stdio: 'inherit',
  env: { ...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: heap, VITE_BLUME_STATIC_DEV: '0' }
})

child.once('error', (error) => {
  console.error(error)
  process.exitCode = 1
})
child.once('exit', (code, signal) => {
  if (signal) {
    process.kill(process.pid, signal)
    return
  }
  if (code !== 0) {
    process.exitCode = code ?? 1
    return
  }
  // Outside out/, which release steps rewrite (source-map debug IDs); the installer checks hashes.
  const bundlePath = fileURLToPath(new URL('../plugin-bundle-out', import.meta.url))
  const bundleArgs = ['--filter', '@blume/agent-mcp-node', 'plugin:bundle', '--out', bundlePath]
  const bundle = spawnSync(
    command,
    isWindows ? ['/d', '/s', '/c', 'pnpm', ...bundleArgs] : bundleArgs,
    {
      stdio: 'inherit'
    }
  )
  if (bundle.error) console.error(bundle.error)
  process.exitCode = bundle.status ?? 1
})

function badgeSvg(variant) {
  if (variant === 'stable') return ''
  // A soft ribbon across the bottom of the tile names the channel.
  const ribbonFill = variant === 'dev' ? '#c9b9ee' : '#f3c397'
  const ribbonText = variant === 'dev' ? '#51406e' : '#72471f'
  return [
    '<g clip-path="url(#dock-tile-clip)">',
    `<rect x="48" y="384" width="416" height="80" fill="${ribbonFill}"/>`,
    `<text x="256" y="442" fill="${ribbonText}" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, sans-serif" font-size="48" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle" letter-spacing="3">${variant === 'dev' ? 'DEV' : 'CANARY'}</text>`,
    '</g>'
  ].join('')
}

function dockIconSvg(flowerDataUrl, variant) {
  // Channel builds shrink the flower so it clears the bottom ribbon.
  const flowerSize = variant === 'stable' ? 312 : 244
  const flowerInset = (512 - flowerSize) / 2
  return [
    '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512">',
    '<defs>',
    '<linearGradient id="dock-tile-fill" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">',
    '<stop offset="0" stop-color="#fef8e7"/>',
    '<stop offset="1" stop-color="#f6efd6"/>',
    '</linearGradient>',
    '<clipPath id="dock-tile-clip"><rect x="48" y="48" width="416" height="416" rx="82"/></clipPath>',
    '</defs>',
    '<rect x="48.5" y="48.5" width="415" height="415" rx="81.5" fill="url(#dock-tile-fill)" stroke="#4b4a43" stroke-width="1"/>',
    badgeSvg(variant),
    `<image href="${flowerDataUrl}" x="${flowerInset}" y="${flowerInset}" width="${flowerSize}" height="${flowerSize}"/>`,
    '</svg>'
  ].join('')
}

async function generateDockIcons() {
  app.commandLine.appendSwitch('force-device-scale-factor', '1')
  await app.whenReady()

  const renderer = new BrowserWindow({
    show: true,
    x: -10_000,
    y: -10_000,
    width: 512,
    height: 512,
    frame: false,
    transparent: true,
    opacity: 0,
    focusable: false,
    skipTaskbar: true,
    webPreferences: {
      backgroundThrottling: false
    }
  })

  try {
    for (const variant of variants) {
      const outputDir = resolve(dockRoot, variant)
      mkdirSync(outputDir, { recursive: true })

      for (const [flower, assetPath] of Object.entries(flowerAssets)) {
        const source = nativeImage.createFromPath(assetPath)
        if (source.isEmpty()) throw new Error(`Flower source is empty: ${assetPath}`)

        const svg = dockIconSvg(source.toDataURL(), variant)
        await renderer.loadURL(`data:image/svg+xml;base64,${Buffer.from(svg).toString('base64')}`)
        await renderer.webContents.executeJavaScript(
          'Promise.all([document.fonts.ready, new Promise(requestAnimationFrame), new Promise(requestAnimationFrame)])'
        )
        const capture = await renderer.webContents.capturePage()
        if (capture.isEmpty()) throw new Error(`Rendered icon is empty: ${variant}/${flower}`)
        const icon = capture.resize({ width: 512, height: 512, quality: 'best' })
        const png = icon.toPNG({ scaleFactor: 1 })
        if (png.length === 0) throw new Error(`Encoded icon is empty: ${variant}/${flower}`)
        const outputs = [resolve(outputDir, `${flower}.png`)]
        // The window icon for dev and canary is the bluebell tile; stable keeps its packaged icon.
        if (flower === 'bluebell' && variant !== 'stable') outputs.push(resolve(windowIconRoot, `icon-${variant}.png`))
        for (const outputPath of outputs) {
          writeFileSync(outputPath, png)
          console.log(outputPath)
        }
      }
    }
  } finally {
    renderer.destroy()
    app.quit()
  }
}

void generateDockIcons().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error)
  app.exit(1)
})
